item.content:encoded:
Dodgers’ Dalton Rushing will have chance to make case for postseason roster spot
- Click here to listen to this article
-
The Dodgers plan to give catcher Dalton Rushing a chance to make his case for a spot on the postseason roster, after playing just four games in the last seven weeks because of a right elbow injury.
He’s set to be activated from the injured list before the end of the season, manager Dave Roberts said, and he’ll serve as a left-handed bat off the bench.
“Just showing them that I can swing it, and it’s an option,” Rushing told The Times after taking live batting practice Tuesday for the first time since landing on the IL earlier this month. “I know that you kind of tie [the team’s] hands up when you can’t play defense. So, I’m not expecting anything… just continue to take at-bats and see where we go from there.”
The slight tear in Rushing’s ulnar collateral ligament made headlines after he landed on the IL on Aug. 3. But Rushing’s MRI scans suggest the UCL — which is associated with Tommy John surgery — is not the issue.
The pain in his elbow seems to stem from a flexor strain. The small tear in his UCL has remained the same size since 2022, he said.
Rushing received platelet-rich plasma injection after aggravating the flexor injury a second time while working through a throwing program at the beginning of the month.
“I’m pretty confident I can still avoid surgery after the shot,” he said, noting that he’s been getting regular scans to monitor his healing. “Obviously, when I re-injured it the second time, I was almost 70-30, thinking that I was for sure going to need surgery. But after I got the shot and it ran its course, I feel as close to healthy in my arm as I have in a pretty long time.”
It was Josue De Paula’s bat that earned him a call-up when Shohei Ohtani landed on the IL. And it’s his bat that’s now making his case for a postseason roster spot.
This time, Rushing has abandoned the throwing program. But he said he doesn’t regret trying to return to the field the first time around.
“In my eyes, me trying to throw is me showing them that obviously I want to help the team win,” he said. “I want to give us the best available option that we have at that moment, and that was my whole plan all along. So I hope they see there wasn’t any selfishness in that.”
The Dodgers will need a left-handed bat off the bench in October, but Rushing now has competition.
Rookie Josue De Paula replaced Shohei Ohtani on the roster when the superstar landed on the 15-day IL two weeks ago. His first major-league hit was a three-run home run, and he entered Tuesday with a .974 OPS in 10 games.
Even if the Dodgers option De Paula on Wednesday when they reinstate Ohtani, 10 days before the NL Division Series, he will be eligible to be added to the NLDS roster via petition to the Commissioner’s Office.
For the past 17 years, Chaz Perea and his four-person crew have been responsible for every bit of stadium landscaping that isn’t the field itself.
“It’s going to be a good debate,” Roberts said. “Hitting off the bench is very difficult, and so you’re just trying to figure out who gives us the best chance. To be quite frank, it’s going to be tougher for Dalton given the time that he’s missed, and … you have three games to get back in the playoff form, which is tough to do. It’s not a knock on him. He’s been great for us. But it’s still tough given that also you’re talking about the consistency of at-bats recently from Josue. We have to have those conversations and make a decision.”
Rushing played a large role in the Dodgers’ regular season. In his second year in the majors, he was thrust into the primary role behind the plate for two months because of Will Smith’s lingering neck injury. Now, he might not see the field in the postseason.
“It sucks,” he said of the injury derailing him down the stretch. “I mean, that’s really the only thing I can say about it, it’s not what I wanted — by no means.”
Looking beyond the playoffs, Rushing plans to evaluate his routine, hoping to set himself up to be available for more of 2027.
“I don’t even want to talk about it right now because we still have obviously a bigger task at hand,” Rushing said. “But my main plan moving into playing every day in the future is, make sure that my body can hold whatever stress or whatever is needed for this team — first base, behind the plate, whatever they need. I want to make sure my body can handle it and do it for 162.”

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have just two series left on their MLB schedule before the playoffs begin next week.
Beginning on Tuesday, the Dodgers will play the San Diego Padres, and in the final weekend of the season, LA will take on the Giants.
However, speaking to Tuesday's game, the Dodgers announced a Kyle Tucker lineup decision before their game one with the Padres.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Announce Emmet Sheehan Demotion Before Padres Series
Kyle Tucker Back in Dodgers Batting Order Hitting 5th
After sitting out for Sunday's game against the Giants, Kyle Tucker is back in the batting order for the Dodgers.
Per @UnderdogMLB, here is the full group:
Dodgers 9/22: "M. Betts SS F. Freeman 1B W. Smith C M. Muncy 3B K. Tucker RF T. Hernández LF J. De Paula DH A. Pages CF T. Edman 2B B. Stewart SP"
Other lineup notes include Josue De Paula getting the nod at DH, Andy Pages being in the lineup after being activated, and Will Smith behind the plate for LA to catch Brock Stewart, who was suddenly announced as the SP for Tuesday's game.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Announce 4 Roster Moves Before Padres Game
Inside Kyle Tucker's Season with the Dodgers
Kyle Tucker is in the middle of his first season with the Dodgers.
It's been a very up-and-down campaign, but Tucker may be hitting a very important stride as October approaches.
He's still batting just .234, but Tucker has 17 home runs now, 70 RBI, and 121 hits over 516 at-bats. His OPS+ is 100, which is exactly league average.
CBSSport.com's RotoWire staff wrote (about Tucker):
"After missing Sunday's series finale against the Giants, Tucker will return to the starting nine for Tuesday's series opener with the Padres. The 29-year-old will bat fifth and man right field for the Dodgers."
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Los Angeles Dodgers Announce Kyle Tucker Decision Before Padres Game appeared first on HEAVY.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — It's the final week of the regular season and the Dodgers are sorting things out as they prepare for the postseason, which they hope will start on October 3 in the National League Division Series rather than September 29 in the wild card round.
Before Tuesday's game, Blake Snell pitched a bullpen session at Dodger Stadium as he works his way back from leaving last Wednesday's start with left groin discomfort. Manager Dave Roberts said Snell is in line to start on Saturday in San Francisco against the Giants, with Tarik Skubal — currently on the bereavement list — starting Friday night at Oracle Park.
Yoshinobu Yamamoto starts Wednesday and Tyler Glasnow Thursday against the Padres.
Also on Tuesday, reliever Will Klein pitched a simulated inning against Dalton Rushing in a battle of players on the injured list. Klein is on the 60-day injured list with elbow discomfort and not eligible to be activated until September 30 at the earliest, but it looks like he'll be in the stay-hot camp should the Dodgers have room to add him at some point later in the postseason, similar to in 2025 when Klein wasn't active until the World Series and he pitched five scoreless innings, including four innings in the marathon Game 3.
"With Will it's more get healthy, show that you're healthy, throw to some hitters," Roberts said. "He'll throw during the week off, then we'll kind of see if there's an opportunity later on in the postseason, sort of like last year."
Rushing is trying to work his way back from elbow discomfort suffered when practicing throwing. His role would be a left-handed bat off the bench, a role currently occupied by Josue De Paula, who has been the designated hitter with Shohei Ohtani out. But Ohtani is expected to be activated Wednesday barring an unforeseen setback.
That essentially sets up a battle between Rushing and De Paula for a postseason roster spot, though Roberts said the plan is to activate Rushing at some point this week to literally get back into the swing of things.
"Quality of at-bat, conducting an at-bat obviously, the ability to swing at strikes, take balls, get on base, get a hit. There's potential slug with both guys. I think it's a good debate," Roberts said. "Hitting off the bench is very difficult so we're trying to figure out who gives us the best chance.
"And to be quite frank, it's going to be tougher for Dalton given the time he's missed, and to think that you have [three] games to get back into playoff form, it's tough to do. It's not a knock on him, he's been great for us, but it's still tough, right, Given that we talk about having the consistency of at-bats recently from Josue. But we have to have those conversations and make a decision."
Activating both Ohtani and Rushing this week, when the Dodgers have 14 active position players, would require two corresponding moves to make room on the active roster. If De Paula doesn't get sent down — "I think Josue has done a fantastic job," Roberts said Tuesday — that might mean rough news for Alexes Call and Freeland, either this week or next.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Dodgers Lineup vs. Padres: Andy Pages, Roki Sasaki Are Back
item.dc:creator: Nelson Espinal
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are opening up for a blockbuster series, their last big test, against the San Diego Padres. Dodgers Lineup 1. Mookie Betts, SS 2. Freddie Freeman, 1B 3. Will Smith, C 4. Max Muncy, 3B 5. Kyle Tucker, RF 6. Teoscar Hernandez, LF 7. Josue De Paula, DH 8. Andy Pages, CF 9. Tommy Edman, 2B Andy Pages is back in the batting order after being activated from the injured list. He broke his hand after getting hit by a pitch, had surgery, and after a month on the shelf, he is back.
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are opening up for a blockbuster series, their last big test, against the San Diego Padres.
Dodgers Lineup
1. Mookie Betts, SS
2. Freddie Freeman, 1B
3. Will Smith, C
4. Max Muncy, 3B
5. Kyle Tucker, RF
6. Teoscar Hernandez, LF
7. Josue De Paula, DH
8. Andy Pages, CF
9. Tommy Edman, 2B
Andy Pages is back in the batting order after being activated from the injured list. He broke his hand after getting hit by a pitch, had surgery, and after a month on the shelf, he is back.
It may take some time for him to shake off the rust at the plate, but his defense should not skip a beat.
The Dodgers are facing righty Michael King, but many of the hottest bats are righties.
Mookie Betts, Will Smith, and Kyle Tucker are among the most dialed-in hitters, and they should drive most of the offense.
Ideally, Freddie Freeman gets going again, since he hasn’t looked right in a while.
Who’s pitching for the Dodgers
The Dodgers will have Brock Stewart as the opener, with Roki Sasaki getting the bulk of the work out of the bullpen.
On Tuesday, hours before the game, Sasaki was activated off the injured list after recovering from his blister.
Sasaki has been great since the All-Star break, posting a 3.05 ERA with 37 strikeouts and 15 walks.
His splitter and slider are fantastic, while the fastball has been the difference-maker, showing some renewed life.
The Japanese righty is set to enter the bullpen in a varied role, either stepping in for a struggling starter or pitching late in high-leverage spots.
Stewart, meanwhile, has been a bit lucky, with a 2.55 ERA and a 3.91 FIP.
FanGraphs’ pitching models have appreciated his stuff and command, and while he has pitched better lately, he is prone to giving up hard contact.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers Top Prospect Josue De Paula Explains Viral Encounter With Shohei Ohtani
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Sandoval; Unknown

"He caught me by surprise, I was giving everybody a
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers top prospect Jose De Paula was surprised to see Shohei Ohtani in the dugout during Friday's game against the San Francisco Giants.
His face made that clear.
De Paula said he didn't expect Ohtani to be in the dugout when he embraced his teammates after scoring a run for the Dodgers in the contest, leading to his viral reaction.
“I actually seen him earlier that day but I wasn’t expecting him to be at the game," De Paula said.
"He caught me by surprise, I was giving everybody a handshake, I gave him a handshake, but then I double take like he’s here.”
De Paula made his MLB debut on Sept. 11 after the Dodgers placed Ohtani on the injured list due to a variety of injuries he's been battling.
The 21-year-old is Ohtani's replacement in the lineup and serves as the Dodgers' designated hitter for now.
De Paula also mentioned that he is excited to see Ohtani back at the plate for the Dodgers.
“I can’t wait until he’s back. To see what he does in the box, you don’t see that every day so I can’t wait," he said.
In 28 at-bats as a Dodger, De Paula has recorded a .268 batting average with a .974 OPS, one home run, seven RBIs and one stolen base.
How Close Is Shohei Ohtani to Returning?
It hasn't been a pretty second half for Ohtani, as he battled with injuries for the better part of a month-plus.
Since the start of August, Ohtani's bat has gone ice cold.
From Aug. 1 until he was placed on the 15-day IL, Ohtani has a .231 batting average with 27 hits, six home runs, 13 RBIs and 19 runs.
While Ohtani's numbers are far below what is expected, the Dodgers hope that is a thing of the past.
Ohtani is eligible to return to the lineup Wednesday, and he's progressing well in his recovery. The 32-year-old took a major step this past weekend, as he was seen running the bases and hitting off the Trajekt machine.
Manager Dave Roberts said he hopes Ohtani will be ready to return Wednesday. If not, the four-time MVP could make his return Thursday.
Ohtani is in his third year with the Dodgers after signing a 10-year, $700 million contract in December 2023.
The two-way superstar has led the Dodgers to back-to-back World Series titles. While he isn't at 100% with the postseason nearing, he's expected to do his part to try to lead Los Angeles to yet another World Series title in 2026.
Sign up for our free newsletter and follow us on X/Twitter and Facebook for the latest news.
Ricardo Sandoval is a freelance writer with On SI. He is a graduate of California State University, Northridge, and specializes in sports writing, particularly in MLB, NBA and NFL. He previously served as an Associate Editor for Dodgers Nation and has worked with Newsweek and The Sporting News.

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers prospect Josue De Paula was named Texas League Player of the Year for the 2026 Minor League season. De Paula was among six members of the Drillers organization to receive honors.
Eric Wedge was named Texas League Manager of the Year, while De Paula, Mike Sirota, Zyhir Hope, Jake Gelof and Nick Robertson were all selected to the All-Star team as well. Of course, Hope’s time with the Drillers came to an end at the deadline as he was included in the trade package sent to the Detroit Tigers for Tarik Skubal.
Less than a week after the trade, Hope was named Texas League Player of the Month for July.
Josue De Paula’s Texas League award
De Paula is the fourth Drillers player to be named the Texas League’s MVP, joining Bubba Smith (1996), Ryan Shealy (2004) and Matt Beaty (2017).
The 21-year-old appeared in four games for Tulsa at the end of last season and spent all of this year with the Dodgers’ affiliate before getting called up to make his MLB debut. De Paula became the first Dodgers position player to get promoted directly from Double-A during president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman’s tenure.
While appearing in 124 games for the Drillers, De Paula batted .303/.401/.547 with 37 doubles, two triples, 27 home runs, 104 RBI and 31 stolen bases. He led all Texas League players in total hits (152), RBI and runs scored (106), and was tied for most doubles.
De Paula additionally set career highs in games played, doubles, home runs and RBI. He additionally was one stolen base shy of equaling his most in any Minor League season and three walks shy of tying a career-best mark.
With his RBI and runs scored totals, De Paula joined Carlos Pena as the only players in Drillers franchise history to have at least 100 in both categories in the same season.
De Paula’s impressive offensive success has carried over with the Dodgers, with remarkable plate discipline translating to quality and productive at-bats.
De Paula has garnered praise from Dodgers manager Dave Roberts and teammates alike, and seemingly played his way into the discussion for a potential postseason roster spot. De Paula also has already made Dodgers franchise history as their first player to ever wear No. 95.

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] The Dodgers’ Josue De Paula can hit. Now he’s out to prove he can play defense, too
item.dc:creator: Maddie Lee
item.description: - Click here to listen to this article - Dodgers rookie Josue De Paula sat down with third base and outfield coach Dino Ebel in the visiting coach’s room at Great American Ball Park. Ebel pulled up defensive metrics on three different outfielders. One was Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong, the National League MVP favorite and MLB’s defensive fWAR leader. Another was Dodgers center fielder Andy Pages, who has evolved into an elite center fielder during his time with the organization.
item.content:encoded:
- Click here to listen to this article
-
Dodgers rookie Josue De Paula sat down with third base and outfield coach Dino Ebel in the visiting coach’s room at Great American Ball Park. Ebel pulled up defensive metrics on three different outfielders.
One was Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong, the National League MVP favorite and MLB’s defensive fWAR leader. Another was Dodgers center fielder Andy Pages, who has evolved into an elite center fielder during his time with the organization. And the third was De Paula.
“There’s a lot of colors in the game, and when you have red, it’s not good, and when you have green, it’s good,” Ebel said in a recent conversation with The Times. “And he saw a lot of green from the other two players, and he saw some green and some red on his side. So it kind of hit home with him.”
The reports broke down his first step, going right and left, arm strength, and so on.
For the past 17 years, Chaz Perea and his four-person crew have been responsible for every bit of stadium landscaping that isn’t the field itself.
“Just comparing [Pages’] journey, too, with mine — and that it’s possible,” De Paula said of what he took from the conversation. “I have all the tools under my belt to be able to do so. It’s more about just being focused throughout the whole thing, and having that drive to want to do it.
“And when I saw it, it was also a motivation for me. It was like, all right, let’s go now.”
It was De Paula’s bat that earned him a call-up when Shohei Ohtani landed on the injured list. And it’s his bat that’s now making his case for a postseason roster spot. (“This is more of a trial run,” manager Dave Roberts said last week.)
For De Paula to stick in the majors, however, his development on the defensive side is going to be key. As he has risen through the system, his outfield play has lagged behind his offensive influence. But the Dodgers have already seen growth this year.
“Our goal is to become, one day, a Gold Glover,” Ebel said. “And I think he’s young enough to do it, and his mindset is right, he’s got a chance to do that.”
Dodgers special assistant Jason Heyward started poring over video of the team’s top prospects — a group chalk full of outfielders, led by De Paula — as soon as he began working for the Dodgers’ front office at the beginning of May.
“He handles constructive criticism, for me, with some of the best of them that I’ve been around,” Heyward said.
Heyward, a five-time Gold Glove outfielder, first met De Paula in spring training in 2024, when the prospect jumped in on outfield drills with the major leaguers. In Heyward’s new role, he’s made multiple trips to Tulsa, Okla., to work with De Paula and the rest of the group there.
Heyward emphasized building a consistent and productive routine.
“He makes it so easy to have something to make relatable to this because I’ve seen his work in the cage, I’ve seen his attention to detail,” Heyward said. “He takes on challenges, but it’s not a, ‘Let me hurry up and get to this challenge, let me rush through this.’ He’s like, ‘No, I’m going to go about this how I want to go about it, I’m not going to be rushed, I’m going to lock in, and I’m going to give this like all my focus.’”
That process on the offensive side was something Heyward encouraged De Paula to tap into in all parts of his game, including defense. But De Paula said Heyward also acknowledged that the nature of playing in the outfield can make that more difficult.
“Hitting, you are always unfocused on the next pitch, your mind is always going,” De Paula said. “But you could go three days without getting a fly ball. So it’s kind of easy for your mind to drift and stuff like that. But it’s just more about tips of engagement and that intensity of focus.”
Heyward was a fitting person to deliver the message. Once a heralded prospect for the Braves, he put together a 16-year MLB career that included a second-place rookie of the year finish, an All-Star nod, and a stellar reputation for defense and veteran leadership.
“It’s a blessing to have somebody like that in your corner, especially rooting for you, to be able to see your talent, like what you’re capable of,” De Paula said. “He’s been through it, so he knows, man. So it’s awesome to have somebody like that as your mentor.”
Coincidentally, De Paula would go on to launch a three-run home run as his first major-league hit, a feat he shares with Heyward — although Heyward did it in his first at-bat.
“It’s a very commendable job that all of our staff have done at every level,” Heyward said. “... I’d be doing a big injustice without giving everyone their flowers on this because it’s definitely been a group effort. … For someone like him who became a part of the organization at 16 years old, he’s a Dodger through and through.”
Over the past week and a half, the major-league coaching staff, which also had De Paula in major-league spring training camp the last two years, has taken over. And already, they’ve seen the benefit of the routine he’s developed this year.
“All the reports that we’ve gotten from our minor-league staff are right on cue,” Ebel said. “He’s been working, he’s bringing it right here to the major leagues. And it’s a pleasure for me, with some energy, coming out early every day — hasn’t missed. We’re working on game situations, ground balls, left, right, right at him, fly balls, shags during BP. So we’re on the right track.”
Dodgers two-time Cy Young winner Blake Snell joined them one day in Miami, catching De Paula’s throws in early work. Though the new teammates wanted to keep the specifics of their conversations between them, Snell’s advice and encouragement made an impression — “It’s like putting fuel in a rocket,” De Paula said.
“He’s just really, really talented, lots to learn,” Snell said. “And excited for him in his journey and what it could turn into.”
In the next city, Cincinnati, Roberts spent an afternoon in left field with him while he was shagging fly balls during batting practice.
“I wanted to be up close to watch him get off on the baseball, watch his reads, his angles to balls and make sure he’s shagging the right way,” Roberts said. “Had some instruction for him; he was great.”
Mookie Betts hits three doubles and the Dodgers piled up 15 hits in a 10-4 win over the San Francisco Giants with Shohei Ohtani’s return on the horizon.
Roberts, too, has challenged De Paula to make defense a strength, one that will keep him in games, rather than lifted for a defensive replacement. And De Paula has met it with bright eyes and motivation.
“The trust on the defense is going to come,” De Paula said. “I have to prove it over time. And with the work that I’m doing on the field, I know I’m going to gain it.”
A gold glove is a goal of his too.
“That’s one thing about me, when my mind is set on something, I feel like it’s no going back,” De Paula said. “So, I’ve gotten a lot of hate on my defense, and I just love to prove people wrong. So I’m like, hey, all right, there’s a weakness there, but I’m gonna shut you up. Just give me some time. I’ve got you.”

item.title: [whittierdailynews.com] Are the Dodgers finding the best version of themselves just in time?

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — The energy emanating from the steamroller heading up I-5 on Monday radiated for miles.
Fuel was used to power the buses the San Diego Padres used to make the trip north for a three-game series that starts Tuesday night, but only because they didn’t try adrenaline.
Winners in 13 of their past 14 games, the Padres are poised to accomplish team history over the next few days. Never in their existence have they made the playoffs in three consecutive seasons.
San Diego has a magic number of two to clinch a National League wild-card spot, although the Padres intend to run through the finish line with a chance at ascending to the top of the wild-card heap in the NL.
“I feel like the whole team is in a good spot right now,” San Diego’s Fernando Tatis Jr. told the San Diego Union-Tribune on Sunday. “We’re playing really good baseball. We’re checking in when we have to. The entire lineup is in a good spot right now. So when it’s going like that, it’s … a good time.”
The Dodgers already have another NL West title secured (their 13th in the past 14 years), but they also have a magic number of three to clinch a top-two seed in the NL playoffs and a bye into one of the best-of-five Division Series.
“I think it’s going to be a good kind of (playoff) primer,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of the upcoming series. “They’re a very talented team. They’re playing as good as anyone in all of baseball. I’m looking forward to playing those guys and just kind of ramping it up a little bit more for our guys.”
With the Dodgers on a 14-3 run since Sept. 3, they are on a familiar final month charge toward the playoffs. Second-half lulls in each of the past two seasons have transformed into Septembers when the group has discovered the best version of itself.
Last season, the Dodgers were swept in a three-game series by the Angels in August then opened September with a three-game dud in Pittsburgh. A disastrous loss in Baltimore lit the fire after Yoshinobu Yamamoto lost a no-hitter with two outs in the ninth inning and the Dodgers never recorded another out while losing the game.
The wide-awake Dodgers went 15-5 the rest of the way, stormed through the NL playoffs – going 9-1 against the Cincinnati Reds, Philadelphia Phillies and Milwaukee Brewers – then came out on top in a dramatic seven-game World Series against the Toronto Blue Jays.
Earlier this month, it was a brutal 8-6 loss in 10 innings to the St. Louis Cardinals on Sept. 2 that was the wake-up call. It included a four-strikeout night from Shohei Ohtani, who played just one more game before taking his current spot on the injured list.
Properly motivated, the Dodgers have gone on a tear ever since, but it has come at the expense of teams that were not in playoff contention like the Washington Nationals, Reds, Miami Marlins and San Francisco Giants.
This week marks the Dodgers’ first chance to face a team playing at the peak of its powers since they faced the Boston Red Sox, Chicago Cubs, Milwaukee Brewers and Atlanta Braves all in a recent 25-game stretch. They flubbed that test by going 1-12 in those games.
Mookie Betts, Kyle Tucker and Will Smith all have put a charge into the resurgence, while the arrival of rookie Josue De Paula has given the lineup another hitter who can extend at-bats with a discerning eye, along with Max Muncy.
Betts went 0 for 4 in Sunday’s 3-1 victory over the Giants, yet he still is hitting .373 with six home runs, 20 RBIs and a 1.215 OPS in 17 games since the start of September.
Far from content with an offense that has averaged 5.8 runs per game this month, Betts said the Dodgers can do even more. After all, Andy Pages is set to return Tuesday, while Ohtani could be back later this week.
“Some guys are hitting, some guys are not,” Betts said. “I think that’s the beauty of the lineup. You get a couple guys going, and a couple guys here can carry a team, and you never know. You just never know who’s it going to be, it’s different guys every day.”
Amid a brutal first season with the Dodgers, Tucker has done his part lately by going 15 for 36 (.417) over his past 11 games with five home runs and 11 RBIs. He was limited to coming off the bench on Sunday after he fouled a ball off his right knee on Saturday.
Tucker was not with the club for last year’s September revival, but he has helped power this one. When it comes to team potential, Tucker is a big-picture guy.
“I think our potential is winning the World Series,” Tucker said. “So (when) we do that, then I can say we reached it. But we feel like we’re in a good spot right now. Our pitching staff’s done a great job all year giving us an opportunity to win every single night. Our defense has played pretty well behind them and then offensively we’ve done a solid job as well.”
“Right now, we got a few guys that are feeling good. A few guys that are banged up. But we’re still out there grinding trying to win as many games as possible before the season ends and just trying to carry it all the way to the playoffs.”
At the very least, confidence will be high this week, in both dugouts.
UP NEXT
Padres (RHP Michael King, 12-9, 3.03 ERA) at Dodgers (TBA), Tuesday, 7:10 p.m., SportsNet LA, 570 AM

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] MLB Injury Report: Dodgers to get Shohei Ohtani, Andy Pages, and Roki Sasaki back for postseason run
item.dc:creator: Jorge Montanez
item.description: In this week's Injury Report, the Dodgers are getting a number of key players back this week as they prepare for another deep playoff run in their quest to three-peat. Alex Bregman hopes to return sometime in the postseason after suffering multiple facial fractures in a terrible, freak accident on the on-deck circle. And Dylan Cease has likely made his last start after experiencing shoulder fatigue. That and more in the final week's injury report. ⚾️ Baseball is back! MLB returns to NBC and Peac
item.content:encoded:
In this week's Injury Report, the Dodgers are getting a number of key players back this week as they prepare for another deep playoff run in their quest to three-peat. Alex Bregman hopes to return sometime in the postseason after suffering multiple facial fractures in a terrible, freak accident on the on-deck circle. And Dylan Cease has likely made his last start after experiencing shoulder fatigue. That and more in the final week's injury report.
⚾️ Baseball is back! MLB returns to NBC and Peacock in 2026! In addition to becoming the exclusive home of Sunday Night Baseball, NBC Sports will broadcast MLB Sunday Leadoff, "Opening Day" and Labor Day primetime games, the first round of the MLB Draft, the entire Wild Card round of the postseason, and much more.
Shohei Ohtani (knee, biceps)
Andy Pages (hand)
Blake Snell (groin)
Roki Sasaki (blister)
Ohtani has been out of action for the last two weeks, sidelined with lingering knee and biceps injuries. Manager Dave Roberts told reporters on Sunday that the 32-year-old star should be expected to return from the injured list and join the Dodgers lineup on Wednesday. Ohtani should be in the lineup for the remaining games to get some needed at-bats before the postseason. The team also gets Pages back this week, activating him from the injured list ahead of Tuesday's series opener against the Padres. He's been out for a month with a left hand fracture. The two additions this week are obviously a significant boost for a Dodgers team looking to three-peat. Their returns likely shift rookie Josue De Paula to a reserve or utility role.
On the pitching side, Snell left his start last Wednesday against the Reds with left groin tightness. He stated the issue was not serious and plans on making one more start before the postseason. That start isn't going to come when his spot in the rotation comes up on Tuesday, but the plan is for him to pitch over the weekend, according to Roberts.
From Yordan Alvarez to Zack Wheeler, an A-to-Z look at the players, performances, and trends that defined the 2026 MLB regular season.
Alex Bregman (face)
Bregman was struck by a foul ball while on the on-deck circle on Sunday against the Reds and was sent to the hospital, where he was diagnosed with multiple facial fractures. The freak accident is an unfortunate development this late in the season as the Cubs prepare to enter the playoffs. The team is hoping to get their 32-year-old star third baseman back at some point in the postseason, and it is a relief that the injury didn't result in anything more serious. Meanwhile, Sasaki was activated on Monday after missing some time with a blister issue and will pitch as a one-inning reliever, auditioning for a spot in the Dodgers bullpen in the postseason.
Dylan Cease (shoulder)
Cease has likely made his final start of the season. The 30-year-old right-hander underwent an MRI on his right shoulder over the weekend after experiencing some fatigue. The imaging revealed some shoulder inflammation, but no structural damage that would require surgery, and nothing that would bring into question his availability for next season. With the Blue Jays 3.5 games out of a Wild Card spot, it doesn't make much sense for Cease to push for one more start over the final weekend. If his season is indeed over, he'll end the year with a strong 2.40 ERA, 1.10 WHIP, and 239 strikeouts over 169 innings.
Andrés Muñoz (knee)
Muñoz left Sunday's game against the Rockies with a knee injury after giving up a home run and a walk. He was set to undergo an MRI on his right knee, the results of which are still unknown. The 27-year-old right-hander had a tough, disappointing season, posting a 4.24 ERA, 1.22 WHIP, and 89 strikeouts over 57 1/3 innings while converting 28 of 38 save chances. If he's unable to pitch over the final week, it could be Seranthony Domíguez closing out the remaining games.
Bryce Eldridge (concussion)
More Giants injuries that seemingly come out of nowhere. Eldridge was scratched from Friday's lineup against the Dodgers due to a head laceration after bumping his head on a low-hanging ceiling at the team hotel. He still "felt woozy" throughout the weekend and entered the concussion protocol before the team ultimately placed him on the 7-day concussion injured list. The move is retroactive to Friday, so there's a chance he could return for the final weekend series, though that's probably unlikely. The 21-year-old slugger flashed immense potential this season, hitting .269/.364/.461 with 17 homers and 57 RBI across 448 plate appearances.
Colt Keith (thumb)
Keith's season is over after the team placed him on the 10-day injured list with a left thumb sprain. It's an issue that the 25-year-old infielder has been playing through over the last several weeks. He ends the season hitting a modest .258/.322/.406 with 10 homers, 51 runs scored, 36 RBI, and six steals across 423 plate appearances.

item.content:encoded:
El prospecto dominicano Josué De Paula, el prospecto principal de los Dodgers, se ha convertido en una pieza clave para el equipo de Grandes Ligas durante la recta final de la temporada en la última semana y media. Sin embargo, esto sucedió tras una campaña magnífica en el equipo de Doble-A de Tulsa; el lunes fue nombrado Jugador Más Valioso (MVP) de la Texas League.
Josue De Paula got called up from Double-A to the big leagues at 21 years.
Here are his stats after 10 MLB games and 38 PA.👇
.286 AVG
.474 OBP
.500 SLG
.974 OPS
4 XBH
10 BB
4 K
🔥 pic.twitter.com/DKg7saFAyL
Jugando para los Drillers, De Paula registró una línea ofensiva de .303/.401/.547, con un wRC+ de 145, 27 jonrones, 37 dobles, 106 carreras anotadas, 104 carreras impulsadas y 31 bases robadas en 124 partidos. Estableció marcas personales en todos los rubros, incluyendo más del doble de sus registros anteriores en jonrones (su máximo previo era de 12) y extrabases (66, frente a los 30 anteriores).
Lideró la liga en carreras anotadas, carreras impulsadas, hits y dobles; además, se ubicó entre los cinco mejores de la liga en OPS, porcentaje de slugging, porcentaje de embasado (OBP), promedio de bateo, jonrones, bases robadas, bases totales (274) y extrabases.
También el lunes, Baseball America nombró a De Paula como el Jugador del Año de las ligas menores de los Dodgers.
De Paula no ha dejado de rendir desde su ascenso a las Grandes Ligas; se ha embasado 18 veces en 38 visitas al plato —con 10 bases por bolas que más que duplican sus cuatro ponches— y registra una línea ofensiva de .286/.474/.500, con tres dobles y un jonrón en sus primeros 10 partidos en las mayores.
Los Dodgers contaban con una gran cantidad de prospectos en los jardines este año; de hecho, todos los jardineros seleccionados para el Juego de Estrellas de la Texas League pertenecían a los Tulsa Drillers: Zyhir Hope —traspasado el 2 de agosto a los Detroit Tigers en la operación por Tarik Skubal— y Mike Sirota acompañaron a De Paula. Otros jugadores de Tulsa seleccionados para el Juego de Estrellas fueron el jugador de cuadro Jake Gelof (como bateador designado) y el relevista Nick Robertson.
Eric Wedge fue nombrado Mánager del Año de la Texas League, convirtiéndose en el quinto dirigente de los Tulsa Drillers en obtener este galardón y el primero desde Tim Ireland en 2002, cuando Tulsa era filial de los Texas Rangers. Este reconocimiento llega 19 años después de que Wedge ganara el premio al Mánager del Año de la Liga Americana con Cleveland en 2007.
Hasta ahora, un jugador de ligas menores de los Dodgers ha ganado el premio al Jugador Más Valioso (MVP) en los tres niveles de temporada completa: De Paula se une al jardinero Charles Davalan (Great Lakes, Clase A Avanzada/Midwest League) y al primera base Ontario Easton Shelton (Clase A/California League). Cuando se anuncien los premios de Triple-A, James Tibbs III tendrá buenas posibilidades de ganar el MVP de la Pacific Coast League.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers playoff roster projection: Could Edwin Díaz, Josue De Paula, even Hyeseong Kim surprise?
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris

They are a seemingly safe four games clear of the Atlanta Braves for a first-round bye. And, unless they can close a two-game gap on the Milwaukee Brewers without holding the tiebreaker, they will finish as the NL's No. 2 seed, getting home-field advantage at least for the NL Division Series. item.content:encoded:
Entering the final week of the regular season, the Dodgers more or less know their postseason fate.
They've locked up the National League West. They are a seemingly safe four games clear of the Atlanta Braves for a first-round bye. And, unless they can close a two-game gap on the Milwaukee Brewers without holding the tiebreaker, they will finish as the NL's No. 2 seed, getting home-field advantage at least for the NL Division Series.
Thus, the real intrigue for now is who might be on the Dodgers' postseason roster when the playoffs begin next month.
This year, injuries and fluctuating performances have forced them to cycle 53 different players through their clubhouse.
And while the core of the group is clear, many questions remain about how the club will construct its lineup and pitching staff for this fall's pursuit of a third-straight World Series.
Here is the California Post's best guess about how it will all shake out.
Lineup locks
Will Smith, Freddie Freeman, Tommy Edman, Mookie Betts, Max Muncy, Teoscar Hernández, Andy Pages, Kyle Tucker, Shohei Ohtani, Kiké Hernández, Miguel Rojas, Hunter Feduccia
There won't be any big surprises in how the Dodgers line up to begin the playoffs, assuming Ohtani is healthy enough to resume everyday DH'ing duties.
Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker have cemented their place as everyday hitters thanks to late-season surges. Andy Pages is due back on Tuesday from a fractured hand. Freddie Freeman still seems somewhat limited by his right knee injury, but has nonetheless been able to manage it well enough to this point. And while Tommy Edman has been slumping lately, he doesn't seem to be in immediate danger of losing at-bats.
On the bench, Hunter Feduccia has locked up the back-up catching job, and could be a left-handed hitting option as a pinch-hitter. Kiké Hernández and Miguel Rojas, meanwhile, each provide versatile defensive depth, as well as extensive track records for postseason heroics when called upon.
Entering the final week of the regular season, the core of the Dodgers' position player group looks as they expected.
Dodgers Lineup questions
Bubble candidates: Josue De Paula, Dalton Rushing, Alex Call, Alex Freeland, Hyeseong Kim
The Dodgers will still have one, if not two, position player spots to fill depending on how they construct their roster (i.e. an even 13 pitchers/13 hitters, or a 12/14 split like they used last year?)
And for those, they could have a number of difficult decisions.
First and foremost: Will Josue De Paula make the playoff roster?
If he does, it will likely be as a left-handed bench bat; though if there is any lingering uncertainty with Ohtani, he could also provide insurance as a backup DH option. His main competition right now figures to be Alex Call (who might be redundant to Rojas and Hernández as a right-handed bench bat) or Dalton Rushing (who is an intriguing alternative as a left-handed bat, but remains sidelined from the setback he suffered with his elbow injury earlier this month).
In just 10 MLB games, De Paula has quickly built a strong case, showing supreme plate discipline (10 walks to only four strikeouts) and the potential for power (three doubles, one home run, seven RBIs). At this point, it might be more of a surprise if he doesn't make it.
If the Dodgers elect to carry an extra position player on top of that, the choices are even more varied.
Last year, they rostered two base-running/defensive specialists throughout the playoffs in infielder Hyeseong Kim and outfielder Justin Dean. Dean is now gone, and Hernández could serve as a late-game defensive outfield replacement anyway. But Kim remains in consideration, manager Dave Roberts said, thanks to his speed and infield glove. Alex Freeland could also factor in here, as someone capable of providing more at the plate.
Lineup projection for Los Angeles
C: Will Smith
1B: Freddie Freeman
2B: Tommy Edman
SS: Mookie Betts
3B: Max Muncy
LF: Teoscar Hernández
CF: Andy Pages
RF: Kyle Tucker
DH: Shohei Ohtani
Bench: Kiké Hernández, Miguel Rojas, Hunter Feduccia, Josue De Paula, Hyeseong Kim*
*If the Dodgers carry 14 position players
Dodgers pitching staff locks
Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow, Roki Sasaki, Tanner Scott, Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips
The Dodgers' starting rotation is set, assuming no further setbacks with Blake Snell's groin injury. The back end of the bullpen has come into focus, too, with Tanner Scott and/or Roki Sasaki the most logical candidates to serve as closer, and Alex Vesia and Evan Phillips separating themselves as the team's next most-trusted high-leverage relief options.
The only real question here is how the Dodgers will line up the rotation. Yamamoto-Skubal would make sense for Games 1 and 2 of a division series (keeping them both on-line for a potential Game 5). But could Tyler Glasnow's potential issues with traveling tempt the Dodgers to use him primarily at home, if they can? All factors to consider in the coming weeks.
Pitching staff questions
Roster bubble candidates: Brock Stewart, Edwin Díaz, Blake Treinen, Kris Bubic, Jack Dreyer, Emmet Sheehan, Justin Wrobleski, Edgardo Henriquez, Will Klein, Eric Lauer
The first thing the Dodgers need to figure out here is health.
Edgardo Henriquez will almost certainly be on the playoff roster, and pitching in a high-leverage role, if he can make a full recovery from his recent back strain. Will Klein and Eric Lauer might also be available health-wise, though lack clear roles to step immediately back into.
Otherwise, the Dodgers will effectively have at least four open spots for six to seven other pitchers.
For added right-handed depth, they might be deciding between Brock Stewart (who has been a go-to weapon against right-handed hitters recently), Edwin Díaz (who is trying to salvage his dismal debut season, and did throw a pair of scoreless outings this weekend) and Blake Treinen (who has curiously pitched only five times in three weeks since being activated from the injured list, and not in the highest of leverage).
For another left-handed option, they could go with Kris Bubic (the trade deadline acquisition who has impressed with three scoreless appearances since returning from an injury) or Jack Dreyer (who was one of the Dodgers' best relievers from June to August, but has given up five runs in his last seven outings).
And for a multi-inning role, they will have Emmet Sheehan (who has looked like a different pitcher in three sterling starts since returning from a minor-league demotion) and Justin Wrobleski (the breakout All-Star who has finally shaken some of his home run problems since moving to the bullpen).
There are many permutations that the Dodgers could employ depending on opponent. They're still figuring out the exact hierarchy of all their bullpen arms, too.
But as long as their rotation is dominant, everything else should take care of itself.
Pitching staff projection
Rotation: Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow
Bullpen: Roki Sasaki, Tanner Scott, Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips, Brock Stewart, Kris Bubic, Edwin Díaz, Emmet Sheehan, Justin Wrobleski

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers have lineup problem they cannot afford to solve by benching Josue De Paula
item.dc:creator: Miracle Dimwesh
item.description: Josue De Paula was supposed to give the Los Angeles Dodgers another young bat for the final weeks of the regular season. Instead, the rookie has created a lineup problem the team may not be able to ignore. De Paula has been too productive to simply remove from the lineup. The 21-year-old has reached base at a .474 clip through his first 10 MLB games, giving the Dodgers another dangerous left-handed hitter before the postseason. That creates an interesting problem when Shohei Ohtani returns. The
item.content:encoded:
Josue De Paula was supposed to give the Los Angeles Dodgers another young bat for the final weeks of the regular season. Instead, the rookie has created a lineup problem the team may not be able to ignore.
De Paula has been too productive to simply remove from the lineup. The 21-year-old has reached base at a .474 clip through his first 10 MLB games, giving the Dodgers another dangerous left-handed hitter before the postseason.
That creates an interesting problem when Shohei Ohtani returns. The Dodgers have several established outfielders, but De Paula's bat is making it harder to find room for everyone.
Josue De Paula has been doing this all year
The rookie's hot start is not coming out of nowhere. De Paula dominated Double-A pitching throughout the season before earning his September call-up.
Minor League Baseball named him the 2026 Texas League MVP on Monday. He hit .303/.401/.547 with 27 home runs, 31 stolen bases, 152 hits and 104 RBIs in 124 games for Tulsa.
That production earned him a direct jump from Double-A to Los Angeles. He has continued showing the same offensive approach against MLB pitching.
De Paula has gone 8-for-28 with 10 walks, one home run and seven RBIs in his first 10 games. He has also played two games in left field, showing the Dodgers can move him around when necessary.
Dodgers face a difficult Ohtani lineup decision
Feb 24, 2026; Phoenix, Arizona, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Josue De Paula against the Cleveland Guardians during a spring training game at Camelback Ranch-Glendale. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
The situation becomes more complicated with Ohtani nearing a return. Manager Dave Roberts said there is a good chance Ohtani will be activated Wednesday against the San Diego Padres. He will return as a hitter, not a pitcher.
That puts Ohtani back at DH and removes the easiest path to keeping De Paula in the lineup.
The Dodgers already have Kyle Tucker in right field, Teoscar Hernández in left and Andy Pages in center. Tucker signed a four-year, $240 million deal before the season, while Hernández and Pages have remained important parts of the club's outfield plans.
De Paula can play the outfield, but moving him there would force another decision. Taking one of the established outfielders out also means changing a group that has helped Los Angeles reach this point.
The Dodgers do not have to solve the entire problem today. But De Paula's performance has made one thing clear: when Ohtani returns, finding enough at-bats for everyone will be one of Dave Roberts' biggest lineup challenges heading into October.

item.title: [True Blue LA] Josue De Paula wins Texas League MVP
item.dc:creator: Eric Stephen
item.description: Dodgers top prospect Josue De Paula has become major league stretch-run contributor over the last week and a half. But that followed a wonderful season in Double-A Tulsa, and on Monday he was named Texas League MVP. De Paula with the Drillers hit .303/.401/.547 with a 145 wRC+, 27 home runs, 37 doubles, 106 runs scored, 104 RBI, and 31 stolen bases in 124 games. He set career highs across the board, including more than doubling his previous marks for home runs (previous high of 12) and extra-bas
item.content:encoded:
Dodgers top prospect Josue De Paula has become major league stretch-run contributor over the last week and a half. But that followed a wonderful season in Double-A Tulsa, and on Monday he was named Texas League MVP.
De Paula with the Drillers hit .303/.401/.547 with a 145 wRC+, 27 home runs, 37 doubles, 106 runs scored, 104 RBI, and 31 stolen bases in 124 games. He set career highs across the board, including more than doubling his previous marks for home runs (previous high of 12) and extra-base hits (66, up from 30).
He led the league in runs scored, RBI, hits, doubles, and was in top five in the league in OPS, slugging percentage, on-base percentage, batting average, home runs, stolen bases, total bases (274), and extra-base hits.
De Paula hasn’t stopped producing since getting his first call-up to the majors, reaching base 18 times in 38 trips to the plate with his 10 walks more than doubling his four strikeouts, hitting .286/.474/.500 with three doubles and a home run in his first 10 games in the majors.
The Dodgers were loaded with outfield prospects this year, and the entire Texas League All-Star outfield were Tulsa Drillers, with Zyhir Hope — traded on August 2 to the Detroit Tigers in the Tarik Skubal deal — and Mike Sirota joining De Paula. Other Tulsa All-Stars were infielder Jake Gelof at designated hitter plus relief pitcher Nick Robertson.
Eric Wedge was named Texas League manager of the year, the fifth Tulsa Drillers manager to capture the award, and the first since Tim Ireland in 2002 when Tulsa was a Texas Rangers affiliate. This honor comes 19 years after Wedge won American League manager of the year with Cleveland in 2007.
So far a Dodgers minor leaguer has won Most Valuable Player at all three full-season levels, with De Paula joining High-A Great Lakes outfielder Charles Davalan in the Midwest League and Class-A first baseman Ontario Easton Shelton in the California League. Whenever the Triple-A awards are announced, James Tibbs III has a good shot at winning Pacific Coast League MVP.

item.content:encoded:
メジャー屈指の有望株にとっても、大谷翔平は同じチームにいることが信じられないほどの存在であるようだ。
現地時間18日、ロサンゼルス・ドジャースは本拠地ドジャー・スタジアムでサンフランシスコ・ジャイアンツと対戦した。大谷の負傷者リスト（IL）入りに伴って現地11日に2Aタルサから昇格したホスエ・デパウラは、3打数2安打2得点の活躍を見せ、8-2での快勝に大きく貢献した。
この試合、デパウラの2度目のホームインはムーキー・ベッツのホームランによるものだった。生還後、ベッツに続いてダグアウト前でチームメイトたちとハイタッチを交わした際の一幕が、現在SNSで大きな話題を呼んでいる。
見事な『二度見』動画がSNSで話題に
デパウラは祝福の列にいた大谷に気づかずさりげなくハイタッチを交わすが、その直後驚いた表情で振り返り見事な『二度見』を披露した。この場面の動画がSNSに投稿されると、「可愛すぎる」「彼も私たちファンと同じ反応だね」といった声が相次ぎ、瞬く間に拡散された。
デパウラ本人が当時の心境を明かす
Josue De Paula breaks down his viral moment with Shohei Ohtani on Friday where he did a double take when he saw him in the Dodgers dugout 😂
“I actually seen him earlier that day but I wasn’t expecting him to be at the game. He caught me by surprise, I was giving everybody a… pic.twitter.com/YN5PMqMhTe
ドジャース専門メディア『Dodgers Nation』のノエル・サンチェス記者は、デパウラ本人を直撃し当時の心境を尋ねた。すると彼は思わず笑顔を見せ、「実はその日、すでに彼（大谷）を見かけてはいたんだけど、まさか試合（のベンチ）に来ているとは思っていなかったんだ」と告白。「みんなとハイタッチをしていて、彼とも手を合わせた直後に『えっ、いるじゃん！』って気づいて、思わず二度見してしまったよ。結構驚いたね」と率直な思いを明かした。
また、大谷のチームメイトとしてプレーすることについて問われると、「最高だよ。彼が復帰するのが待ちきれない。彼のバッティングや活躍は、誰もが毎日見られるようなものじゃないからね。本当に楽しみだよ」と答えた。
現在、デパウラはメジャー昇格後の10試合で打率.286、OPS.974と躍動している。大谷の復帰を心待ちにしつつ、ドジャースが誇る21歳の最有望株のさらなる活躍にも注目していきたい。

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Josue De Paula's Early Success Might Be Bad News For This Dodgers Veteran
item.dc:creator: Aaliyan Mohammed
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers called Josue De Paula up from Double-A earlier this month, and he has been making headlines with his bat early on. It was the first time under Andrew Friedman that the Dodgers called a position player up directly from Double-A. De Paula's defense is not great, but Shohei Ohtani being injured has allowed him to serve as the designated hitter. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers called Josue De Paula up from Double-A earlier this month, and he has been making headlines with his bat early on.
It was the first time under Andrew Friedman that the Dodgers called a position player up directly from Double-A. De Paula's defense is not great, but Shohei Ohtani being injured has allowed him to serve as the designated hitter.
In 10 games, he is slashing .286/.474/.500 with half of his hits going for extra bases. His bat and eye at the plate have been as advertised. He is the Dodgers' top prospect and the No. 6 prospect in baseball. He won't be eligible for the postseason since he was not on the 40-man roster by Sept. 1, but his future for the Dodgers looks bright,
He is bound to slump at some point, but his early success means even if he is in Triple-A to start the season next year, it won't be long for him to be back with the big league club. However, Ohtani will be back, and De Paula will need a spot in the outfield. Unfortunately for Teoscar Hernández, he is the most likely to lose his job to De Paula.
Hernández has one year left on his contract, and his OPS has taken a big dive after his All-Star season in 2024. De Paula has shined with the bat and is working hard to improve his defense. If he can do that, he should take Hernández's spot.
What would that mean for Hernández? Well, it's not really the Dodgers' style to trade away their own stars, but De Paula needs to play. Hernández is about to be 34, and he still has trade value. He is not a great defender, so if De Paula is going to replace one of the Dodgers' starting outfielders, it's going to be the one who also isn't great defensively and is old. Kyle Tucker and Andy Pages are not going anywhere.
It's unclear what the Dodgers will do with De Paula next year. They've seen that his bat is ready for the big leagues, but may still want him to get some Triple-A work before making him an every day player in the big leagues. Eventually, he will start to slump in the Majors, like every young hitter, and will have to make adjustments. Regardless, his early success is a threat to Hernández's future with the team.

item.dc:creator: Aaliyan Mohammed

The Dodgers even have Jason Heyward, who they hired as a special assistant in the spring, helping him improve defen
item.content:encoded:
For the first time under Andrew Friedman, the Dodgers called up a position player directly from Double-A in Josue De Paula.
His bat has been stellar, and even though he is the Dodgers' top prospect and the No. 6 prospect in baseball, defense has been a huge knock on him. He has a 40-grade fielding tool, the lowest of any position player in the top 10 on MLB Pipeline's Top 100 list. The Dodgers even have Jason Heyward, who they hired as a special assistant in the spring, helping him improve defensively.
De Paula knows his defense needs to be better if he wants to make a real impact in the big leagues, and he's not running from it.
"I know that's a big area of improvement for me," De Paula told The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya. "I know I got a lot of hate on it. I'm that type: if I get hate on it, I'm going to focus on it more. So I'm gonna shut a lot of people up with my defense very soon. It's gonna take some time."
So far, De Paula has just one start in the outfield as a big leaguer. However, that's because Shohei Ohtani is currently on the injured list, and the Dodgers have the luxury of playing him in the designated hitter spot. Whether the Dodgers decide to send him back to play in Triple-A or not at some point, he will not be able to serve as a designated hitter permanently.
That spot belongs to Ohtani, so De Paula's path to playing daily is in the outfield. So far, his bat is good enough, and he has great poise at the plate. However, it may actually benefit the Dodgers to have him start next season in Triple-A to iron out his defense.
More MLB: Paul Skenes Reveals Whether World Baseball Classic Is To Blame For Down Year

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers top prospect Josue De Paula recently made his MLB debut with LA.
He’s had a few very solid moments at the plate, and he’s showcased his impressive plate discipline with an ability to put the ball in play and drive it to the opposite side of the field.
De Paula is still very young, so there’s plenty of time to develop in the coming years, but it’s been a welcome sign thus far in his first handful of MLB action.
Recently, Josue De Paula shared an honest message about dealing with critics to Dodgers reporter Fabian Ardaya.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Get Major Andy Pages Update Ahead of Padres Series
Josue De Paula Shares Honest Message
Per Ardaya, here is what Josue De Paula had to say about critics calling out his defense:
“I know that’s a big area of improvement for me,” said De Paula. “I know I got a lot of hate on it. I’m that type: if I get hate on it, I’m going to focus on it more. So I’m gonna shut a lot of people up with my defense very soon. It’s gonna take some time.”
Even manager Dave Roberts said that De Paula still has a lot of development to do in the outfield, but it’s been clear De Paula’s defense isn’t the reason he’s in the show.
Ardaya notes that De Paula could have a full-time role with the Dodgers if he shores up his defensive ability:
“The list of helpful voices kept growing over the first 10 days of De Paula’s big-league career. His bat could be special, but De Paula’s path to impacting the 2027 Dodgers becomes a lot easier if he proves he can handle the corner outfield. Mookie Betts, a six-time Gold Glove winner in right field, gave him pointers on how to shag fly balls. Manager Dave Roberts, who spent 10 years patrolling big-league outfields, goes out of his way to ensure De Paula emphasizes the details.”
With all the stars on the Dodgers roster, De Paula’s development is in good hands.
More MLB on Heavy: New York Mets Trade Pitch Offloads Mark Vientos to Pirates
Josue De Paula’s Rookie Campaign Thus Far
Josue De Paula has played in just 10 games for LA, and across his first 38 MLB plate appearances, he’s batted .286 with 10 walks, eight hits, six runs, one home run, and 3 doubles.
Those are very solid numbers to start your MLB career, and especially as a top prospect.
Here is some of De Paula’s prospect bio, per MiLB.com:
“De Paula draws comparisons to a slightly smaller but more athletic version of Yordan Alvarez, thanks to his precocious combination of swing decisions and exit velocities. He offered at just 14 percent of pitches outside the strike zone last season — by comparison, Juan Soto led the Majors with a 16 percent rate — and is supremely comfortable working deep counts in order to find pitches he can punish.”
Yordan Alvarez? The frontrunner for 2026 AL MVP? Not a bad comparison. The future looks bright for Josue De Paula thus far.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Announce 4 Sudden Roster Moves During Giants Series

item.title: [Dodger Blue] Josue De Paula responds to criticism about defense with bold prediction
item.dc:creator: Blake Williams
item.description: Josue De Paula has been everything the Los Angeles Dodgers could have hoped for in the batter’s box during since getting called up for his MLB debut. Since being added onto the Dodgers roster to replace Shohei Ohtani as the everyday designated hitter, De Paula has shown off his patience, ability to take a quality at-bat, and power and speed combination. The sky is the limit for De Paula’s offensive capabilities, and that’s what carried him to the MLB level. But his defense in the outfield is a m
item.content:encoded:
Josue De Paula has been everything the Los Angeles Dodgers could have hoped for in the batter’s box during since getting called up for his MLB debut.
Since being added onto the Dodgers roster to replace Shohei Ohtani as the everyday designated hitter, De Paula has shown off his patience, ability to take a quality at-bat, and power and speed combination. The sky is the limit for De Paula’s offensive capabilities, and that’s what carried him to the MLB level.
But his defense in the outfield is a major area of concern, and it’s part of the reason the Dodgers did not call De Paula up until needing a regular DH. As they look ahead to the postseason, De Paula is likely to be limited to being a bat off the bench, given his defensive struggles and the uptick of production from Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker.
However, De Paula knows he needs to improve in the outfield, and he’s made it a focus during his first stint at the MLB level.
“Every day. I know that’s a big area of improvement for me, and I know I’ve got a lot of hate on it,” De Paula said. “I’m the type that if I get hate on it, I’m going to focus on it more. I’m going to shut a lot of people up with my defense very soon.”
De Paula has spent time before every game practicing his defense, working with Dodgers coaches to become more of a usable option in the outfield. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts has taken notice of that, and issued a challenge to De Paula.
“Well, it’s clear he needs to improve on his defense,” Roberts said. “How do you shut people up? You perform better. You practice hard, and that’s how you do it. My challenge to him is to be a complete baseball player, and not just to be a hitter. So he’s putting a lot of good work with Dino every day, and so I welcome that.”
Josue De Paula praises Dodgers teammates
De Paula became the first position player promoted from Double-A by Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman, creating lofty expectations for himself.
The 21-year-old has felt prepared to meet the challenge of playing in the Majors head-on and credits his Dodgers teammates for creating an environment conducive to letting him play freely.
“Probably the biggest is takeaway is it’s basically the same game, just around different people,” De Paula said on SportsNet LA. “But one thing I didn’t expect was this team to be so cool. Like, all the players, the way they accepted me, the way they greeted me, making me feel comfortable. It put me in a better position to be me.”

item.title: [Dodgers Way] How Dodgers can fit Josue De Paula onto playoff roster for Corey Seager-like debut
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ranaudo
item.description: With Shohei Ohtani landing on the injured list with knee and biceps issues, the Dodgers called Josue De Paula straight up from Double-A Tulsa to the major leagues. The move meant he was skipping Triple-A entirely, making him the first position player prospect promoted directly from Double-A under Andrew Friedman's tenure and the first Dodgers hitter to skip Triple-A since Yasiel Puig. The numbers that got him to the big leagues are absurd. De Paula hit .303 with 27 home runs, 104 RBI, and 29 sto
item.content:encoded:
With Shohei Ohtani landing on the injured list with knee and biceps issues, the Dodgers called Josue De Paula straight up from Double-A Tulsa to the major leagues.
The move meant he was skipping Triple-A entirely, making him the first position player prospect promoted directly from Double-A under Andrew Friedman's tenure and the first Dodgers hitter to skip Triple-A since Yasiel Puig.
The numbers that got him to the big leagues are absurd. De Paula hit .303 with 27 home runs, 104 RBI, and 29 stolen bases at Double-A this season, an .966 OPS, and MLB had him as the No. 6 overall prospect in the game before the promotion.
An advanced hit tool forcing a September call-up before anyone expected it is exactly what makes a Corey Seager comparison worth investigating. Seager got the call in September 2015, made his debut with a two-hit, two-RBI performance, and then hit .337 with four homers and 17 RBI over his final 27 games of the season. That was enough for the Dodgers to name him the starting shortstop job over veteran Jimmy Rollins heading into October.
Seager and the Dodgers didn't make much noise that year, losing to the New York Mets in the NLDS, but it signaled to the team and fanbase they were willing to give the keys to the kid. Seager wound up leading the Dodgers to the 2017 World Series, and again in 2020, finally winning it all. He was World Series MVP and the NLCS MVP the series before, so LA can only hope this move for De Paula follows somewhat similarly.
Where Josue De Paula fits on the Dodgers' playoff roster
So where does De Paula actually fit for October? With Ohtani out, the DH spot is wide open, and De Paula is expected to see the bulk of his early opportunities there, with some reps in the corner outfield mixed in. Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic mentioned, of his first 37 MLB pitches he has seen that were outside the zone, De Paula has only swung at five, and didn't strike out until his 17th big league at-bat.
If he keeps hitting anywhere close to the way he has in his minor league career and glimpses in these first few games, there's a path to him being a useful bat off the bench or a semi-regular DH option on the postseason roster. That combo would be adding thump, energy and speed the Dodgers don't currently have without sacrificing anything on defense, since he'd be playing a spot that doesn't ask much of his glove yet.
None of that matters unless the Dodgers can legally get him on a postseason roster, and that's going to be a bit of a hurdle. Since De Paula wasn't on the 40-man as of September 1, per MLB's rules regarding postseason roster requirements, the Dodgers need to petition the Commissioner's Office, which requires him to have been in the organization by August 31 and to be replacing an injured player who's already served his minimum IL time.
De Paula clears the first requirement, but the second gets a little trickier. Andy Pages, is one of the options for De Paula to replace, but is also inching closer toward a return around the end of September and likely will be reclaiming his everyday outfield job, not sitting out for procedural reasons.
Dalton Rushing is the more interesting case, since he's already been ruled out from catching this season, and if the front office likes what it's seen from De Paula, shifting Rushing to the 60-day IL cleanly, locks in his unavailability. It opens the exact spot the Dodgers would petition around. In that case, Pages plays center and De Paula takes the roster spot Rushing leaves behind.
It's a real procedural step, not a guarantee, and it depends on the front office actually preferring De Paula's over Rushing. It also assumes the Dodgers have no other injuries before then, which is always a roll of the dice. But if the front office wants De Paula's bat and energy in October, this is the door they'll need to walk through.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants, 3-1, on Sunday and improved to 96-60 on the year. They completed the series sweep of the divisional rivals and notched their fourth-straight win (and 14th of the last 17).
After Jack Dreyer took the start and allowed an earned run in the first inning, Emmet Sheehan pitched the next 5.1 frames and stole the show on the mound. He struck out nine, allowed one hit, one walk and no earned runs.
Offensively, Teoscar Hernndez, Freddie Freeman, Max Muncy and Josue De Paula each had a two-hit game. De Paula was 5-for-10 over the course of the series, just the first of hopefully many more at Dodger Stadium.
Ahead of the eventual victory, southpaw Tarik Skubal unfortunately had to be placed on the bereavement list. As he deals with his personal matter, it is likely that he will still make one more start (he is next scheduled for Sept. 26) before the postseason.
In other news, manager Dave Roberts made a somewhat surprising admission regarding superstar Mookie Betts. After hitting just .235 before the All-Star break, Betts has completely turned things around and looks like a more familiar version of himself, hitting .322 in his last 30 games.
"I couldn't tell you that I saw this," Roberts said on Saturday regarding Betts' turnaround. "But I just felt that he was stronger. He's worked hard on that. He looks great. He's not going to stop working, and just for it to come together has been great."
Finally, a Dodgers pitcher was demoted as part of the four-player roster move made on Sunday. The right-hander has an impressive 1.32 ERA across 26 games (27.1 innings) at the Triple-A level, but in 11 appearances with the Dodgers this season, he has an 8.10 ERA across 10 innings of work.

item.title: [sbsun.com] Emmet Sheehan strengthens postseason case as Dodgers sweep Giants
item.dc:creator: Bill Plunkett
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Hiding behind that 5.00 ERA Emmet Sheehan toted around for much of the season might have been a valuable postseason piece. Sheehan allowed just one hit in 5⅓ scoreless innings on Sunday afternoon as the Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants, 3-1, to complete a three-game sweep. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Hiding behind that 5.00 ERA Emmet Sheehan toted around for much of the season might have been a valuable postseason piece.
Sheehan allowed just one hit in 5⅓ scoreless innings on Sunday afternoon as the Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants, 3-1, to complete a three-game sweep.
Sheehan retired 16 of the 18 batters he faced, allowing just one single and walking one while striking out nine.
“I’ve loved the version we’ve seen of Emmet the last three outings,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. “He’s been fantastic.
“We’ve seen confidence. We’ve seen when you’re essentially fighting for your life to create an opportunity for yourself. That’s what I see. There’s urgency. I like the way that he’s trusting his stuff. He’s in a good spot physically, and you know the performance has been fantastic.”
The outing was Sheehan’s third consecutive outstanding performance this month as he has bounced between Triple-A and the majors. It cemented a spot in the Dodgers’ postseason bullpen after a rough season for the 26-year-old right-hander – an outcome that did not seem likely when he was demoted to Triple-A in early August.
“I don’t know that I proved anything to myself. It was just getting a couple things right and I think I’m in a much better spot now,” Sheehan said.
“My confidence stayed the same the whole time. I knew the coaches down there were going to help me and I was going to get right. I took that approach going into it. I wasn’t helping the team here so I needed that a little bit.”
Sheehan has been called up for two starts this month and pitched in ‘bulk’ following Jack Dreyer as an opener on Sunday. Sheehan carried a 5.29 ERA into September after 20 starts for the Dodgers that landed him back in the minors.
In his three September outings, though, Sheehan has shown rediscovered fastball command after working on his delivery in Triple-A. He has allowed just one run in 17 innings, holding hitters to a .105 average (6 for 57) with 24 strikeouts and three walks. After giving up 20 home runs in those first 20 starts, he has allowed just one in his 17 September innings.
If his confidence didn’t need repair, his delivery and pitch mix needed some work.
Now two years removed from Tommy John surgery, Sheehan was thrown by not quite having recovered all of his fastball velocity this year. When he chased those extra miles per hour, it was counterproductive. He has become more comfortable at 94-95 mph now.
“I think it’s a few things,” he said Sunday. “Definitely … being more comfortable in my delivery, being out there staying free and easy with everything, not trying to do too much. Instead of saying, ‘I need 97 here.’ It’s more like ‘If I hit my spot, he’s not going to hit it.’”
They haven’t. Sheehan has gotten 50 swings-and-misses in his three outings this month, nearly half of them (24) on his reborn four-seam fastball. He also got six on his curveball on Sunday.
“That’s something that (assistant pitching coach) Connor (McGuinness), (pitching coach) Mark (Prior) and I and the coaches down in Triple-A have been working on is just expanding the front-to-back game with the fastball and the curveball,” Sheehan said. “I think some guys ended up throughout the season sitting mid-speed, slider-changeup, on me. Having that change of speeds the last couple has been very important.”
The Dodgers moved Sheehan to the bullpen for the postseason last October and saw him as a big weapon in that role. The results were mixed, however, in part because of some pitch tipping issues which Sheehan said have been addressed. He will be wiser this time around, he said.
“Definitely,” Sheehan said. “I think the routine of everything can be a little bit hard to adjust to right away. So having that experience helps a lot. Just getting back into that, I know what I need to do to get ready to go into the game.”
The Dodgers gave him a little bit of a test drive by using Dreyer as an ‘opener’ before him. The Giants scratched out one run in the first inning against Dreyer when he walked leadoff man Jonah Cox. Cox moved to second base on a wild pickoff attempt by Dreyer, stole third and scored on Victor Bericoto’s RBI single. The Giants had just one more hit in the game.
“I think that obviously there’s a 97 that plays better, but 94-95 commanded still misses bats,” Roberts said of Sheehan, who will rejoin Oklahoma City for the Triple-A playoffs this week before returning to the Dodgers for the postseason. “That’s one part of it. The other part of it is holding the velocity. And so, for me, the last three or four since he’s been back here, he’s held those 94s and 95s for the, call it 85 pitches.”
The Giants’ run against Dreyer stood up as the only run of the day until Tommy Edman emerged from a 2-for-41 slump to hit a solo home run in the sixth inning.
The Dodgers broke the 1-1 tie in the seventh on singles by Max Muncy and Josue De Paula followed by an RBI double from Kiké Hernandez.
They stranded De Paula and Hernandez in scoring position, but singles by Teoscar Hernandez, Freddie Freeman and Muncy produced another run in the eighth inning.
Kris Bubic, Brock Stewart and Tanner Scott combined on 2⅔ innings of hitless relief to close out the combined two-hitter for the Dodgers’ 96th win. With the win, the Dodgers’ magic number to clinch a first-round bye over the Atlanta Braves (who clinched the National League East division title on Sunday) dropped to three with six games left in the regular season.
The Dodgers (96-60) remain two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers (98-58) for the top seed, though the Brewers also hold the head-to-head tiebreaker. The No. 3 seed – currently Atlanta (92-64) – will play host to a best-of-three Wild Card Series against either the Chicago Cubs (87-69), San Diego Padres (87-69) or Philadelphia Phillies (86-70).

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Josue De Paula Breaks Down Viral Clip With Shohei Ohtani
item.dc:creator: Aaron Coloma
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers top prospect Josue De Paula went viral Friday after doing a double take following a high five with Shohei Ohtani. De Paula, who came up to replace Ohtani upon the MVP’s move to the injured list, had a huge game from the No. 9 spot on Friday, going 2-for-3 with two runs and an RBI. His second run of the game came off of a Mookie Betts homer, and he followed the All-Star through the dugout giving high fives to his teammates. Upon reaching Ohtani in the line, De Paula casually g
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers top prospect Josue De Paula went viral Friday after doing a double take following a high five with Shohei Ohtani.
De Paula, who came up to replace Ohtani upon the MVP’s move to the injured list, had a huge game from the No. 9 spot on Friday, going 2-for-3 with two runs and an RBI. His second run of the game came off of a Mookie Betts homer, and he followed the All-Star through the dugout giving high fives to his teammates.
Upon reaching Ohtani in the line, De Paula casually gave him a high five before doing a double take with a surprised look on his face.
“I actually seen him earlier that day but I wasn’t expecting him to be at the game,” De Paula said to Dodgers Nation’s Noel Sanchez. “He caught me by surprise, I was giving everybody a handshake, I gave him a handshake, but then I double take like he’s here.
“I can’t wait until he’s back. To see what he does in the box, you don’t see that every day so I can’t wait.”
De Paula is just 21 years old, and is already making quite the impact with the Dodgers. Through nine games with the team so far, De Paula has a .929 OPS with one homer and seven RBIs. His underlying numbers look great across the board, as he strikes out at an extremely low clip while maintaining fantastic quality of contact in his small MLB sample size.
When Will Shohei Ohtani Be Back?
Ohtani hasn’t played since Sept. 7, as he is nursing a biceps issue. He is slowly returning to baseball activities, and began running the bases prior to Saturday’s game against the San Francisco Giants.
Following Saturday’s game, manager Dave Roberts revealed he could return against the San Diego Padres in the Dodgers’ next series, which begins on Tuesday. His return would be huge for the Dodgers just before the postseason, and while he may not be able to pitch in October, he will play a huge role at the top of the Dodgers’ lineup as they aim to win their third World Series in a row.
