item.content:encoded:
Emmet Sheehan dominates Giants in long relief as Dodgers cap sweep
(Photo credit: William Liang)
Emmet Sheehan pitched brilliantly in long relief, Enrique Hernandez broke a seventh-inning tie with a run-scoring double and the Los Angeles Dodgers completed a three-game home sweep of the rival San Francisco Giants with a 3-1 victory Sunday afternoon.
Tommy Edman homered for Los Angeles (96-60), which won its fourth straight and remained four games ahead of the Atlanta Braves (92-64) in the race for the National League's No. 2 seed and a first-round bye in the playoffs.
After Victor Bericoto had singled home Jonah Cox in the first inning against Dodgers opener Jack Dreyer, Sheehan took over to start the second and held the Giants to just one hit over the next 5 1/3 scoreless innings. Nine of the 16 outs he recorded came via strikeout.
Meanwhile, Edman's homer, his seventh of the season, produced a 1-1 tie in the sixth. It came off Giants reliever Carson Seymour, who had replaced Matt Wilkinson after five shutout innings.
Making his fifth career start, Wilkinson limited the Dodgers to three hits while striking out six.
The clubs took the 1-1 tie into the bottom of the seventh, when one-out singles by Max Muncy and Josue De Paula off Sam Hentges (1-7) set the stage for Hernandez, whose double to center field drove in the go-ahead run.
Muncy provided an insurance run with an RBI single in the eighth that scored Teoscar Hernandez, who had singled.
Kris Bubic (4-2), Brock Stewart and Tanner Scott threw the final 2 2/3 innings for the Dodgers, allowing just two baserunners, one on an error and the other via a walk.
Scott walked Brett Harris with two outs in the ninth, bringing the potential tying run to the plate. But the left-hander locked down his 23rd save by striking out Osleivis Basabe.
Muncy, De Paula, Teoscar Hernandez and Freddie Freeman had two hits apiece for the Dodgers, who will host the second-place San Diego Padres for three games before closing the regular season with three in San Francisco beginning Friday.
Jung Hoo Lee joined Bericoto with the only hits for the Giants (64-92), who completed their road schedule with a 28-53 record.
--Field Level Media

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Tarik Skubal goes on bereavement list, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts says he'll miss 'a couple days'
item.dc:creator: Ian Casselberry
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers placed pitcher Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list on Sunday, which means he could miss his final regular-season turn in the rotation next week. Skubal's next start is scheduled for Friday against the San Francisco Giants, which could fall within the three-to-seven days that players are allowed to be away from the team while on the bereavement list. But Dodgers manager Dave Roberts appeared to believe that Skubal will be back by Friday, telling reporters he would miss "a
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers placed pitcher Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list on Sunday, which means he could miss his final regular-season turn in the rotation next week.
Skubal's next start is scheduled for Friday against the San Francisco Giants, which could fall within the three-to-seven days that players are allowed to be away from the team while on the bereavement list. But Dodgers manager Dave Roberts appeared to believe that Skubal will be back by Friday, telling reporters he would miss "a couple days."
"Some personal stuff going on, but he's fine," Roberts said, via MLB.com's Sonja Chen.
Skubal pitched in Saturday's 10-4 win over the Giants, allowing four runs and eight hits over five innings. He walked two batters with three strikeouts, tying his lowest total of the season. Saturday's game was the first time Skubal gave up more than three runs in his nine starts with the Dodgers. according to The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya.
Tarik Skubal pitched five innings and allowed four runs but is grateful for the offensive support.
“Yeah, no doubt. Obviously, I wasn't very good today, but the offense and defense and bullpen picked me up big time, and that's what good teams do,” Skubal said. “You know, they… pic.twitter.com/4TUdrQqgH8
"Obviously, I wasn't very good today, but the offense and defense and bullpen picked me up big time, and that's what good teams do," Skubal said after the game.
In his nine starts with the Dodgers since being acquired from the Detroit Tigers before the MLB trade deadline, Skubal has a 2.95 ERA and 4-2 record with 60 strikeouts in 55 innings.
The Dodgers took a 2-0 lead on a first-inning RBI double by Max Muncy and Mookie Betts hitting a run-scoring single in the second. But San Francisco tied the score in the third on a 2-run homer from Victor Bericoto, hitting a fastball left in the very middle of the strike zone by Skubal.
The two teams then traded runs during the third through fifth innings, resulting in a 4-4 tie, before the Dodgers pulled away on a 2-run hit by Tommy Edman and RBI single from Miguel Rojas. In the following inning, the Dodgers added three more runs with Will Smith driving in a run and Josue De Paula hitting a 2-run single.
To fill Skubal's spot on the active roster, Emmet Sheehan was recalled from Triple-A Oklahoma City. He pitched 5 1/3 scoreless innings with one hit allowed and nine strikeouts, taking over for opener Jack Dreyer in the Dodgers' 3-1 win. In his previous two starts before being optioned, Sheehan allowed one run over 11 2/3 innings with 15 strikeouts.

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Is it still a rivalry? Dodgers complete sweep of woeful Giants
item.dc:creator: Kevin Baxter
item.description: Is it still a rivalry? Dodgers complete sweep of woeful Giants - Click here to listen to this article - Only the Pirates and Cubs have met more often than the Dodgers and Giants, who faced off for the first time in 1889. The Dodgers and Giants have also won more pennants, made more World Series appearances and have more players wearing their caps in the Hall of Fame than any other National
item.content:encoded:
Is it still a rivalry? Dodgers complete sweep of woeful Giants
- Click here to listen to this article
-
Only the Pirates and Cubs have met more often than the Dodgers and Giants, who faced off for the first time in 1889. And over all that time, the Dodgers are just two games better, with 1,294 wins to the Giants’ 1,292.
The Dodgers and Giants have also won more pennants, made more World Series appearances and have more players wearing their caps in the Hall of Fame than any other National League teams, all of which fueled a rivalry that was once among the most visceral and passionate in American sports.
But that was then and this is now.
After Sunday’s 3-1 victory over the Giants, the Dodgers’ 14th win in their last 17 games, the team could finish a season with 100 wins for the fourth time in six years. The Giants have had just one winning record in that time.
The Dodgers (96-60), who have won five straight division titles, are headed to the postseason for a record-tying 14th consecutive year. The Giants will miss the playoffs for a fifth straight season.
So is the rivalry dead? That depends on who you ask.
“It’s always a rivalry,” Giants pitcher Logan Webb. “We’d like to make it a little closer when it comes to the standings. But I definitely feel it when I throw against them.”
But then Webb, who is from Northern California, grew up with the rivalry and, as the longest-tenured Giant, pitched against the Dodgers in games that mattered. Giants coach Ron Washington, who made his major league debut with the Dodgers when the rivalry was still a thing, said many players on San Francisco’s roster don’t know that background.
Mookie Betts hits three doubles and the Dodgers piled up 15 hits in a 10-4 win over the San Francisco Giants with Shohei Ohtani’s return on the horizon.
“It should be a rivalry. But I don’t think the young kids we got know anything about a rivalry. They’re not history buffs.”
Webb said it’s the responsibility of the veterans on both sides to keep that history alive by explaining the enmity to the young players.
“I think there are still guys that came up in the system that know what it’s like,” he said. “It’s my job to kind of hype these guys up to play a game like this.”
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts, who played for the Dodgers and Giants during his 10-year career, agrees the rivalry now exists more in the history books than the current standings, where the Giants have been overtaken by the San Diego Padres, who will finish second to the Dodgers in the N.L. West for the fourth time in five seasons.
“It’s certainly a rivalry in the sense of the history, the fan bases,” Roberts said. “But obviously it’s about relevancy. The Padres have been successful the last handful of years, and so it’s certainly built some momentum. The geography lends itself to that too.
“But Dodgers Giants is always fun.”
It hasn’t been so much fun for the Giants lately. San Francisco hasn’t won the season series with the Dodgers since 2021 and has lost more than 90 games this year for the first time in nine seasons.
On Sunday they went in front three batters into the game with Johan Cox working Dodger opener Jack Dreyer for a leadoff walk, then making his way around the bases on Dreyer’s throwing error, a stolen base and a one-one single by Victor Bericoto.
But San Francisco didn’t get another hit until Jung Hoo Lee singled with one out in the sixth.
That allowed the Dodgers to tie the score in the sixth on Tommy Edman’s seventh home run of the season just inside the right-field foul pole. An inning later they went ahead to stay when Max Muncy singled under a sliding Cox at second, moved to third on a single by rookie Josue De Paula and scored on Kiké Hernández’s double to center.
A two-out single by Muncy, his second of the game, scored Teoscar Hernández, who also had two hits, in the eighth inning with the final run.
Even the slumping Freddie Freeman contributed to the Dodgers’ 11-hit attack, ending an 0-for-11 slide with a broken-bat single in the fourth then singling again in the eighth.
Sunday’s result helped clarify the Dodgers’ once-muddy playoff picture. With six games left in the regular season, the Dodgers lead Atlanta by four games in the race for the second seed in the National League playoffs, which would give them a first-round bye and the homefield advantage in the division series.
The team’s postseason roster may be getting clearer as well. Right-hander Emmet Sheehan, who made 22 starts this season, came out of the bullpen for the first time Sunday and was brilliant in his audition for the playoffs.
“If there is a role in the postseason, it will be out of the [bull]pen,” Roberts said of Sheehan, who gave up just a hit and walk, striking out nine — one off his season high — in 5 1/3 innings.
Tyler Glasnow hasn’t had the greatest of seasons, but the Dodgers will need him to deliver in the playoffs if they want to win another World Series title.
De Paula, meanwhile, who also doubled in running his modest hitting streak to four games, appears to have secured a job as the team’s left-handed bat off the bench while utility player Hyeseong Kim, who has spent the last four months in the minors, will rejoin the Dodgers after the triple-A playoffs and be considered for a roster spot as a pinch-runner and late-inning defensive replacement.
“My expectation is that Hyeseong will be here during the off week and potentially be a conversation for the postseason because he has the ability to run, play defense, and steal a base,” Roberts said.
After Monday’s off day, the final break of the regular season for the Dodgers, the team is expected to activate Andy Pages, Roki Sasaki and Shohei Ohtani from the injured list during its three-game series with the Padres.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Emmet Sheehan Brilliant in Sweep-Securing Win Over Giants
item.dc:creator: Aaron Coloma
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers took a 3-1 win in their series finale against the San Francisco Giants on Sunday, finishing a three-game sweep. The Dodgers had a scheduled bullpen day on Sunday, but Emmet Sheehan handled most of the pitching. He had arguably his best outing of the season, completely shutting down the Giants over the course of his 5.1-inning performance. He only allowed one hit and one walk, keeping the Giants from scoring while striking out nine batters on the afternoon. The right-hande
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers took a 3-1 win in their series finale against the San Francisco Giants on Sunday, finishing a three-game sweep.
The Dodgers had a scheduled bullpen day on Sunday, but Emmet Sheehan handled most of the pitching. He had arguably his best outing of the season, completely shutting down the Giants over the course of his 5.1-inning performance.
He only allowed one hit and one walk, keeping the Giants from scoring while striking out nine batters on the afternoon.
The right-hander is putting together a serious case to make the postseason roster, allowing just one earned run over his last 17 innings pitched while striking out 24 batters.
Sheehan entered the game trailing, though, as Jack Dreyer allowed a run in the opening inning of the game. Jonah Cox took full advantage of a walk, advancing to second base on a throwing error before stealing third base. He came around to score on a Victor Bericoto single.
The Dodgers scattered baserunners over the course of the next several innings, and finally made a breakthrough in the sixth inning.
Tommy Edman took full advantage of an inside cutter, hitting his seventh homer of the season to tie the game.
The Dodgers scored yet again in the seventh inning, as both Max Muncy and Josue De Paula singled to put two on with just one out.
Kiké Hernandez stepped up to the plate, doubling into the gap in right-center field to bring home Muncy and give the Dodgers the lead.
They scored yet again in the eighth inning, as Teoscar Heranndez and Freddie Freeman both singled to bring Muncy to the plate. He came through yet again for the Dodgers, adding some insurance heading into the ninth inning.
Tanner Scott came in for the ninth inning, and got out without allowing a run despite a walk early in the frame.
The Dodgers get an off day Monday before heading into a three-game series against the San Diego Padres, which begins Tuesday at 7:10 p.m. PT.

item.title: [presstelegram.com] Dodgers’ Dave Roberts trying to find ‘balance’ as Freddie Freeman struggles to rediscover his swing
item.dc:creator: Bill Plunkett
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Dave Roberts has a dilemma. His first baseman, Freddie Freeman, just turned 37 years old and has been slumping badly down the stretch while playing through patellar tendinitis in his right knee. Never one to accept days off as the answer to anything, Freeman would probably benefit from some downtime this week – but he also needs at-bats to rediscover the swing that had him batting .300 for the season just two weeks ago or recalibrate it to accommodate his balky knee. “There’s rest,
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Dave Roberts has a dilemma.
His first baseman, Freddie Freeman, just turned 37 years old and has been slumping badly down the stretch while playing through patellar tendinitis in his right knee. Never one to accept days off as the answer to anything, Freeman would probably benefit from some downtime this week – but he also needs at-bats to rediscover the swing that had him batting .300 for the season just two weeks ago or recalibrate it to accommodate his balky knee.
“There’s rest, but there’s also trying to find your swing,” Roberts acknowledged after putting Freeman in the lineup on Saturday and Sunday – a day game following a night game.
“I think it’s a work in progress,” Roberts said of Freeman’s swing. “The other day in Cincinnati (a three-hit game on Tuesday), I think it was looking pretty good, and then. I actually thought yesterday there were a couple good swings there.
“Obviously, the results weren’t there for him, and he’s frustrated, and I think that you just kind of have to count on him to figure it out and bet on him. And that’s kind of where we’re at. But again, having the week off (with a first-round bye) would be huge too.”
Freeman said he has been doing some different drills in the batting cage, focused on hitting the ball “out front” more.
“I feel like my faults are I try to hit the ball to the opposite field too much, and I let the ball get too deep, and it caused me to slide,” Freeman said earlier this week. “So today (in the cage) was – foot down early, catch the ball out front a little bit.”
Even with that three-hit game in Cincinnati and a two-hit game on Thursday, Freeman went into Sunday just 6 for his past 48 (.125), hitless in nine at-bats in the first two games of the series with the Giants.
“Got to go for results-based things right now,” Freeman said. “Looking to be hot for a few weeks. That’s all I’m trying to do.
“I’m just trying to find something that gives me results. We’re at the time where we’re just trying to get hot for five weeks here. So kind of like I did in the World Series a couple years ago (when his ankle was injured), I did the step-out move. That’s not sustainable over six months. I’m not trying to find something that’s sustainable. I’m trying to find something that works for four weeks.”
OHTANI WORK
The “hope” is that Shohei Ohtani will be ready to come off the injured list when he is eligible on Wednesday, Roberts said. When he does, Roberts expects him to be in the lineup for the final five games.
“Absolutely,” Roberts said. “Yeah, he’ll need those live at-bats.”
Roberts has said Ohtani is “pain-free” but he acknowledged that Ohtani won’t be feeling 100% when he returns – but will be closer to it than he has been in weeks.
“Discomfort you can play through,” Roberts said of how Ohtani is feeling. “I think there’s a difference between discomfort and pain. Is it 100%? Probably not. Is it better than it was a week ago? Yes.
“Honestly I think that’s just a better question for Shohei to give more specifics, but I do think that when he’s activated it’s going to be the best physical place he’s been in in quite some time.”
Ohtani has spoken with the media just once in the past five weeks (before he went on the IL).
KIM CALL
Signed to a three-year, $12.5 million contract, South Korean infielder Hyeseong Kim has spent most of the second season of that contract in Triple-A where he hit .265 with a .682 OPS in 84 games. He hasn’t been up with the Dodgers since May but Roberts said Kim will be part of the “conversation” for the postseason roster.
“My expectation is Hyeseong will be here during the off week (next week) and potentially be a conversation for the postseason (roster) because he has the ability to run, to play defense, and steal a base,” Roberts said. “He’s in the conversation, yes.”
Kim was on the postseason roster last fall, appearing in just two games. It will be difficult to give him a spot on a bench that seems set with Alex Call, Hunter Feduccia, Miguel Rojas, Kiké Hernandez and Josue De Paula.
ROSTER MOVES
The Dodgers placed pitcher Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list on Sunday and recalled Emmet Sheehan from Triple-A to pitch ‘bulk’ in Sunday’s game.
Also, reliever Seth Halvorsen was returned to Triple-A and reliever Kyle Hurt was recalled.
Sheehan is still under consideration for a bullpen role on the postseason roster.
UP NEXT
The Dodgers are off on Monday.
Padres (TBA) at Dodgers (TBA), Tuesday, 7:10 p.m., SportsNet LA, 570 AM

item.title: [True Blue LA] Better late than never: Dodgers offense pounces on the Giants’ bullpen in win
item.dc:creator: Estevão Maximo
item.description: Repeating the trend of these series’ first two games, the Dodgers didn’t take the lead until the second half of the game—this time keeping their scoring to nearly the minimum needed to overcome the Giants, sweeping their rivals with a 3-1 victory that relied heavily on Emmet Sheehan’s work as the bulk man, following Jack Dreyer. Better late than never: Dodgers offense pounces on the Giants’ bullpen in win Emmet Sheehan’s outstanding work as a follower allowed the Dodgers to beat the Giants with
item.content:encoded:
Repeating the trend of these series’ first two games, the Dodgers didn’t take the lead until the second half of the game—this time keeping their scoring to nearly the minimum needed to overcome the Giants, sweeping their rivals with a 3-1 victory that relied heavily on Emmet Sheehan’s work as the bulk man, following Jack Dreyer.
Better late than never: Dodgers offense pounces on the Giants’ bullpen in win
Emmet Sheehan’s outstanding work as a follower allowed the Dodgers to beat the Giants with just three runs
Without putting the ball in play, the Giants placed a man on third in the opening inning, manufacturing a run partially thanks to Dreyer’s loose grip on the running game. Leadoff hitter Jonah Cox earned a walk as Dreyer struggled to locate his heater, moved to second on an errant pickoff attempt, and aggressively stole third—hardly a surprise for a rookie with 13 stolen bases in just 140 plate appearances. Cox was driven in by a Jonah Bericoto single, a run that would loom large given the effectiveness of both Sheehan and Giants starter Matt Wilkinson.
Deceptive with his low-90s fastball that gets terrific results, Giants starter Matt Wilkinson didn’t encounter many problems holding the Dodgers scoreless through five innings of work. Only twice did Wilkinson need to strand one-out doubles, but on both occasions with minimal stress. That success was at least partially owed to a lefty-heavy lineup—three of the four outs Wilkinson recorded with a runner in scoring position came against a left-handed hitter, but then again, one of the doubles came from Josue De Paula, so we mustn’t read too much into it.
As soon as Wilkinson got the hook, though, the Dodgers would tie the game in the bottom of the sixth, thanks to a solo shot from Tommy Edman off Carson Seymour. Traditionally a better power hitter from the right side, Edman was looking in the whole way and crushed one all the way out to the Giants’ bullpen.
The only reason why the Dodgers were able to tie the score with just one swing was the fact that Sheehan matched Wilkinson pitch for pitch and then some. Overall, few players have improved their case for a significant postseason role over the past couple of weeks with the Dodgers quite like Sheehan, a new pitcher since his return following a one-month stint in Triple-A. Pitching as brilliantly as he did in two September starts, Sheehan completely shut down the Giants’ lineup through 5.1 innings, enjoying great success with a curveball that induced six whiffs on 12 swings, leading him to strike out nine batters.
Proving Wilkinson and his difficult-to-pick-up fastball were the problem, the Dodgers’ offense scored again in the seventh—they took the lead thanks to a Kiké Hernández RBI single after De Paula and Max Muncy set the table despite an unfavorable matchup against the southpaw.
Mookie Betts nearly put this game to bed, but what would’ve been a two-out, three-run bomb died at the wall, leaving the score at 2-1. The Dodgers would still find a way to provide a little cushion to Tanner Scott in the ninth inning, adding one more run in the bottom of the eighth thanks to a Max Muncy two-out RBI single.
Game particulars
- Home run— Tommy Edman (7)
- WP—Kris Bubic (4-2): 0.2 IP, 1 strikeout
- LP— Sam Hentges (1-7): 0.1 IP, 3 hits, 1 run
- SV Tanner Scott (23): 1 IP, 1 walk, 1 strikeout
Up next
It’s a rare off day at home for the Dodgers before the San Diego Padres come into town on Tuesday hoping to clinch their playoff berth. Although neither team has announced their starters, based on the current schedule, the first game of that series would pit Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Robbie Ray against each other. It’s a standard 7:10 p.m. (PT).

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers kept right fielder Kyle Tucker out of their lineup for Sunday’s game after he exited Saturday’s win early.
Tucker fouled a ball off of his shin Saturday, and left the game shortly after. Manager Dave Roberts expected Tucker to return to the lineup Sunday, but the outfielder clearly isn’t fit to participate.
Who is Starting for the Dodgers?
The Dodgers are running a bullpen day on Sunday, and could have a few players fill in if needed. Jack Dreyer is getting the ball first for the Dodgers, making his second start of the season. He has a 3.19 ERA through 63 appearances with 68 strikeouts in 59.1 innings pitched.
Emmet Sheehan has a locker at Dodger Stadium as well, and could handle bulk for LA on Sunday.
Who is in the Dodgers’ Lineup?
Shortstop Mookie Betts remains in the leadoff spot for the Dodgers, and center fielder Tommy Edman shoots up the order to bat second. Left fielder Teoscar Hernandez bats third, and first baseman Freddie Freeman serves as the cleanup hitter.
Miguel Rojas enters the lineup as the second baseman and No. 5 hitter, and third baseman Max Muncy slides down the order to the No. 6 spot. Josue De Paula remains the team’s designated hitter, and following him are left fielder Kiké Hernandez and catcher Hunter Feduccia to round out the Dodgers’ lineup.
Dodgers Lineup vs. Giants
1. Mookie Betts, SS
2. Tommy Edman, CF
3. Teoscar Hernandez, LF
4. Freddie Freeman, 1B
5. Miguel Rojas, 2B
6. Max Muncy, 3B
7. Josue De Paula, DH
8. Kiké Hernandez, LF
9. Hunter Feduccia, C
Who is Starting for the Giants?
On the mound for the Giants is left-hander Matt WIlkinson, who will be making his seventh appearance of the year. He has a 4.58 ERA through 19.2 innings pitched, striking out 12 batters durign that time.
The rookie struggled in his first stint as a starter, transitioning to relief for his last two appearances and holding his opponents scoreless.
The Dodgers will look to break his scoreless streak in Sunday’s game, which begins at 1:10 p.m. PT.

item.title: [cubbiescrib.com] Dodgers could offer Cubs perfectly-timed solution to looming Ian Happ farewell

item.content:encoded:
At the very least, it seems likely that the Chicago Cubs will let both Ian Happ and Seiya Suzuki test the free-agent waters this offseason. Between the two, Suzuki makes sense for the Cubs to sign to a long-term deal, but he's positioned to be one of the best hitters available.
Even if Suzuki does return to the Cubs next season, there' the question of replacing Happ. Not to mention, as a whole, the offense could be without Carson Kelly, Michael Conforto, and Tyrone Taylor next season. Pitching is going to be the focus for the Cubs during the offseason, but they can't ignore the position-player side of the roster.
If the Cubs are going to make an addition of consequence to their starting lineup this offseason, chances are it will be in the outfield. That is where things get interesting for the Cubs, considering the rise of Josiah Hartshorn and Kane Kepley this season. Hartshorn and Kepley have both finished the 2026 season with Double-A Knoxville, and while it would aggressive for what the Cubs typically do, one of the two could find their way to Wrigley Field by the end of the 2027 season.
Not to mention, Matt Shaw and Pedro Ramirez could be options, and Ethan Conrad still figures to be involved in the long-term outlook in the outfield.
But given that the Cubs are in the middle of a contention window, it makes sense for them to look for a stopgap in the outfield for the 2027 season. While the free-agent market is thin, the trade market could point them in the direction of the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Teoscar Hernández could give Cubs exactly the stopgap they need if they move on from Ian Happ
FanSided's Pat Ragazzo takes an early look at offseason trade candidates, and among the names mentioned is Dodgers outfielder Teoscar Hernández. While the Dodgers doubled down on Hernández's role at the start of September, and he responded a resurgent month, conventional wisdom points to him being someone LA would be willing to move this offseason. Especially since Josue De Paula looks ready for an expanded role next year.
Hernández is owed over $22 next season, and carries a $15 million club option for the 2028 season. The option also includes a $6.5 million buyout. For a team that has a short-term need in the outfield with over $100 million coming off the books after the season, Hernández wouldn't be that crazy of an option for the Cubs.
The concern is that Hernández's resurgence this month could be a blip. Overall, his numbers have trended in the wrong direction over the last two years, and that could position him to be massively overpaid next season. Ultimately, that could be the reason why the Cubs steer clear of the veteran outfielder in trade talks. But if they are willing to take a gamble, this could be a move to watch for during the offseason.

item.title: [cbssports.com] Dodgers eye sweep of Giants behind surging Mookie Betts
item.dc:creator: FLM
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers will continue getting their house in order when they face the San Francisco Giants on Sunday afternoon to complete the Dodgers' next-to-last home series of the regular season. Los Angeles will use a bullpen game Sunday when it seeks a three-game series sweep, while the Giants will send left-hander Matt Wilkinson (1-3, 4.58 ERA) to the mound for his first appearance against the Dodgers. Los Angeles has a lot of uncertainty heading into its 14th consecutive playoff appearan
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers will continue getting their house in order when they face the San Francisco Giants on Sunday afternoon to complete the Dodgers' next-to-last home series of the regular season.
Los Angeles will use a bullpen game Sunday when it seeks a three-game series sweep, while the Giants will send left-hander Matt Wilkinson (1-3, 4.58 ERA) to the mound for his first appearance against the Dodgers.
Los Angeles has a lot of uncertainty heading into its 14th consecutive playoff appearance -- including the rotation because Blake Snell is working through groin discomfort -- while the offense has Shohei Ohtani (biceps inflammation, knee soreness) and Andy Pages (left hand fracture) nearing a return from the injured list.
The revival of Mookie Betts, along with the arrival of Josue De Paula from the minor leagues, has brought renewed energy after a mid-summer swoon.
The Dodgers still do not have a return date for Ohtani, with Betts the latest to claim the star's leadoff spot. Betts had two home runs among his three hits as the leadoff hitter Friday, then returned to the top spot Saturday and went 4-for-4 with three doubles and a walk. He has 10 hits over his past three games.
"The main thing is doing it when it counts," Betts said. "So right now, we just keep laying the foundation, and then when playoffs come, just need it to show up (offensively)."
Betts had an RBI single in the second inning and an RBI double in the fourth Saturday as the Dodgers earned a 10-4 victory over the Giants.
"He's not a chase guy anyway, but he's cut that down considerably," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. "The quality of contact is considerably higher. And then now you've got that attitude, that confidence, that we're used to seeing with Mookie."
The Dodgers' Will Smith also is rounding into form after missing three months with neck inflammation. Smith returned at the start of September and has three home runs over his past nine games, including one in each of the past two games.
Smith started consecutive games Friday and Saturday for the third time since he returned, although he is expected to be used off the bench, if at all, on Sunday.
The Giants have their own injury concerns. Ace Logan Webb was the latest to see his season end early, due to a blister on his right middle finger.
On Saturday, first baseman Bryce Eldridge missed his second consecutive game with a head laceration. The 6-foot-7 rookie bumped his head on a low overhang at the team hotel.
"He's still feeling the implications of that deal," Giants manager Tony Vitello said Saturday. "It's kind of a weird spot in the hotel. I checked it out. (Friday) it was a little bit more about just his comfort. But now, stemming from last night and this morning, those guys have been monitoring him like crazy. Just some lingering effects."
Giants rookie Victor Bericoto hit a two-run home run Saturday in his second game since returning from the injured list and now has five homers in 35 career games.
With a win Sunday, the Dodgers can earn their first three-game sweep over the Giants since April 2024. Los Angeles leads the season series 5-4, with one game remaining in L.A. and three games at San Francisco to end the regular season.

item.title: [El Nacional — La voz de todos] Mookie Betts batea de 4-4 con tres triples y dos impulsadas
item.source: El Nacional — La voz de todos

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers doblegan Giants
Mookie Betts batea de 4-4 con tres triples y dos impulsadas
El novato dominicano Josué De Paula pega sencillo impulsador de 2 carreras, anota dos y recibe dos bases por bolas
LOS ÁNGELES.— Mookie Betts bateó de 4-4 con tres dobles, Will Smith agregó tres hits, incluyendo un jonrón, y los Dodgers de Los Ángeles vencieron a los Gigantes de San Francisco 10-4 el sábado por la noche.
El sencillo de dos carreras con dos outs de Tommy Edman ante el relevista Philip Abner rompió el empate a 4 en la quinta entrada. El bateador emergente Miguel Rojas conectó un sencillo productor para poner el marcador 7-4 a favor de su equipo, y Edman fue puesto out en el plato para finalizar la entrada.
Todos los Dodgers conectaron al menos un hit, excepto Freddie Freeman, quien tuvo un mal desempeño y se fue de 0 de 5. Betts igualó su mejor marca de la temporada en hits y el equipo superó a los Giants en jonrones, 15-8. El ex Jugador Más Valioso de la Liga Americana bateaba .249 hace una semana y desde entonces ha elevado su promedio a .261.
Los Dodgers anotaron carreras en seis entradas consecutivas al inicio de un partido por primera vez en 10 años. Han anotado 15 carreras en sus últimas siete entradas ofensivas, incluyendo cuatro jonrones en la octava entrada contra Abner en el primer partido de la serie del viernes.
Los campeones de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional (95-60) ganaron su partido número 95 para colocarse 35 juegos por encima del .500, su mejor marca de la temporada.
El tercer doble de Betts abrió la sexta entrada y anotó con un sencillo productor de Smith ante el relevista Joel Kuhnel. El novato Josue De Paula añadió un sencillo productor de dos carreras, ampliando la ventaja a 10-4.
En tres ocasiones, los Giants remontaron para empatar el partido, solo para ver cómo los Dodgers volvían a tomar la delantera, destacando el jonrón de dos carreras de Victor Bericoto, de 425 pies, que empató el partido en la tercera entrada.
El abridor de los Dodgers, Tarik Skubal (11-7), no estuvo especialmente brillante, permitiendo cuatro carreras y ocho hits en cinco entradas. El zurdo ponchó a tres y otorgó dos bases por bolas, y los Dodgers ganaron sus últimas seis salidas.
El relevista Edwin Díaz lanzó una octava entrada sin permitir carreras en su segunda aparición consecutiva desde que salió de la lista de lesionados el viernes.
El abridor de los Giants, Yunior Marte (0-1), permitió seis carreras y ocho hits en 4 2/3 entradas con dos ponches.
El jardinero derecho de los Dodgers, Kyle Tucker, recibió un foul en la rodilla y fue reemplazado por Alex Call en la séptima entrada.

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Scout's Josue De Paula assessment will excite Dodgers fans
item.dc:creator: Pat Ragazzo

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers might have their next homegrown superstar in outfielder Josue De Paula. That's at least according to one National League scout who spoke with FanSided.
"JDP is the most polished young hitter I have seen in my 17 years of professional baseball," the scout said. "He is never rushed, immensely confident, and has been incredibly consistent since entering pro ball."
De Paula has done nothing but produce in the minor leagues since signing with the Dodgers out of the Dominican Republic as a 16-year-old in 2022. This season, he slashed .303/.401/.547 with a .948 OPS, 27 homers, 104 RBI and 31 stolen bases in 124 games in Double-A. As a result, he replaced Shohei Ohtani, who went on the IL with knee and biceps injuries, on the Dodgers' roster this month.
De Paula, 21, was called up to make his MLB debut on September 11. He proceeded to crush a moonshot of a three-run home run two days later for his first career big league hit. The future is certainly bright for the left-handed hitter. De Paula is the Dodgers' No. 1 ranked prospect and No. 4 in all of baseball, per Baseball America.
Dodgers rookie Josue De Paula was compared to MLB legend Manny Ramirez
The same scout told FanSided that De Paula's natural hitting skills compare to a former Dodger and legendary slugger.
"The only fair comparison to the ease in which hitting comes to (De Paula) is Manny Ramirez," the scout said. "He was born to hit and has done nothing but refine his gift the last four-plus years."
This is good company to be in. Ramirez was a 12-time All-Star and nine-time Silver Slugger Award winner across 18-years in the big leagues. He led the American League in RBI (1999), won a batting title (2002) and led the AL in home runs (2004). Ramirez was also a two-time World Series champion with the Boston Red Sox and won World Series MVP in 2004. Ramirez would be in the Hall of Fame if not for his ties to performance-enhancing drugs.
If De Paula can have similar results in the majors as Ramirez, the youngster will be in pretty good shape, and so will the Dodgers. Los Angeles has center fielder Andy Pages under control through 2030, left fielder Teoscar Hernandez is entering the final year of his deal in 2027, and Kyle Tucker is in year-one of a four-year, $240 million deal that has opt outs after 2027 and 2028. Luckily, De Paula is expected to be a future core piece of the Dodgers' outfield for many years to come.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers Notes: LA Promotes Outfielder, Shohei Ohtani Injury Update, Teoscar Hernandez Trade?

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants, 10-4, on Saturday night and improved to 95-60 on the year.
Left-hander Tarik Skubal had an uncharacteristic start, striking out just three batters over five innings while allowing four earned runs. Fortunately, the bullpen picked him up with four scoreless innings.
Offensively, Mookie Betts had a marvelous four-hit night and Will Smith notched three hits of his own, including a home run. Rookie Josue De Paula continued to impress with two walks and a two-run single with the bases loaded.
After the game, manager Dave Roberts provided an update on Shohei Ohtani, saying he has a "good chance" of being activated during the team's series against the San Diego Padres this week.
While Ohtani is eligible to be activated on Wednesday, it's currently unclear if that's the day he'll be back.
Either way, the Dodgers are expecting Ohtani back soon, and he took a major step on Saturday, hitting off the Trajekt machine and running the bases before the game.
In his stead, De Paula has done an unbelievable job as the everyday designated hitter.
In other news, the Dodgers recently promoted an outfielder who previously thought that his season might be over. The third-round pick in the 2024 MLB Draft was hitting .306 with a .985 OPS across 35 games in High-A and 71 appearances in Double-A this season.
Finally, veteran outfielder Teoscar Hernández was recently labeled as a likely trade candidate by Pat Ragazzo of FanSided. The insider explained that the influx of outfield talent, combined with an expiring contract that was reportedly being shopped around over the offseason, could lead to the team parting ways with "Mr. Seeds."
"The Dodgers have No. 1 prospect Josue De Paula and other young outfielders in their farm system, who could replace Hernandez in left field next season," Ragazzo wrote. "It would make sense for the Dodgers to ship Hernandez out this offseason with one-year remaining on his deal."
Here’s all the latest Dodgers news and stories (click the headline for the full article):
Dodgers Tweets of the Day
Sign up for our free newsletter and follow us on X/Twitter and Facebook for the latest news.
Gabe Smallson is a sportswriter based in Los Angeles with a focus in sports and entertainment content. Gabe has previously worked at Newsweek and Dodgers Nation. He graduated from San Francisco State University in 2020 and received his Masters of Science at the University of Southern California in 2025.

item.title: [pasadenastarnews.com] Mookie Betts stays hot as Dodgers hammer Giants
item.dc:creator: Doug Padilla
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Mookie Betts is showing that the view from the top offers a wide range of possibilities. Hitting in Shohei Ohtani’s leadoff spot for the second consecutive game, Betts’ four-hit performance on Saturday night topped his three-hit output from Friday and started some serious downhill momentum toward a 10-4 victory over the San Francisco Giants. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Mookie Betts is showing that the view from the top offers a wide range of possibilities.
Hitting in Shohei Ohtani’s leadoff spot for the second consecutive game, Betts’ four-hit performance on Saturday night topped his three-hit output from Friday and started some serious downhill momentum toward a 10-4 victory over the San Francisco Giants.
The victory kept the Dodgers (95-60) two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers (97-58) for the best record in the National League and four games ahead of the Atlanta Braves (91-64) for the No. 2 playoff seed with seven games remaining. That includes four games against the Giants, who continue to limp toward the finish line of a miserable, injury-riddled season.
Betts couldn’t be feeling better, with his past two games part of a run of 10 hits over the last three games he has played. After more than two months of looking for an offensive leader, Betts has charged into the role, while reaching base five times on Saturday.
“It’s good; It’s fun,” Betts said. “But the main thing is doing it when it counts. So right now, we just keep laying the foundation, and then when playoffs come, we just need it to show up (offensively).”
The Dodgers expect Ohtani to return for the playoffs as he makes progress from biceps and knee discomfort. Betts, though, is proving to be a more-than-adequate emergency replacement.
“You know, I couldn’t tell you that I saw this (coming), but I just felt that he was stronger,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. “He’s worked hard on that. He looks great. He’s not going to stop working, and just for it to come together has been great, and I think for me it’s just trying to keep him confident.”
The Dodgers also have been transformed by the emergence of catcher Will Smith, who returned at the start of September after three months away because of neck inflammation. He had a home run among his three hits Saturday to give him homers in consecutive games, with three over his past eight contests.
“He’ll play two or three that last series (at San Francisco), but yeah, after that, he’ll be our guy (for the playoffs),” Roberts said.
There is also 21-year-old rookie Josue De Paula, who has continued to operate with ease since arriving in the major leagues last week. De Paula had a two-run single Saturday and walked twice while scoring two runs.
All of it overshadowed Tarik Skubal’s ninth start for the Dodgers. The two-time American League Cy Young Award winner was far from his best, allowing four runs on eight hits over five innings. His three strikeouts were his least in an outing with his new club.
Skubal unleashed his frustrations in the dugout by throwing his glove and cap at the bench, while firing an empty sports drink bottle at the wall.
“Sometimes you get frustrated and you got to get it out,” Skubal said. “It’s no good just keeping it pent up. So yeah, I’m a believer in getting that stuff out and kind of just moving on from the moment. The frustration is based on execution and knowing who I am and I’m just not doing that.”
Skubal blamed a lack of fastball command for the inability to shut down the Giants.
“Not driving it up and in (and) kind of pulling the ball down at times, pushing it up at times,” Skubal said. “I think pitching is almost all fastball command and mine wasn’t great today.”
And yet the offense allowed Skubal (11-7) to pick up the win, while improving to 4-2 with a 2.95 ERA for the Dodgers.
“That’s our job. That’s what we’re supposed to do,” Betts said. “So sometimes it’s them, sometimes it’s us. As long as we win.”
Kyle Tucker provided a scare when he fouled a ball off the side of his right knee early in the game then departed in the seventh inning with the Dodgers leading by six runs. Tucker reached base twice Saturday after collecting six hits with two home runs the previous two games.
“Whatever’s working at the time, you just ride it out, whether or not it’s the way you want to go about it,” said Tucker, who expects to play Sunday. “If it’s working, it’s working. You just try to go up there and put up competitive at-bats and just do your part on defense.”
The offense was not only productive, it was steady. The Dodgers scored runs in each of the first six innings and when they were held scoreless in the seventh, Betts still reached base with a walk.
Betts opened the game for the Dodgers with a leadoff double and scored on a Max Muncy double. Betts brought home his own run with an RBI single in the second.
The Dodgers struck with Smith’s home run in the third and got an RBI double from Betts in the fourth but were still tied 4-4 heading into the bottom of the fifth. They blew the game open from there, getting a go-ahead two-run single from Tommy Edman and an RBI pinch-hit single from Miguel Rojas for a 7-4 lead.
They scored three more times in the sixth, getting a Smith RBI single followed by a two-run single from De Paula.
“I think this is the first time, seems like all year, that we’ve had four or five hitters swing the bats well for four or five games,” Roberts said. “So it’s been really good to see. Obviously, Mookie is a big part of it, but everyone else is doing their part.”
The Dodgers now have a 5-4 lead in the Giants in the season series and are in line for a sweep on Sunday, which would be their first against their longtime rival since April of 2024.

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers outslug Giants 10-4, led by Mookie Betts with four hits
Mookie Betts had four hits, including three doubles, and the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants 10-4
LOS ANGELES -- Mookie Betts went 4 for 4 with three doubles, Will Smith added three hits including a home run, and the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants 10-4 on Saturday night.
Tommy Edman's two-run, two-out single off reliever Philip Abner snapped a 4-all tie in the fifth. Pinch-hitter Miguel Rojas followed with an RBI single for a 7-4 lead, with Edman thrown out at home to end the inning.
Every Dodger had at least one hit, except for struggling Freddie Freeman who was 0 for 5. Betts tied his season high for hits and the team outslugged the Giants, 15-8. The former AL MVP was hitting .249 a week ago, and has since raised his average to .261.
The Dodgers scored runs in six straight innings to start a game for the first time in 10 years. They've scored 15 runs in their last seven offensive innings, including a four-homer eighth off Abner in Friday's series opener.
The NL West champions (95-60) won their 95th game to move a season-high 35 games above .500.
Betts' third double led off the sixth and he scored on Smith's RBI single off reliever Joel Kuhnel. Rookie Josue De Paula added a two-run RBI single, extending the lead to 10-4.
Three times the Giants rallied to tie the game only to see the Dodgers retake the lead, highlighted by Victor Bericoto's game-tying, 425-foot two-run homer in the third.
Dodgers starter Tarik Skubal (11-7) wasn't particularly sharp, allowing four runs and eight hits in five innings. The left-hander struck out three and walked two, with the Dodgers winning each of his last six outings.
Reliever Edwin Díaz pitched a scoreless eighth in his second straight appearance since coming off the injured list Friday.
Giants starter Yunior Marte (0-1) gave up six runs and eight hits in 4 2/3 innings with two strikeouts.
Dodgers right fielder Kyle Tucker fouled a ball off his knee and was replaced by Alex Call in the seventh.
Neither team had announced their starters for the series finale Sunday.
___

item.content:encoded:
Mookie Betts, Dodgers stay hot in romp over Giants
(Photo credit: Jayne Kamin)
Mookie Betts tied a season high with four hits, Tommy Edman delivered a go-ahead two-run single and the Los Angeles Dodgers stayed within two games of the best record in the National League with a 10-4 victory over the visiting San Francisco Giants on Saturday.
Betts has 10 hits over his past three games, including seven in the past two while operating out of the leadoff spot in place of an injured Shohei Ohtani. Will Smith hit a home run as the Dodgers (95-60) won for the fifth time in six games and improved to 13-3 since Sept. 3.
Tarik Skubal (11-7) gave up four runs on eight hits over five innings with three strikeouts. The left-hander is now 4-2 with a 2.85 ERA in nine starts for Los Angeles after a trade from the Detroit Tigers on Aug. 2.
Victor Bericoto hit a home run among his two hits for the Giants (64-91) while Yunior Marte (0-1) gave up six runs on eight hits over 4 2/3 innings in his fourth career appearance and second start.
San Francisco lost for the sixth time in its past eight games in its next-to-last road game of the season.
Max Muncy had an RBI double in the first inning to score Betts as the Dodgers started a stretch in which they scored in each of the first six innings. Betts had an RBI single in the second.
The Giants tied the score in the third on Bericoto's fifth home run over his first 35 career games.
Los Angeles went back on top 3-2 in the third on Smith's leadoff home run. Both teams scored in the fourth, with San Francisco tying the score 4-4 in the fifth on a double from Jung Hoo Lee.
Edman's two-run single in the fifth gave the Dodgers the lead for good and they added another in the inning for a 7-4 lead on a Miguel Rojas single.
In the sixth, Smith added an RBI single, while rookie Josue De Paula followed with a two-run single for a 10-4 advantage.
Los Angeles has a 5-4 advantage in the season series with four games still remaining between the teams.
Smith went 3-for-5 as the Dodgers collected 15 hits.
Lee went 2-for-4 for the Giants and drove in a run. The Giants had two hits in a dozen at-bats with runners in scoring position.
--Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers and San Francisco Giants kept things neck-and-neck through the first half of Saturday night’s contest, but the Dodgers rattled off six unanswered runs in a 10-4 victory.
After Tarik Skubal allowed a two-out walk to Giants designated hitter Victor Bericoto, Jung Hoo Lee attacked the first pitch he saw into the right-center field gap, but a diving play from Kyle Tucker got Skubal out of the inning with the game remaining scoreless.
Mookie Betts started things off in the bottom of the first inning with a leadoff double, and Max Muncy cashed him in with a two-strike, two-out RBI double to give the Dodgers the first lead of the game. Betts would come through again in the bottom of the second inning, lacing an RBI single the other way to plate Josue De Paula and make it a 2-0 Dodger lead.
Skubal worked his way around two baserunners for a scoreless top of the second inning, but after allowing a one-out single to Turner Hill in the top of the third inning, Bericoto launched a 3-2 fastball deep over the center field wall, tying the game at 2. Will Smith wasted no time giving the Dodgers the lead again, hammering a solo home run to lead off the bottom of the third inning, giving him his second home run in as many games.
The Giants responded with a pair of leadoff singles from Andrew Knizner and Osleivis Basabe to begin the top of the fourth inning. A bunt from Christian Koss moved both men into scoring position, and a squeeze bunt from Jonah Cox plated Knizner to tie the game at 3.
The Dodgers would get another one-run lead thanks to an RBI double from Mookie Betts in the bottom of the fourth inning— his second double and second RBI of the game. The Giants wouldn’t let Skubal settle in for the top of the fifth inning, as Bericoto and Lee both doubled to tie the game at four.
Saturday turned out to be Skubal’s worst outing of the season, let alone as a Dodger. Skubal managed to complete five innings of work but allowed a season-high four earned runs, while his three strikeouts on the night were the fewest in any start since striking out three on August 14 of last season against the Minnesota Twins.
Despite the poor start, the Dodgers put Skubal officially in line for the win as Teoscar Hernández ignited a two-out rally with an opposite-field single. Kyle Tucker and Josue De Paula each followed with a walk, and Tommy Edman snapped out of a 1-37 funk with a go-ahead, two-run single to give the Dodgers their first multi-run lead since the third. Miguel Rojas knocked a pinch-hit single to bring home De Paula, but Edman was thrown out at home attempting to make it a four-run inning.
Evan Phillips recorded the first clean inning of the night in relief of Skubal in the top of the sixth inning, and the Dodgers responded with another three-run inning, capitalized by a two-run single by De Paula and giving the Dodgers a six-run cushion.
After a scoreless inning from Alex Vesia in the seventh inning, Edwin Díaz came in for his second consecutive game since returning from injury, pitching a scoreless top of the eighth inning while picking up a pair of strikeouts.
Mookie Betts finished Saturday going 4-4 with three doubles and two RBI, reaching base five times after a walk in the seventh inning. Betts is now 10-12 (.833 average) over his last three games with three doubles, two home runs and five RBI.
With their win over the Giants, the Dodgers maintain a four-game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the no. 2 seed in the National League. They still trail the Milwaukee Brewers by two games for the top seed.
Game particulars
- Home runs— Victor Bericoto (5); Will Smith (9)
- WP— Tarik Skubal (11-7): 5 IP, 8 hits, 4 earned runs, 2 walks, 3 strikeouts
- LP— Yunior Marte (0-1): 4 2/3 IP, 8 hits, 6 earned runs, 3 walks, 2 strikeouts
Up next
The Dodgers wrap things up against San Francisco on Sunday (1:10 p.m. PT, SportsNet LA) before hosting the San Diego Padres for their final regular season home series beginning Tuesday. Both teams have yet to announce their starters.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Andy Pages went through the paces on Saturday afternoon, grinding through an intense on-field workout in the clearest sign yet that he will be ready to return on Tuesday to open the final home series of the regular season.
Pages wore a fitness tracker, similar to what soccer players use to monitor all aspects of physical fitness. Coaches and staff put him through an estimated five simulated innings all in a compressed window of time.
The All-Star center fielder not only tested his broken left hand, but he also pushed his physical fitness to the limits.
Pages went from hitting to defense to base running and then doing it all over again to make sure he is ready for the rigors of play next week. His return is expected to come in the opener of a three-game series against the San Diego Padres.
While that kind of energy output is typically done in a rehab game, there aren’t many minor league options remaining this late in the season.
One thing Pages will not get is the chance to hit off a pitcher at full velocity.
“I think that from what I understand, we don’t have really any available arms,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said about the prospect of a live batting practice session. “A lot of our guys are playing in playoff games in the minors, and we have (Eric) Lauer, who’s on the IL. So, we don’t really have anyone.”
That’s not ideal for a player coming off the uncertainty that comes with a hand injury. But Pages did show that his hand soreness has subsided enough to hit multiple balls over the outfield wall.
“I’m expecting good at-bats,” Roberts said. “I can’t speak to the performance. I just want him to have good at-bats, and I’m not sure where he’s going to hit. Somewhere middle to the bottom (of the order), I think. I think I’m waiting just like you guys are waiting to see how it looks.”
The Dodgers close the season with six consecutive games, including the season-ending series in San Francisco next weekend.
“Six in a row, and that seems pretty aggressive (for Pages),” Roberts said. “So, I think that we do want to get him as many at-bats as possible, but we have to make sure that his legs are under him, feeling good, so we don’t go backward or get injured in that respect. It is going to be a balancing act and just keeping a keen eye on Andy, for sure.”
Regardless of what his swing looks like, the Dodgers still trust him in center field. After all, his World Series-saving catch in Game 7 last season came as a late-inning defensive replacement.
“Playing a premium position and playing it well is hugely important,” Roberts said.
ROTATING THE ROTATION
Left-hander Blake Snell is not expected to pitch in the upcoming series against the Padres, but he has not been ruled out for the series against the Giants next weekend.
Snell left his start Thursday after one inning in Cincinnati because of groin discomfort.
“He’s trending very well,” Roberts said about Snell’s recovery in recent days.
Right-hander Roki Sasaki is expected to pitch in the upcoming series against the Padres, although his role has not yet been specified. There is a chance Sasaki could start a game against San Diego, or come out of the bullpen, which had been his expected role in the postseason.
“It will be multiples for sure,” Roberts said about Sasaki’s innings count. “I just don’t know exactly when.”
A LEADING MAN
Shohei Ohtani is still expected to return to play before the regular season ends next Sunday, although there remains no target date.
In the meantime, the Dodgers continue to weigh their options in the leadoff spot. Tommy Edman was there immediately after Ohtani went on the injured list earlier this month, Josue De Paula took a turn there and Mookie Betts has been the latest to stake a claim.
Betts hit two home runs from the leadoff spot Friday and was back at the top of the lineup on Saturday.
“Yeah, I think that certainly there is an uncertainty with Shohei, all the while expecting him to be back,” Roberts said. “But you do got to kind of prepare for whatever, and I just think that Mookie’s swinging the bat well, has hit there many times throughout his career, so it just kind of makes sense.”
Betts had three hits Wednesday in Cincinnati and three more Friday against the Giants in the leadoff spot, including two home runs. He is batting .356 with six home runs and 18 RBIs in 15 September games.
ALSO
The Dodgers are expected to select a pitcher to pick up bulk innings on Sunday in a hybrid bullpen game against the Giants, but the exact plan remains undetermined.
UP NEXT
Giants (LHP Matt Wilkinson, 1-3, 4.58 ERA) at Dodgers (TBA), Sunday, 1:10 p.m., SportsNet LA, 570 AM, 1020 AM

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Dodgers' September surge continues: L.A. racks up 15 hits in win over Giants
item.dc:creator: Maddie Lee
item.description: - Click here to listen to this article - - Mookie Betts hits three doubles and the Dodgers surge for 15 hits to overcome a shaky start by Tarik Skubal in a 10-4 win over the San Francisco Giants. When Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said earlier this week that the best was yet to come, his expectations were centered on the offense. In the Dodgers’ 10-4 rout of the San Francisco Giants on Saturday, that better version of the offense was on display, putting together a pair of three-run rallies
item.content:encoded:
- Click here to listen to this article
-
- Mookie Betts hits three doubles and the Dodgers surge for 15 hits to overcome a shaky start by Tarik Skubal in a 10-4 win over the San Francisco Giants.
When Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said earlier this week that the best was yet to come, his expectations were centered on the offense.
In the Dodgers’ 10-4 rout of the San Francisco Giants on Saturday, that better version of the offense was on display, putting together a pair of three-run rallies in back-to-back innings to take pressure off the pitching staff.
Before that breakout started in the fifth inning, it was a back-and-forth game.
Dodgers left-handed starting pitcher Tarik Skubal pitched only five innings, tied for his shortest start with the Dodgers. And he surrendered four runs, the worst mark of his Dodgers tenure.
Tyler Glasnow hasn’t had the greatest of seasons, but the Dodgers will need him to deliver in the playoffs if they want to win another World Series title.
Entering the game, Skubal appeared to be peaking. His last two starts, both against the Reds, were some of his most efficient.
That efficiency, however, regressed against the Giants (64-91).
Though he got through the first two innings without giving up a run — thanks in part to a diving catch by right fielder Kyle Tucker made in the gap to end the first — he issued two-out walks in each.
The Dodgers’ offense used that time to mount a lead. Leadoff hitter Mookie Betts, who finished the day with three doubles and a single, hit the first of those doubles in his first at-bat, and Max Muncy authored his own to drive in the first run.
The next inning, rookie Josue De Paula’s walk, and singles from Alex Freeland and Betts combined to push in another run.
Then Skubal began to struggle. With a runner on second and one out, he pitched to a full count against designated hitter Victor Bericoto. Skubal missed down the middle with a fastball, and Bericoto sent it 425 feet to center field. It landed on the netting on the other side of the wall to tie the score.
The Dodgers’ offense, coming alive in September, struck back in the third. Catcher Will Smith hit his second home run in as many nights, launching the second pitch of the frame into left-field stands.
The Giants took a different approach to tie the score for a second time. After back-to-back singles, they used back-to-back sacrifice bunts to advance the runners and score another run.
Then the two teams traded runs again. Betts put the Dodgers (95-60) up with an RBI double in the fourth. Skubal gave up back-to-back doubles in the fifth.
That marked both the end of Skubal’s start and the beginning of the Dodgers’ offensive onslaught.
If the man trying to revive the Montreal Expos as an expansion team succeeds, Dan Evans is his choice for president of baseball operations.
The Dodgers brought seven batters to the plate in the fifth, and all but one reached base. Tommy Edman hit a two-run single. And pinch-hitting Miguel Rojas almost matched him, but Giants left fielder Turner Hill made a perfect throw to nab Edman in a close play at home to end the inning.
Betts’ and Smith’s bats stayed hot to open the sixth with a leadoff double and one-out RBI single, respectively. The Dodgers took advantage of the Giants’ sloppy infield play to load the bases for De Paula, who lined a two-run single into shallow center field.
Those were the kinds of stifling rallies that had defined the Dodgers offense earlier in the season, when they were scoring regularly in double digits.
The Dodgers’ 15 hits Saturday were their most in a game since July 2 against the San Diego Padres, and just two shy of their season high.

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Josue De Paula drawing Juan Soto comparisons hints Dodgers were right to bid low
item.dc:creator: Katrina Stebbins
item.description: Josue De Paula has cooled down a bit since his statement game against the Miami Marlins on September 13, but the Los Angeles Dodgers still have a lot to love about their No. 1 prospect. item.content:encoded:
Josue De Paula has cooled down a bit since his statement game against the Miami Marlins on September 13, but the Los Angeles Dodgers still have a lot to love about their No. 1 prospect. It took him 12 at-bats to suffer his first major league strikeout, and he's only struck out once more since then.
De Paula took his knowledge of the strike zone to another level during the Dodgers' latest series opener against the Cincinnati Reds. He got to a 2-2 count against Reds starter Nick Lodolo in the top of the fifth. Lodolo put a sinker low and away that home plate umpire Tom Hanahan called a ball.
Reds catcher Tyler Stephenson was quick to challenge, but at the same time, De Paula had gotten into a crouch and shook his head as if to say, "That one was definitely out of the zone."
De Paula was right, and the Reds lost their one remaining challenge. He went on to walk on the next pitch, and then steal second.
It wasn't quite a Soto shuffle, but it was close enough to draw comparisons. He responded, "Hey, I'm not mad about it."
Revisiting the Dodgers' Juan Soto pursuit as Josue De Paula draw comparisons
The Dodgers were involved in Juan Soto's free agent market in the 2024-25 offseason and went as far as to offer $600 million, which was, of course, eclipsed by the New York Mets' $765 million and even the New York Yankees' $760 million.
At least part of LA's hesitance to offer him a $700-plus million contract was rooted in keeping Shohei Ohtani atop the payroll and not supplanting their star player, but De Paula, though still a very distant eventuality, was on the horizon as well.
Soto and De Paula's prospect profiles are startlingly similar — 70-grade hit, 65 power, 50 run, arm, and field for Soto, and 65-grade hit, 60 power, 40 run and field, and 50 arm for De Paula. Both, as Paula has already put on display, have an advanced understanding of the strike zone.
The Dodgers don't plan well enough around their prospects to try to make a claim that they exited the Soto bidding because they had De Paula in the chamber, but it's certainly been a happy development that the one massive free agent the Dodgers didn't go all-in on happens to be reflected in their No. 1 prospect two years later.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Dodgers Lineup vs. Giants: Mookie Betts, Kyle Tucker Look to Stay Hot
item.dc:creator: Nelson Espinal
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are hoping to keep the momentum rolling after an electric series-opening win against the San Francisco Giants. The Dodgers won 8-2 on Friday night at Dodger Stadium, their first game back from a seven-game road trip. Many struggling Dodgers got a notable confidence boost, and the hope is that it carries over. Dodgers’ Lineup 1. Mookie Betts, SS 2. Freddie Freeman, 1B 3. Will Smith, C 4. Max Muncy, 3B 5. Teoscar Hernandez, LF 6. Kyle Tucker, RF 7. Josue De Paula, DH 8. Tom
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are hoping to keep the momentum rolling after an electric series-opening win against the San Francisco Giants.
The Dodgers won 8-2 on Friday night at Dodger Stadium, their first game back from a seven-game road trip. Many struggling Dodgers got a notable confidence boost, and the hope is that it carries over.
Dodgers’ Lineup
1. Mookie Betts, SS
2. Freddie Freeman, 1B
3. Will Smith, C
4. Max Muncy, 3B
5. Teoscar Hernandez, LF
6. Kyle Tucker, RF
7. Josue De Paula, DH
8. Tommy Edman, CF
9. Alex Freeland, 2B
On Friday, Kyle Tucker went 2-for-3 with a home run and a walk. Over the last seven games, he is raking: .333/.467/.792 through seven games with three home runs, six walks, and just three strikeouts.
Additionally, Mookie Betts is red-hot. Over his last 15 games, he is hitting .356/.457/.729, according to MLB.com.
The Dodgers are facing a righty, but for Betts, it has not mattered what hand the pitcher uses.
Tucker could use another good game to keep the ball rolling, but really, Freddie Freeman is the name to watch.
He is still in a slump, and as he battles a knee injury, Freeman will be worth monitoring.
Who is pitching for the Dodgers?
The Dodgers have Tarik Skubal on the mound, making his penultimate regular-season start as a Dodger.
Skubal has really started rounding into form. He has a 2.52 ERA through eight games in blue, with just 57 strikeouts and 11 walks.
The stuff for Skubal still hasn’t reached its former peak, but his last start was a real taste of what he brings. He pitched seven innings, allowed 1 walk, three hits, and totaled nine strikeouts.
Skubal is building toward a classic Skubal outing, looking unhittable through every pitch.

item.title: [USA Today] ‘It’s like a movie:' Josue De Paula embraces spotlight in Los Angeles
item.dc:creator: Andrés Soto
item.description: ‘It’s like a movie:' Josue De Paula embraces spotlight in Los Angeles When the Los Angeles Dodgers were in Cincinnati on the second leg of their most recent road trip, manager Dave Roberts approached Josue De Paula. "Just wait until we get back to LA," he recalled Roberts telling him. "It's different." item.content:encoded:
‘It’s like a movie:' Josue De Paula embraces spotlight in Los Angeles
When the Los Angeles Dodgers were in Cincinnati on the second leg of their most recent road trip, manager Dave Roberts approached Josue De Paula.
"Just wait until we get back to LA," he recalled Roberts telling him. "It's different."
Sure enough, the raucous 48,000 fans -- a light crowd by Dodger Stadium standards -- packed inside Chavez Ravine for his home debut on Friday, Sept. 18 surpassed whatever the rookie's expectations were. Everything, from the environment to the deafening cheers that only seemed to grow louder as the Dodgers slugged their way to an 8-2 win over the hated rival San Francisco Giants, to the air itself, felt different.
"It's like a movie, man," De Paula told USA TODAY Sports.
De Paula, 21, has played his role perfectly through his first week in the big leagues.
The No. 6 prospect in baseball carries himself with a confidence that's rarely seen in someone as young as him. He's played in only eight games since being called up straight from Double-A Tulsa after Shohei Ohtani was placed on the injured list, or "just thrown into it" as he put it, but De Paula has relied on the skillset that got him here. He controls the strike zone, seeing the ball extremely well and is selective with what pitches he swings at, rarely chasing. That part of his game has transitioned seamlessly.
When De Paula does see a pitch he likes, his calm demeanor at the plate helps him stay centered and keeps him from jumping out ahead of the ball.
"I feel the adrenaline, but I feel like I just know how to pinpoint it and focus it," he said. "I'm so locked in, but I know how to calm myself down."
And when he does make contact, it's loud. So is De Paula.
That was seen in the bottom of the sixth inning on Friday. De Paula walked up to "Ima Boss" by Meek Mill (his third different walk-up song of the night by the way, this one was chosen by his mom). The triumphant horns on the 2011 anthem produced by Jahlil Beats had barely subsided over the loudspeakers when De Paula slapped a first-pitch slider from Giants reliever Jason Foley 107 mph into the gap in the right field for an RBI double that scored the go-ahead run from first.
Once he got to second base standing up, De Paula threw his hands in the air and hit the Dodgers' on-base celebration, swiveling his hips around before putting his own twist on it: pounding his chest and flexing toward his teammates in the dugout.
"He loves playing the game," Mookie Betts said. "He's full of life. When he gets on the field, it's like a quiet focus, but when he's off the field he likes joking ... and whatnot. He's a good kid."
Where does that unflappable joy come from?
"We got some swag in Brooklyn. We got some swag in the Dominican Republic. I just feel like I got a chip on my shoulder," De Paula said. "And it just comes out naturally."
That came out again in the bottom of the eighth when Giants reliever Philip Abner threw a first-pitch fastball up that was called a strike by umpire Louie Krupa. De Paula immediately tapped his helmet to challenge, and ABS showed the ball had missed the top of the zone 0.1 inches. The Dodger Stadium crowd got fired up as they watched the replay unfold on the jumbotron and the call was overturned to ball one, and De Paula nodded his head toward his teammates before working a two-out walk on four pitches.
Betts homered in the very next at-bat to break open a five-run lead. Will Smith then followed that up with the Dodgers' fourth long ball of the inning.
"Love De Paula," Roberts said. "I just love his at-bats. It's one of those things that we knew that coming up to the big leagues, he wasn't going to get overwhelmed, and it just helps when you control the strike zone. He takes his walks, when the ball is in the hitting zone, he can slug you, but he also knows how to get a base hit. It's been very professional."
De Paula finished his Dodger Stadium debut 2-for-3 with two runs, and RBI and a walk to bring his OPS up to .924. It's been a very small sample size, and baseball has a way of humbling even the most skilled hitters. It is, after all, a game of failure. But what he has been able to do in his first "trial run", filling in for the back-to-back National League MVP no less, might be indicative of something larger.
At the very least, he's played himself into the postseason roster conversation.
"To have (Roberts) believe in me so much," De Paula said. "I always have confidence in myself but to have someone like that believe in you, it just puts another oomph on your shoulder. It feels amazing."
For now, De Paula's just working. The weakest area of his game is his defense, and while the vast majority of this first stint in the majors will be as a designated hitter, he's using the opportunity get better. De Paula's taking advice from Roberts and the entire coaching staff. He's asking his teammates questions. He's shagging fly balls every day.
"I'm gonna shut a lot of people up with my defense very soon," he said. "It's gonna take some time."
That opportunity likely won't come for a while; Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker are both getting hot and settling into their rhythms in the corner outfield spots in the final two weeks of the regular season. If De Paula does make the postseason roster after Ohtani comes back, it would probably be as a lefty bat off the bench.
Whatever happens over the next two weeks before October, De Paula's focused on the now, enjoying every moment he can. He got the ball back from his first Dodger Stadium hit – a leadoff single to right field in the fifth inning – and he knows exactly where to put it.
"I'm gonna give it to my parents," De Paula said. "I might give it to them right now."
If you purchase through our links, the USA Today Network may earn a commission. Prices were accurate at the time of publication but may change.

item.title: [New York Post] Dodgers phenom Josue De Paula goes viral after starstruck Shohei Ohtani moment
item.dc:creator: Grant Young
item.description: The Dodgers have received a surge of energy from Josue De Paula. The 21-year-old rookie was a star in his Dodger Stadium debut on Friday night, going 2-for-3 with two runs and an RBI in an 8-2 win over the Giants. But a hilarious moment involving Shohei Ohtani is what’s making De Paula (who has a .924 OPS in 21 at-bats with Los Angeles) even more beloved among Dodgers fans. The SportsNet LA broadcast for Friday night’s game followed De Paula walking down the Dodgers’ dugout after he scored a run
item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers have received a surge of energy from Josue De Paula.
The 21-year-old rookie was a star in his Dodger Stadium debut on Friday night, going 2-for-3 with two runs and an RBI in an 8-2 win over the Giants.
But a hilarious moment involving Shohei Ohtani is what’s making De Paula (who has a .924 OPS in 21 at-bats with Los Angeles) even more beloved among Dodgers fans.
The SportsNet LA broadcast for Friday night’s game followed De Paula walking down the Dodgers’ dugout after he scored a run. At one point, De Paula high-fives Ohtani and then turns around in what appeared to be starstruck awe, as if just realizing he touched the two-way superstar’s hand.
To be clear, De Paula and Ohtani have probably interacted before. De Paula was at the Dodgers’ spring training, after all.
But De Paula was called up when Ohtani was placed on the injured list with right biceps inflammation earlier this month, and Ohtani hadn’t been traveling with the team during its recent road trip.
Therefore, this could have been the first time Ohtani was in the dugout during De Paula’s Dodgers stint. Or it could just have been the first time De Paula saw Ohtani that night, either of which could have prompted his starstruck reaction.
Any Dodgers fan would be in awe if they got to interact with Ohtani. This is what made De Paula’s response feel so relatable, endearing him to his team’s fan base even further.
