item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI -- Try as they might to view 2026 as its own season, everything the Dodgers have done this year is impossible to separate from the larger context of what they have accomplished in more than a decade of excellence.
The Dodgers hit another key milestone in their title defense by reclaiming the NL West crown with an 8-2 victory over the Reds on Thursday afternoon at Great American Ball Park. Three days after their traditional champagne toast in honor of clinching a postseason berth, winning the West brought on a wild clubhouse celebration -- which they hope will be the first of many over the next several weeks.
"You get so mired in each year, it’s hard to have any perspective," president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said. "We’ve had our share of troubles this year. Things where we had to work harder than we expected on a couple of fronts. But the important thing is how we finish and how we go into October."
In their record-tying 14 consecutive postseason appearances, the Dodgers have 13 division titles. The only team to unseat them was the 2021 Giants, who edged them in one of the most highly contested NL West races in recent memory.
Since divisional play began in 1969, the Dodgers lead all big league teams with 24 division titles, one more than the Braves -- currently in line to win the NL East -- and three more than the Yankees. Each year's achievements raise the bar for every ensuing year. The expectations facing the Dodgers have become nearly impossible to meet. But they've embraced them gladly.
"There is certainly a higher expectation when, if you don't win the World Series, you fail," manager Dave Roberts said. "But that's kind of part of what you signed up with the Dodgers.”
The Dodgers' offense, whose inconsistency has been a perpetual concern over the course of the season, provided plenty of early support to back a scheduled bullpen game. Kyle Tucker led the way with a four-hit, three-RBI showing, finishing a triple shy of the Dodgers’ first cycle since 2017. Freddie Freeman, Max Muncy, Josue De Paula and Miguel Rojas also knocked in runs.
Justin Wrobleski opened the bullpen game with three perfect innings, and while Blake Treinen surrendered a solo home run in the fourth, Landon Knack pitched four scoreless frames before Seth Halvorsen allowed a run in the ninth.
With nine games remaining in the regular season, the Dodgers are far from full strength. Their best hitter, Shohei Ohtani, is on the 15-day IL, as is first-time All-Star Andy Pages. The six-man rotation they carried for most of the season has been reduced to four fully stretched-out starters on the active roster, necessitating Thursday's bullpen game.
"It's been the same thing the last couple years," Muncy said. "We've had guys go down. We've had guys step up in their place. … That's all that we ask, and we've been able to survive a lot."
The Dodgers are expecting reinforcements back before the postseason, and would greatly benefit from securing a first-round bye to advance directly to the NL Division Series -- giving them five days off after the end of the regular season. They hold a four-game lead over the Braves for the No. 2 seed in the National League.
This edition of the Dodgers is not without its flaws, but then again, neither were the back-to-back champion teams in 2024 and '25. After becoming the first team in a quarter-century to defend their title last year, they will vie for the Majors' first three-peat since the 1998-2000 Yankees.
While the talk of a three-peat began almost from the moment the Dodgers became back-to-back champions last November, Roberts urged his team to stay focused on the present while keeping the larger goal in mind. In his annual speech on the first day of full-squad workouts during Spring Training, he delivered the following message: Be a greyhound, looking forward with blinders on.
Tarik Skubal was not a Dodger when Roberts gave his spring address, but he saw the message play out after he was dealt to L.A. ahead of the Trade Deadline. He arrived at the beginning of a season-high seven-game losing streak -- and the tough stretch gave him a feel for the culture that has led to his new team's sustained success.
"I think there was no panic from this group," Skubal said. "I think that’s why in big moments, pressure doesn't really get to these guys."
The Dodgers have a long road ahead as they look to get back to the World Series, but it bears similarities to the roads they have traveled before. The slate might be wiped clean every year, but they have experience weathering the challenges along the way to the promised land.
"It's a different year, but I think it's kind of the same," Mookie Betts said. "The same group of guys. We know what to expect. We know what to expect from each other. It's the same goal every year. Getting here, you can't really get too focused on how, as long as you get there."

item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers clinched the NL West on Thursday afternoon. With their 8-2 win over the Cincinnati Reds, the Dodgers captured their 13th division title in the past 14 seasons. LA won the series over the Reds and is now 93-60. Up next for LA? October baseball. Following the victory over the Reds on Thursday, rookie prospect Josue De Paula made an honest statement about the Dodgers. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers clinched the NL West on Thursday afternoon.
With their 8-2 win over the Cincinnati Reds, the Dodgers captured their 13th division title in the past 14 seasons. LA won the series over the Reds and is now 93-60.
Up next for LA? October baseball.
Following the victory over the Reds on Thursday, rookie prospect Josue De Paula made an honest statement about the Dodgers.
More MLB on Heavy: Mookie Betts Drops Heartfelt Message After Dodgers-Reds Game
Jose De Paula's Message to Dodgers After NL West Clinch
In Thursday's game, Josue De Paula went 1-for-4 with 1 RBI and a walk.
Here was his message following winning the NL West:
"Being on a winning team, I live for those special moments. I can't wait until we start winning in the playoffs. It's going to be cool."
De Paula hasn't played much with LA this season, as he's been busy tearing up the minors, but it's good he can't start wait until the team starts winning in October.
It also has to be a pretty cool moment for De Paula, who has been up with the Dodgers for all of a week and a half, and is already experiencing a division celebration champagne shower.
More MLB on Heavy: Tarik Skubal Sends Hilarious Message to Blake Snell After Reds Win
Josue De Paula's Early Showings in MLB
So far, De Paula has played in just six games for the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Across 14 at-bats, he has two hits, including a home run, two runs scored, six walks, and an OPS of .829.
It's not a huge sample size, and De Paula still has plenty of time to develop with the Dodgers.
He is still the Dodgers' #1 prospect.
In 501 ABs in AA this season, he hit 27 home runs, 37 doubles, and 31 stolen bases.

item.content:encoded:
Redacción FOX Deportes
Sin Shohei Ohtani, los Dodgers amarraron su quinto título divisional
El equipo angelino derrotó a los Cincinnati Reds y se colocó en una posición privilegiada
Los Angeles volvió a teñirse de fiesta al vencer 8-2 a los Cincinnati Reds. Con este triunfo, los Dodgers aseguraron su quinto título consecutivo de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional. La ofensiva brilló gracias a Kyle Tucker, quien pegó home run y produjo tres carreras, junto a cuadrangulares de Miguel Rojas y producciones de Freddie Freeman, Max Muncy y Josué De Paula.
La hazaña cobra un valor aún más especial por las complejas circunstancias que rodeaban al equipo en el terreno. La superestrella japonesa Shohei Ohtani tuvo que ver la celebración desde la banca, marginado del line up tras ingresar a la lista de lesionados por molestias físicas. Sin la imponente presencia de su bateador designado titular, la alineación angelina tuvo que reinventarse y responder con contundencia en el momento exacto.
Ante la ausencia del fenómeno japonés, la profundidad del plantel asumió la responsabilidad de dar la cara por el proyecto. Bateadores de experiencia y jugadores de rol enlazaron turnos de alta calidad para sostener a la ofensiva en los momentos más tensos de la jornada. Paralelamente, el pitcheo dictó cátedra desde la loma para silenciar los bates rivales y mantener el control del encuentro de principio a fin.
Al caer el último out de la tarde, el vestidor estalló en júbilo para dar inicio al ya tradicional baño de champán. Este quinto banderín divisional al hilo confirma la jerarquía de una organización construida para sobreponerse a cualquier adversidad. Con el billete a octubre garantizado, Los Angeles envía un mensaje contundente a toda la liga de cara a la postemporada.
LO MÁS VISTO

item.content:encoded:
Los Dodgers reconquistan el Oeste de la Liga Nacional y sellan su 14ª postemporada consecutiva
CINCINNATI._ Por más que intenten ver el 2026 como una temporada independiente, todo lo que los Dodgers han hecho este año es imposible de separar del contexto más amplio de lo que han logrado en más de una década de excelencia.
Catorce clasificaciones consecutivas a la postemporada. Cinco títulos divisionales seguidos. La inusual oportunidad de luchar por un tricampeonato de la Serie Mundial.
Los Dodgers alcanzaron otro hito importante en la defensa de su título al recuperar la corona del Oeste de la Liga Nacional con una victoria de 8-2 sobre los Rojos la tarde del jueves en el Great American Ball Park. Tres días después de su tradicional brindis con champaña para celebrar que aseguraron un lugar en la postemporada, conquistar el Oeste desató una eufórica celebración en el clubhouse, que esperan sea la primera de muchas durante las próximas semanas.
En sus 14 participaciones consecutivas en la postemporada, igualando un récord, los Dodgers han conquistado 13 títulos divisionales. El único equipo que logró destronarlos fueron los Gigantes del 2021, que los superaron por estrecho margen en una de las luchas por el Oeste de la Liga Nacional más reñidas de los últimos tiempos.
La ofensiva de los Dodgers, cuya inconsistencia ha sido una preocupación constante a lo largo de la temporada, brindó bastante respaldo desde temprano para apoyar un juego de bullpen programado. Kyle Tucker encabezó el ataque con cuatro hits y tres carreras impulsadas, quedándose a un triple de conseguir el primer ciclo de los Dodgers desde el 2017. Freddie Freeman, Max Muncy, el dominicano Josué De Paula y el venezolano Miguel Rojas también remolcaron anotaciones.
Justin Wrobleski abrió el juego de bullpen con tres innings perfectos, y aunque Blake Treinen permitió un jonrón solitario en el cuarto episodio, Landon Knack lanzó cuatro entradas en blanco antes de que Seth Halvorsen concediera una rayita en el noveno acto.
Con nueve juegos restantes en la temporada regular, los Dodgers están lejos de contar con todo su plantel. Su mejor bateador, Shohei Ohtani, está en la lista de lesionados de 15 días, al igual que el cubano Andy Pagés, llamado por primera vez al Juego de Estrellas. La rotación de seis abridores que utilizaron durante gran parte de la temporada se ha reducido a cuatro abridores completamente acondicionados en el róster activo, lo que hizo necesario recurrir a un juego de bullpen el jueves.
Los Dodgers esperan recuperar refuerzos antes de la postemporada y se beneficiarían enormemente de asegurar el descanso en la primera ronda para avanzar directamente a la Serie Divisional de la Liga Nacional, lo que les daría cinco días libres después del final de la temporada regular. Tienen una ventaja de 4.0 juegos sobre los Bravos por el segundo puesto de la Liga Nacional.
Esta versión de los Dodgers no está exenta de defectos, pero tampoco lo estuvieron los equipos campeones consecutivos del 2024 y 2025. Después de convertirse el año pasado en el primer equipo en un cuarto de siglo en defender con éxito su título, buscarán el primer tricampeonato de Grandes Ligas desde los Yanquis de 1998 al 2000.
“Tenemos tanta hambre como en el 2024 y 2025”, dijo el piloto Dave Roberts. “Esta es una temporada aparte. Nuestros muchachos lo entienden”.
(Con información de MLB)

Dodgers clinch 5th straight NL West title, 13th in 14 years, Tucker has 4 hits in 8-2 win over Reds
The Los Angeles Dodgers clinched their fifth consecutive NL West division title and 13th in the 14 seasons, sparked by four hits from Kyle Tucker that included a first-inning home run in an 8-2 win over the Cincinnati Reds, The two-time World Series ch...
CINCINNATI -- The Los Angeles Dodgers clinched their fifth consecutive NL West division title and 13th in the 14 seasons, sparked by four hits from Kyle Tucker that included a first-inning home run in an 8-2 win over the Cincinnati Reds on Thursday,
The two-time World Series champions already were assured of their 14th straight postseason appearance, trying the record Atlanta set from 1991 to 2005. Los Angeles (93-60) had clinched no worse than a wild-card berth on Monday.
Los Angeles opened a 9 1/2-game lead over second-place San Diego and has the second-best record in the NL as they try to overtake Milwaukee (95-57 entering Thursday) for the top NL seed. The division clinching was the fourth earliest for the Dodgers after Sept. 10 in 2019, Sept. 13 in 2022 and Sept. 16 in 2023.
Tucker fell a triple short of the cycle and had three RBIs, hitting a single and a pair of doubles. He hit his 16th homer, a two-run drive in the first off Brady Singer, who allowed seven runs, nine hits and four walks in 3 1/3 innings.
Freddie Freeman's sacrifice fly and Tucker's RBI double boosted the lead in the second, and the Dodgers opened a 7-0 lead in the fourth on Max Muncy's two-run double and Josue De Paula's RBI single.
Dodger left-hander Justin Wrobleski, making his 22nd start this season and first since Sept. 6, did not allow a baserunner in three innings while striking out three.
Wrobleski and Blake Treinen combined to retire their first 11 batters before Sal Stewart's 32nd homer.
Landon Knack (1-0) allowed four hits over four scoreless innings for his first big league win since May 31 last year.
Miguel Rojas homered off Brandon Williamson in the ninth.
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said reliever Edwin Díaz (neck inflammation) finished his minor league injury rehabilitation assignment and will be activated this weekend.
Dodgers: RHP Tyler Glasnow (4-1, 3.50) starts Friday against San Francisco, who send LHP Cesar Perdomo (0-1, 3.68) to the mound,
Reds: RHP Chase Burns (15-3, 2.80) starts Friday against the Chicago Cubs.
___

item.content:encoded:
On Thursday afternoon, the Los Angeles Dodgers will finish their series with the Cincinnati Reds in Ohio.
They have won two out of the first three games, so they will look to take the series.
Most recently, the Dodgers lost by a score of 6-2 on Wednesday night.
Josue De Paula was not in the lineup.
That said, he had one walk off the bench.
Los Angeles Dodgers Make De Paula Change
For Thursday’s game, the Dodgers have announced their starting lineup.
Underdog MLB wrote: “Dodgers 9/17 T. Edman CF F. Freeman 1B K. Tucker RF T. Hernández LF M. Muncy 3B J. De Paula DH H. Feduccia C A. Freeland 2B M. Rojas SS J. Wrobleski SP”
De Paula is back in the lineup (and hitting 6th) on Thursday.
The 21-year-old rookie is batting .143 with two hits, one home run, three RBIs, two runs and one stolen base in his first six games at the MLB level.
He made his debut earlier this month.
The Dodgers wrote (via X) on September 11: “The Dodgers have selected the contract of OF Josue De Paula and placed designated hitter/pitcher Shohei Ohtani on the injured list with right biceps inflammation, backdated to 9/8. In order to make room on the 40-man roster, the Dodgers moved LHP Eric Lauer to the 60-day injured list.”
Looking At The Dodgers Right Now
The Dodgers come into the day as the top team in the National League West with a 92-60 record in 152 games.
They have won seven out of their last ten games (and are 45-32 in 77 games on the road).
Following the Reds, the Dodgers will return home to host the San Francisco Giants on Friday night.
Looking At The Reds Right Now
The Reds have had a tough 2026 season.
They are at the bottom of the National League Central with a 71-81 record in 152 games.
At home, the Reds have gone 37-40 in 77 games.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers brought third baseman Max Muncy and outfielder Josue De Paula back into the lineup for Thursday’s series finale against the Cincinnati Reds.
The Dodgers lost Wednesday’s game after Cy Young winner Blake Snell went down with a groin injury after pitching just one inning. Luckily, Snell believes he can still make a start before the end of the regular season, which ends in less than two weeks.
LA won the first two games of the series, shutting down a powerful Reds lineup, and will look to do the same to win the series Wednesday.
Who is Starting for the Dodgers?
Justin Wrobleski will start for the Dodgers on Wednesday, making his 25th appearance of the regular season. Two of his last three appearances have come out of the bullpen, and none of them have lasted more than three innings since his return from the injured list with a forearm problem.
He has a 3.78 ERA on the year, striking out 111 batters over the course of 133.1 innings—his heaviest workload in an MLB season so far.
How deep into the game he goes depends on him, but the Dodgers will have backup in the form of Landon Knack whenever Wrobleski is ready to come out.
Who is in the Dodgers’ Lineup?
The Dodgers still don’t have Shohei Ohtani in the lineup, but Tommy Edman has replaced him well and will play center field on Thursday. Freddie Freeman moves up a couple of spots into the No. 2 hole, followed by right fielder Kyle Tucker, who will bat third.
Left fielder Teoscar Hernandez takes over the cleanup spot, followed by Muncy, who slides back into third base and bats fifth. De Paula serves as the designated hitter and will bat sixth, with catcher Hunter Feduccia giving Will Smith an off day in the No. 7 spot.
Second baseman Alex Freeland will bat eight for the Dodgers, with Miguel Rojas rounding out the lineup and playing shortstop—giving Mookie Betts a well-deserved rest day.
Dodgers Lineup vs. Reds
1. Tommy Edman, CF
2. Freddie Freeman, 1B
3. Kyle Tucker, RF
4. Teoscar Hernandez, LF
5. Max Muncy, 3B
6. Josue De Paula, DH
7. Hunter Feduccia, C
8. Alex Freeland, 2B
9. Miguel Rojas, SS
P. Justin Wrobleski, LHP
Who is Starting for the Reds?
Veteran right-hander Brady Singer is starting for the Reds, making his 30th appearance of the season. He has reached that mark in each of the last three seasons, and has 25 or more appearances in all seven of his MLB campaigns bar 2020.
He isn’t having the best year despite his regular consistency, though, as he has a 5.38 ERA through 150.2 innings with only 125 strikeouts on the season.
Singer didn’t face the Dodgers in last week’s series in Los Angeles, but he has a pretty good track record against the team. In three appearances against LA, all of which came during his time with Kansas City, he has a 1.89 ERA through 19 innings with 15 strikeouts.
The Dodgers will hope to break that trend on Thursday as they look to bring themselves even closer to a first-round postseason bye. The first pitch of Thursday’s game comes at 9:40 p.m. PT.

item.title: [FanSided] Ranking the most important Dodgers who could come back for the MLB Playoffs
item.dc:creator: Christopher Kline
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are on track to win the NL West and probably earn a first-round bye in the postseason. That comes despite a recent onslaught of injuries. Los Angeles is not unaccustomed to a stacked injury list, but the Dodgers' elite depth — aided by a top-ranked farm system and unrivalred spending power — makes them uniquely resilient. What has helped L.A. win back-to-back World Series titles, however, is their knack for getting healthy at the right time and charging into October at fu
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are on track to win the NL West and probably earn a first-round bye in the postseason. That comes despite a recent onslaught of injuries. Los Angeles is not unaccustomed to a stacked injury list, but the Dodgers' elite depth — aided by a top-ranked farm system and unrivalred spending power — makes them uniquely resilient.
What has helped L.A. win back-to-back World Series titles, however, is their knack for getting healthy at the right time and charging into October at full strength. The Dodgers are hoping to do just that, again. Let's rank six potential returners who could make an outsized impact.
6. RHP Edwin Díaz
Should Edwin Díaz actually come back for the playoffs? He got rocked in his recent Triple-A rehab appearance. The Dodgers' prized $69 million investment has only pitched 13.2 innings in the majors this season, with a disastrous 11.85 ERA (not a typo). Díaz has not looked right at any point.
While the Dodgers presumably want such an expensive and accomplished reliever on the postseason roster, it may be smarter to punt on this season entirely. Díaz is more than capable of rebuilding confidence and getting healthy in the offseason, but it's unclear if L.A. can rely on him in even the lowest-leverage spots currently. Rather than playing with fire, so to speak, the Dodgers should probably lean on their spectacular bullpen depth and keep Díaz on the sidelines. The risk far outweighs the potential reward of rushing him back.
That said, when healthy, Díaz has a long track record as one of MLB's best closers. We know he can electify in the late innings. If the Dodgers are confident for reasons we on the outside aren't privy too, never say never on a triumphant turnaround.
5. RHP Roki Sasaki
Through two seasons, the Rōki Sasaki experience has not quite lived up to expectations for Dodgers fans. Hailed as the best Japanese pitching prospect in a generation, the 24-year-old looks an awful lot like... a prospect. A work in progress. Los Angeles expected immediate results. Now, the Dodgers are hoping Sasaki can iron out command issues against MLB competition. He appeared briefly in the minors this season, but the Dodgers are effectively all-in on Sasaki as a major league pitcher.
Sasaki is expected to recover from a blister before the playoffs, although the Dodgers are uncertain about his exact role. The rotation is much too deep for Sasaki to start in a must-win environment. He was effectively L.A.'s closer last October — a role in which he thrived — but a healthy Tanner Scott removes Sasaki from consideration for that role. Expect him in the bullpen, probably handling bulk work if one of L.A.'s starters is forced out early.
4. C Dalton Rushing
Dalton Rushing was recently returned to the IL after suffering a setback in his recovery from UCL surgery. He's done catching for the season, but L.A. still hopes the 25-year-old can return as a hitter. Of course, if Rushing is effectively relegated to DH, it will be hard to get him in the lineup with Shohei Ohtani also on the roster. Rushing could end up as a situational, pinch-hitter type in October, if he's even on the roster.
It's a credit to how deep the Dodgers are that Rushing being "situational," rather than essential, is even in the cards. The rookie backstop cooled off after the All-Star break, but he's still phenomenally talented. He has a .798 OPS and 120 wRC+ as a rookie, with 12 home runs in only 250 at-bats.
Rushing is stuck behind Will Smith on the org chart, which complicates his future somewhat, but the Dodgers will find ways to use him if he's available.
3. RHP Edgardo Henriquez
The Dodgers hope Edgardo Henriquez can return from a low-grade back strain come the playoffs. The 24-year-old fireballer has quickly established himself as one of baseball's most dominant relievers. He has a 2.85 ERA and 1.03 WHIP with 71 strikeouts in 60.0 innings pitched this season; he ranks in MLB's 99th percentile for both hard-hit rate (27.1 percent) and average fastball velo (100.8 mph).
Henriquez is more than a hard-thrower. He misses barrels and limits explosive hits, able to force groundballs or lifeless bloopers just as often as he forces swing-and-miss. He leans heavily on his four-seam and sinker combo, with a sweeping slider that leaves opposing hitters gasping for air (.191 xwOBA). Should Henriquez return in time, the Dodgers can plug him right into high-leverage spots and expect results. He's the real deal, folks.
2. OF Andy Pages
Andy Pages is back in the batting cage after breaking his hand in mid-August. The Dodgers' centerfielder has enjoyed a proper breakout campaign, posting a .797 OPS and 119 wRC+ with elite defensive metrics and 12 stolen bases. In terms of fWAR, or wins above replacement, Pages ranks third among L.A. positional players (3.9), behind only Shohei Ohtani (6.8) and Max Muncy (4.0).
The Dodgers really need Pages on cleanup duty in centerfield. He covers so much ground and features a killer arm, which wipes runs off the board. Pages' bat cooled down before the injury, but he's still far more dangerous than L.A.'s alternatives — although the recent promotion of top prospect Josue De Paula does create a difficult decision for manager Dave Roberts, assuming the DH spot reverts back to Ohtani.
Speaking of which...
1. DH Shohei Ohtani
This was obvious, yeah? Shohei Ohtani is currently on ice as he attempts to shed bicep and knee problems. That said, the Dodgers plan to get him back before the regular season ends — and it would be absolutely shocking if Ohtani weren't leading off in Game 1 of the Dodgers' first postseason series.
The nagging nature of Ohtani's injuries mean he won't take the mound again in 2026, but he's still the most valuable hitter in the majors, on balance. Yes, Yordan Álvarez and Pete Crow-Armstrong are enjoying better seasons, but Ohtani is the man you want at the plate in a big spot. Drafting a fantasy team, he's your No. 1 pick. So on and so forth.
After spending the early portion of his MLB career on an unserious Angels team, Ohtani is two-for-two in the World Series since joining the Dodgers. He has consistently come up large in the playoffs. Assuming Ohtani is anywhere close to 100 percent, the Dodgers are once again (easy) favorites to win it all.

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers star Kyle Tucker may be getting hot just in time for the playoffs.
The National League West-leading Dodgers (90-57) will look to extend their winning streak to nine games when they visit the Miami Marlins (72-76) on Saturday. The Marlins, in turn, have lost seven of their past eight games.
Tucker went 3-for-3 with a season-high five RBIs in Los Angeles’ 6-2 victory over Miami on Friday. He fell a double short of the cycle.
Entering Friday, Tucker was on pace for his fourth straight month with an OPS at or below .700, and that’s not what the Dodgers thought they were getting when they signed him to a four-year, $240 million contract in January.
Tucker, who has posted OPS numbers of .993 and .841 over the past two years, impressed Marlins manager Clayton McCullough with his performance on Friday.
“Independent of how this season has gone, (Tucker) is still a terrific hitter,” McCullough said. “He handles lefties well. He got a hanging breaking ball and turned the game for them.”
Tucker produced five straight seasons with more than 20 homers before mustering just 14 in 2026. But if he can finish strong, that will help a Dodgers squad that is missing injured sluggers Shohei Ohtani (right biceps inflammation), Freddie Freeman (right knee) and Andy Pages (left hand). Those three players have hit a combined 67 homers this season.
Los Angeles also saw Josue De Paula make his MLB debut on Friday. De Paula went 0-for-3 with a walk after tearing up Double-A pitching.
“We want to get him some major-league at-bats to see what it looks like,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said.
The Dodgers will turn to right-hander Tyler Glasnow (4-0, 3.12 ERA) to make the start on Saturday.
His per-nine-innings averages are outstanding in terms of hits allowed (5.3), walks (2.7) and strikeouts (10.9). The Dodgers are 8-2 when he starts, and this will be his fourth start since coming back from a near-three-month injury absence.
Glasnow is 1-1 with a 3.86 ERA in five career starts versus the Marlins.
Miami will counter with right-hander Tyler Phillips (5-6, 3.51), who is 1-0 with a 6.94 ERA in six career appearances (one start) against the Dodgers.
For his career overall, Phillips has a sterling 2.49 ERA in 71 relief appearances, but a 5.13 ERA in 25 career starts.
As for Miami’s offense, the Marlins are hoping that shortstop Otto Lopez is back on track after a 4-for-5 performance on Friday.
This year, Lopez hit .322 in March/April; .339 in May; and .340 in June. That hot start made him a first-time All-Star. However, he batted .284 in July and just .236 in August.
Thanks to Friday’s big game, he is now hitting .342 in September.
“After the phenomenal first half, he struggled for a bit,” McCullough said. “He looks to be back in a good spot, hitting the ball to all fields. It’s something we have grown accustomed to, and it bodes well for us to have him get hits in bunches.”
–Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
Despite dour predictions from some insiders, Los Angeles Dodgers superstar Shohei Ohtani might be back in action for the Boys in Blue sooner rather than later.
Ohtani hit off a tee on Tuesday in his bid to return from knee, arm and neck pain, issues that led to a very uncharacteristic slump in the weeks before he was placed on the injured list.
Having already been shut down as a pitcher, Ohtani has also been sidelined as a hitter, though that may not be for too much longer.
Dave Roberts shares expectations for Ohtani’s return
On Tuesday, manager Dave Roberts said Ohtani “felt good” after hitting off the tee.
“I don’t know what’s in store for tomorrow, but I know there’s going to be a consistent buildup. Don’t know when the time of return to play is, but today was positive and hopefully, we can just keep building towards that,” he said.
When asked if he expects Ohtani back during the regular season, Roberts answered with a definitive “I do.”
View this post on Instagram
“Whether it happens or not is to be determined, but I do expect him to be back to play in some regular season games,” he said. “Don’t know how many though.”
Roberts’ prediction flies in the face of at least one Dodgers insider, who predicted that the Japanese superstar was out for the rest of 2026.
The saga has also raised questions about whether Ohtani was honest with the team about his injuries, and whether the team perhaps mismanaged their superstar.
Many of those questions will only be answered with time, though if Ohtani does indeed come back this year and looks more like his old self, the criticism will likely be much quieter.
What would Shohei Ohtani’s return mean for the Dodgers?
While Ohtani’s absence hasn’t impacted the Dodgers too much this month, that could be because the Boys in Blue have one of the easier September scheduled in the National League.
In October, though, the playoffs are on, and the quality of opponent will be much higher.
Some of those likely opponents, such as the Atlanta Braves, have recently given the Dodgers fits, and a healthier Ohtani returning to the batting order would almost assuredly improve the Dodgers’ chances of winning a third straight World Series.
Ohtani’s replacement, the much-hyped prospect Josue De Paula, has flashed moments of brilliance in his first few games in the big leagues, but getting back perhaps the best baseball player ever would be a huge boost for the Dodgers, especially from a mental perspective.
Do you think Shohei Ohtani will be back this year and, if so, will it be before the playoffs begin?

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Dodgers History: Josue De Paula's 2027 RoY campaign would put him in legendary company

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers may have spoiled Josue De Paula's breakout game, but his monster home run against the Miami Marlins on Sunday sent a message: this kid may live up to his billing as LA's No. 1 prospect.
The Dodgers still have to figure out how they're going to fit him on the roster when Shohei Ohtani comes off the IL, but as long as his brief audition at the tail end of this season continues to go well, that should be a priority this offseason.
Maybe we're getting way ahead of ourselves here, but if the Dodgers figure out how to get him regular at-bats in 2027, we could be looking at the next in a long and storied line of Dodgers Rookie of the Year Award-winners.
The Dodgers have an MLB-leading 18, beginning, of course, with Jackie Robinson in 1947, the man the award is named after. Their latest winner was Cody Bellinger in 2017.
Sandwiched in between are franchise legends Jim Gilliam, Fernando Valenzuela, Eric Karros, and Hideo Nomo, just to name a few. De Paula could find himself in some very good company by the end of 2027.
Putting Josue De Paula's future Rookie of the Year campaign into context with other Dodgers greats
De Paula has been compared heavily to Yordan Alvarez, probably Andrew Friedman's greatest trade regret as the Dodgers' chief executive. Of the 12 position player Rookies of the Year the Dodgers have produced, none are quite the same archetype as Alvarez — David Ortiz, Kyle Schwarber-esque players who can flat-out hit.
But perhaps the most apt comparison is Mike Piazza, LA's winner in 1993. Piazza came into the league with far fewer expectations attached than De Paula, but both are defensively weaker position players with massive power potential and advanced plate discipline. De Paula has yet to strike out in the four games he's appeared in.
It would be unfair to expect the same kind of offensive production from De Paula that Piazza offered up in his rookie season, when he hit .318 with a .932 OPS, 35 homers, and 112 RBI to kick off what would become a Hall of Fame career.
But when the Dodgers, who are usually so enthused about their prospects, were all but champing at the bit to find him a place to play this season, that says a lot as to where they think his ceiling could be.

item.content:encoded:
Max Muncy is out of the Los Angeles Dodgers lineup for Wednesday's game against the Cincinnati Reds, and the move didn't come as a surprise. Dave Roberts already said as much a day earlier.
The Dodgers manager told reporters Tuesday night that Muncy, infielder Alex Freeland, and outfielder Josue De Paula weren't expected to start Wednesday, according to DodgerBlue on X.com.
The reasoning behind the move is that Andrew Abbott is scheduled to start for the Reds, a lefty with a 6-11 record and a 4.78 ERA this season. All three batters are left-handed hitters who have struggled against left-handed pitching.
We will probably have to remind everyone tomorrow, but Dave Roberts already said Max Muncy, Alex Freeland and Josue De Paula aren’t expected to be in the lineup.
— Dodger Blue (@DodgerBlue1958) September 16, 2026
Muncy has hit .222 against left-handed pitching over his career, compared to .235 against right-handers. Ironically, this season, Muncy has hit better against pitching from the left side, batting .257 with six home runs and 15 RBIs versus .249 with 22 homers and 56 RBIs against the right side.
Those numbers have shaped how Roberts has deployed Muncy late in games and against certain matchups. The 36-year-old is in the middle of a bounce-back year that included his third career All-Star selection, his first since 2021.
The Dodgers enter Wednesday's game with a 92-59 record and a 10-game lead over the San Diego Padres in the National League West, needing just one more win or a Padres loss to clinch the division. The Dodgers have already locked up a playoff berth for the 14th straight season, tying the major league record with the Atlanta Braves.
While the Dodgers will be without left-handed bats, Roberts will lean on left-hander Blake Snell on the mound, giving the Dodgers the best possible matchup to attack Abbott without their top left-handed bats.
The Greatest Dodgers of All-Time

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers designated outfielder Ryan Ward for assignment ahead of Wednesday’s game, ending his seven-year stay in the Dodgers’ organization.
To replace Ward on the 40-man roster, the Dodgers reinstated trade deadline acquisition Kris Bubic from the 60-day injured list while optioning right-hander Paul Gervase to Triple-A.
Ward, 28, made his MLB debut with the Dodgers this season, but his time in the organization goes well beyond the 20 games he played for the team this season.
He begun making headlines during the 2025 season for his unbelievable performances in Triple-A, with many calling for him to replace outfielder Michael Conforto, who struggled during his one-year tenure in Los Angeles.
Ward won the Pacific Coast League MVP in 2025, hitting 36 homers and driving in 122 runs over the course of 143 games, posting a career-high .937 OPS. He hadn’t appeared in MLB since June prior to his DFA.
Why Did the Dodgers Choose to DFA Ward Over a Pitcher?
While the Dodgers have plenty of pitchers on their 40-man roster, especially some who haven’t performed up to MLB standards this season, so why DFA Ward?
The decision likely comes due to Ward’s positional redundancy. A left-handed outfielder, which the Dodgers have plenty of—especially after calling up Josue De Paula directly from Double-A last week.
The Dodgers view De Paula as the future and already have him in MLB, which effectively put the nail in the coffin for Ward’s time with the Dodgers.
De Paula, the Dodgers’ top prospect, only has five MLB games under his belt, but is turning heads across the league already. He has a homer and three RBIs to go with five walks and a .797 OPS across his five appearances.
How Did Ryan Ward Perform in the Majors?
Ward had a decent year in the majors for the Dodgers, but not quite up to his standards in Triple-A. Through his 20 games, he stepped up to the plate 60 times and posted a .738 OPS.
He hit three homers over the course of those games, driving in 12 runs, though his OPS sat below .300 for all of the final 12 games with the Dodgers.
The 28-year-old got off to a good start with the Dodgers when they called him up for two games in April, logging two hits in his debut and driving in his first MLB RBI.
He came back at the end of May, hitting his first career home run against the Philadelphia Phillies, the. crushed another one against the Los Angeles Angels a few days later. Ward rode a five-game hit streak from June 4-10, but struggled to put up results for the remainder of the year. He logged just four hits over the following 11 games.
Ward returned to the minors at the end of June and had a decent couple of months, but a September slump may have cost him his spot on the 40-man roster. Since Sept. 1, Ward had a .191 batting average with a .565 OPS, hitting just one home run in a hitter-friendly league.
LA can still keep Ward if he clears waivers, but the probability of teams passing on a player with his track record is extremely low.

item.content:encoded:
De Paula is not in the lineup for Wednesday's game in Cincinnati.
De Paula made five straight starts upon his promotion to the big leagues, but the left-handed hitter will get a breather as the Reds hand the ball to southpaw Andrew Abbott. Alex Call is grabbing a start in De Paula's place, as Call will play left field while Teoscar Hernandez gets a designated hitter day.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are looking to win their series against the Cincinnati Reds on Wednesday.
The Dodgers took Monday's series opener, 4-1, behind seven shutout innings from Tarik Skubal. Then, they won Tuesday's game, 4-0, behind seven shutout innings from Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
On Wednesday, LA has another superstar pitcher on the mound in left-hander Blake Snell.
“When you’re writing in the lineup and you see those guys, and one trying to up the other guy, and then now you got Snell going [Wednesday] — you feel good about preventing runs,” manager Dave Roberts said.
“A team like the Reds right now, where they’re scuffling a little bit, it’s daunting when you see a starter like those guys that we’re running out there.”
Dodgers vs Reds Pitching Matchup on Wednesday
Snell is looking to continue his run of dominance since returning from midseason elbow surgery.
The left-hander has gone 4-0 with a 1.04 ERA across six starts, striking out 46 while allowing zero home runs over 34.2 innings of work.
Snell, who pitched 5.2 innings in his most recent start, is still looking to go deeper into games moving forward. He hasn't pitched more than six innings in any of his six starts.
“I mean the goal, at worst is definitely six for me,” Snell said. “I also know that I can go seven, eight, nine. I know I’m able to do it. So for me not to, I just have to get more efficient early in the game. I feel like once I get past the first couple innings, I start cruising and start figuring it out."
Opposite Snell will be left-hander Andrew Abbott, who's 6-11 with a 4.78 ERA and 120 strikeouts over 154.1 innings this season.
He's allowed seven earned runs in two of his last three starts, and has a 7.71 ERA since the start of August.
Dodgers Starting Lineup
- Tommy Edman, CF
- Mookie Betts, SS
- Will Smith, C
- Freddie Freeman, 1B
- Teoscar Hernández, DH
- Miguel Rojas, 2B
- Kyle Tucker, RF
- Kiké Hernández, 3B
- Alex Call, LF
Josue De Paula, Max Muncy and Alex Freeland are out of the lineup with the left-handed pitcher on the mound.
How to Watch Dodgers vs Reds on Wednesday
First pitch for Los Angeles Dodgers vs. Cincinnati Reds on Wednesday, Sept. 16 is 3:40 p.m. PT/6:40 p.m. ET.
The game will be broadcast on SportsNet LA and in the MLB app.
The game will be broadcast on the radio on AM570 (in English) and KTNQ 1020 AM (in Spanish).

He was born and raised in Los Angeles and has extensively covered Southern California sports in his career. The New York Mets star called De Paula "el loco mio" on his story as MLB compared the 21-year-old's stance to Soto's. item.content:encoded:
Josue De Paula received a huge shoutout from one of baseball's biggest stars.
Juan Soto posted a clip of De Paula on his Instagram story, where the Dodgers top prospect was in the midst of working his fifth walk in just four major league games. The New York Mets star called De Paula "el loco mio" on his story as MLB compared the 21-year-old's stance to Soto's.
De Paula and Soto both attended "El Niche" baseball academy in the Dominican Republic. Soto, who had a chance to sign with the Dodgers ahead of the 2025 season, has evidently not lost love for his fellow countryman and budding star.
As for whether De Paula was trying to copy the Soto Shuffle, the Dodgers outfielder explained what was going through his head during that at-bat.
"I wasn't exactly trying to emulate it. It was more just me being so locked in and getting into my legs," he told the California Post Tuesday. "But I can understand how it looks like a Soto shuffle. And if people think it looks like that, hey, I'm not mad at it."
De Paula and Soto have developed a relationship as the pair share representation with Boras Coporation. It appears the former has begun his own version of the Soto Shuffle.
The Dodgers promoted De Paula from Double-A last week to fill in for the injured Shohei Ohtani. Despite being the youngest player in the lineup, De Paula exudes confidence and power when he steps in the batter's box.
Moreover, the De Paula's plate discipline is a rarity for young players. Yet, entering Tuesday night's game he had managed to avoid striking out.
Who else does that remind you of?
Soto.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Freddie Freeman Changes Swing as Dodgers Star Battles Knee Pain, Struggles

Things looked shaky for Freeman, who has built a reputation as one of baseball’s most consistent players. However, he put together his best game in weeks, going 3-for-5 on singles, but showing the elite bat-to-ball sk
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers first baseman Freddie Freeman has been battling right knee pain, but the worst of it may be behind the team’s contact specialist.
Entering Tuesday’s game, Freeman was on a 3-for-30 cold streak and had missed three of the last six games because of his knee issue.
Things looked shaky for Freeman, who has built a reputation as one of baseball’s most consistent players.
However, he put together his best game in weeks, going 3-for-5 on singles, but showing the elite bat-to-ball skills that make him a candidate to bat around .300 year in, year out.
After the game, manager Dave Roberts noted that Freeman looked more like himself.
“It looked good,” Roberts said. “It looked more like Freddie.”
Freeman had asked Roberts before the game, jokingly, if he could play on Wednesday, a scheduled day off, if he got three hits.
As a result of Freeman’s performance, the manager is allowing Freeman to skip an off-day on Wednesday and play again, with the infielder eager to get the ball rolling.
“I feel like my faults are I try to hit the ball to the opposite field too much, and I let the ball get too deep,” he said.
“So today was [get the] foot down early, catch the ball out front a little bit, and it kind of worked. I wasn’t squaring the ball up in the game, but I’ll take those three hits and keep that work going tomorrow, and hopefully we’ll get hot.”
What does Freeman’s uptick mean for the Dodgers?
With the best rotation in baseball, the Dodgers are left scrounging around for offense any way that they can find it.
Teoscar Hernandez, Josue De Paula, and Mookie Betts have been the most consistent sources, with Max Muncy and Will Smith in the picture as well.
Still, the Dodgers need as many players in a spot as possible to deliver timely hits, and Freeman’s experience and skills make him a clear-cut candidate to step up.
To deliver results quickly, as he manages his knee and struggles, Freeman has made a mechanical change, getting out in front of the ball to catch it earlier on his bat.
The result may be less clean contact and hard hits, but more consistent contact, with the idea that it makes him valuable come the postseason.
“I’m not trying to find something that’s sustainable,” he said. “I’m trying to find something that works for four weeks.”
Freeman has the right approach to deliver just what the Dodgers need. The entire offense does not need to be excellent; simply being good enough will lead to a three-peat.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers' Dave Roberts Says Josue De Paula Needs to Be Better in One Key Area

item.content:encoded:
When the Los Angeles Dodgers promoted Josue De Paula to the majors last week, they did so in full knowledge that the 21-year-old had more errors (eight) than assists (six) as a Double-A outfielder.
After playing 58 games in left field and 37 in right field for the Tulsa Drillers, De Paula has spent all but five innings at designated hitter during his first five days in the majors. When he caught the only fly ball hit in his direction over five innings Sunday in Miami, De Paula and the Dodgers could exhale. He got the first one out of the way.
It will be difficult for manager Dave Roberts to take De Paula out of the lineup once Shohei Ohtani returns from the injured list if he continues to reach base at such a high clip.
Yet it will be easier to keep De Paula in the lineup if he can play a corner outfield position. To that end, Roberts is hopeful the rookie can become a better defensive outfielder in short order.
"I just think that — just being candid — I don’t think that he’s valued it as much as he will," Roberts said, via Bill Plunkett of the Orange County Register. "And it just has to be important. Certainly, when you get to the big leagues, outs are important, converting outs are important.
“I think that he’s a young player. I mean, he’s 21 years old. His bat has certainly got him here, but it’s our job to make him value defense and get him to be a better defender.”
Besides their mandate to make De Paula a more complete baseball player, the Dodgers have another pressing reason to get the rookie comfortable in the outfield.
If Ohtani and Dalton Rushing are able to return from the injured list prior to October, they can only occupy the roster as designated hitters or pinch hitters. That's a limiting factor in the postseason, when teams can only carry 26 active players in each round.
De Paula gives the Dodgers three left-handed hitting DHs — impractical at best, impossible at worst — unless he can play the outfield.
"He and Dino [Ebel, the Dodgers' outfielders coach] are committed to a routine, which I love,” Roberts said. “I think the other important thing is just so he can see how the quality and how intense the work is up here. And I think that you really don’t know until you know, and I’m excited for him to watch our guys, how they prepare each night.”
Sign up for our free newsletter and follow us on X/Twitter and Facebook for the latest news.
J.P. Hoornstra is an On SI Contributor. A veteran of 20 years of sports coverage for daily newspapers in California, J.P. covered MLB, the Los Angeles Dodgers, and the Los Angeles Angels (occasionally of Anaheim) from 2012-23 for the Southern California News Group. His first book, The 50 Greatest Dodgers Games of All-Time, published in 2015. In 2016, he won an Associated Press Sports Editors award for breaking news coverage. He once recorded a keyboard solo on the same album as two of the original Doors.

item.title: [The New York Times] ‘I just want to feel saucy’: Inside Josue De Paula’s fearless Dodgers debut
item.dc:creator: Fabian Ardaya
item.description: CINCINNATI — Josue De Paula is in his element in the batter’s box. item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI — Josue De Paula is in his element in the batter’s box. He carries himself like a guy who knows his importance to the Los Angeles Dodgers depends on how well he can command himself within those 24 square feet of chalk lines. De Paula asserts himself with a confident shake of the head after each pitch outside the strike zone.
Advertisement
Some head shakes are more exaggerated than others. Each demonstrates the same message: De Paula is not going to give in.
“I just want to feel saucy when I’m up there, you know what I’m saying?” De Paula told The Athletic this week. “I feel like I’m in control, not you. … I want my pitch. Come in the zone. Let’s go.”
This is who De Paula wants to be. He describes hitting as “aggressive patience,” an approach that puts him on the attack.
“It’s almost like a war for me in my head,” De Paula said. “I look confident. I look saucy. I feel saucy when I’m in the box, so it’s like, ‘Hey bro, let’s keep it rocking.’”
It took four games for De Paula to inspire fascination within the Dodgers dynasty, where his every at-bat feels like a must-watch example of how to command a zone. Of the first 37 big-league pitches De Paula saw outside of the strike zone, he swung at just five. He made it 17 plate appearances without striking out before going down swinging in the seventh inning and looking in the ninth in the Dodgers’ 4-0 win over the Reds on Tuesday. De Paula does not seem fazed that he is just 2 for 14 (.143) since being called up, including five hitless at-bats in his first game in the leadoff spot.
That’s because he believes in his process. A day earlier, De Paula battled back from down in the count against Reds lefty Nick Lodolo, a former All-Star. The left-handed batter took a 2-2 fastball just below the knees, crouched and shook his head. A pitch later, De Paula walked for the fifth time in his short career.
The clip of the head shake drew a chuckle from the proprietor of the “Soto Shuffle” himself, Juan Soto, who, like De Paula, once honed his craft at the El Niche Baseball Academy in the Dominican city of Santo Domingo.
Josue De Paula live reaction to you trying to get him to chase. https://t.co/CrmRSnDVgO pic.twitter.com/dbXGz8WYL0
— Chad Moriyama (@ChadMoriyama) September 14, 2026
“El loco mío,” Soto shared to his Instagram story in Spanish, stamping his approval with a laughing emoji. My guy.
Advertisement
“I swear I wasn’t trying to do like the whole thing,” De Paula said with a laugh. “I just got into my legs, and I was shaking my head … but I’m not mad. That’s not a bad player to look like.”
De Paula, 21, feels like an injection of youthful exuberance for baseball’s oldest lineup. The Brooklyn-born son of a Dominican father (and relative of NBA veterans Stephon Marbury and Sebastian Telfair) speaks with a thick New York accent and oozes the confidence of a player who carries that swagger into the box.
De Paula is the crown jewel of a Dodgers farm system that is expected to prolong this run of excellence. Last week, he became the first position player ever to be called up directly from Double A by this Andrew Friedman-led front office group.
De Paula is here because he can hit, has always hit, and the Dodgers need him to hit. De Paula is here to serve as the Dodgers’ designated hitter, at least until Shohei Ohtani returns from the injured list. No one with the Dodgers, however, is ruling out the possibility that De Paula could help them in October as they seek a third consecutive World Series title.
“I hope he makes our decision hard,” manager Dave Roberts said.
Through De Paula’s torrid run through the Dodgers’ farm system, officials raved about his keen ability to pick up the baseball, make proper swing decisions and recognize spin.
“He doesn’t give away any pitches, which I love, let alone give away any at-bats,” Roberts said.
Pair that with a preternatural ability to make contact, and De Paula entered this season as one of the highly-regarded young hitters in the league. The Dodgers implemented a change to De Paula’s swing this year, lowering his hands and opening up his resulting bat path to keep the barrel in the zone longer. That has allowed him to access more power by pulling more fly balls and has made him a lethal producer at Double A.
Advertisement
De Paula slugged 27 home runs this season in Double A, more than double what he had in any of his first four professional seasons. His first hit Sunday in Miami was a mammoth upper-deck shot to right field on the kind of awe-inspiring swing that has come much more easily for De Paula than in years past.
“When all those things are kind of clicking, it’s tough for any pitcher to compete with,” hitting coach Robert Van Scoyoc said. “So it’s been very impressive so far.”
De Paula became a Dodger partially as a byproduct of the COVID-19 pandemic, which shut down the New York baseball season and prompted De Paula’s father, Josue Sr., to send him to the Dominican Republic to work at El Niche under Cristian “Niche” Batista.
“It was like stepping into a whole other world,” De Paula said.
It was there, during an offseason workout, that De Paula met Soto, who broke into the big leagues at 19 years old with the kind of swaggering command of the batter’s box that De Paula hopes to replicate. Rather than enter the amateur draft, De Paula signed directly with the Dodgers as an international amateur for a bonus of just under $400,000. De Paula estimated that, in one of his two tryouts with the organization and with several of the club’s brass in attendance, he collected nine hits in 10 at-bats.
“I killed,” De Paula said, reliving the memory as if it just happened.
He has hit ever since, ascending to the top of prospect lists. His list of star-studded admirers grew, too. After accompanying Soto in being represented by super agent Scott Boras, De Paula was asked by Boras to name some of his favorite players. De Paula selected Elly De La Cruz, who at that time was set for his first season as a breakout star for the Cincinnati Reds but was already dominating the minor leagues. Boras invited De Paula to his Newport Beach offices in Southern California after that and surprised him by bringing De La Cruz.
Advertisement
The two have remained close, working out together in the Miami area in the winters. Friday, just before he made his major-league debut against the Marlins in Miami, De Paula called De La Cruz on FaceTime. When they met up again this week in Cincinnati, they posed for a picture.
“I’m really happy for what he’s doing,” De La Cruz said.
De Paula sees a kinship between De La Cruz and Soto.
“We’re all killers,” De Paula said with a knowing smirk.
When De Paula spent his first spring training in big-league camp with the Dodgers in 2025, he quickly heard from Mookie Betts. The former Gold Glove right fielder wanted to make De Paula and fellow newcomers Zyhir Hope and Justin Dean feel welcome, so over dinner at a Phoenix-area soul food restaurant, he talked shop. When De Paula went out for early defensive work in the outfield this week, he had Roberts and Betts at different points offer some advice.
Now in a clubhouse filled with stars, De Paula said he feels at home. Whether he stays there heading into October will depend on how the rest of the regular season goes. The first few games have left a strong first impression.
“It’s a slow heartbeat,” Van Scoyoc said. “He’s not overwhelmed at all. It seemed like he picked up where he left off in Double A. … I wouldn’t say it’s surprising, but it’s just nice to see.”
Ohtani is expected to return from his nagging biceps and knee injuries by year’s end. De Paula has a lack of defensive utility at this point. While he did play in left field on Sunday, the Dodgers still want to work on getting De Paula to “value” the defensive side of the ball first, Roberts said. That means his path to the Dodgers’ postseason roster will likely be as a left-handed bat off the bench, essentially the role the club envisioned for Dalton Rushing before his most recent IL stint.
Advertisement
That decision is still up in the air, Roberts said. There will be “growing pains,” as Roberts said after Tuesday’s performance. The manager said he “didn’t love” the quality of De Paula’s at-bats. But October is a scenario De Paula feels he will be ready for.
“Especially in big moments, I feel like my mind just goes to a whole ‘nother level,” De Paula said. “Especially competing. The bigger the moment is … it’s like the more my mind hyper-focuses. So when I’m hyper-focused like that a lot, it’s dangerous.”

item.title: [True Blue LA] Dodgers notes: Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Teoscar Hernández, Shohei Ohtani
item.dc:creator: Jacob Macofsky
item.description: The Dodgers’ winning ways in September were briefly interrupted for two games against the Miami Marlins, but they have picked back up against the Cincinnati Reds, taking the first two games of a four-game set. After Tarik Skubal shut down Cincinnati over seven innings on Monday, Yoshinobu Yamamoto continued the trend of marvelous results from the rotation with a seven-inning scoreless gem on Tuesday, working through a pair of lead-off walks while allowing just one hit while striking out seven. Y
item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers’ winning ways in September were briefly interrupted for two games against the Miami Marlins, but they have picked back up against the Cincinnati Reds, taking the first two games of a four-game set.
After Tarik Skubal shut down Cincinnati over seven innings on Monday, Yoshinobu Yamamoto continued the trend of marvelous results from the rotation with a seven-inning scoreless gem on Tuesday, working through a pair of lead-off walks while allowing just one hit while striking out seven. Yamamoto has amazed in his two most recent starts— both against the Reds— allowing just one run over 14 innings while racking up 17 strikeouts compared to just three walks.
Yamamoto held the Reds to just a 1-21 clip after walking his first two hitters of the game on Tuesday, and the right-hander managed to take a page out of Skubal’s playbook for his dominating efforts, notes Sonja Chen of MLB.com.
Yamamoto was able to learn from how the Reds approached Skubal the night before, and Snell was no doubt gathering similar information on Tuesday.
“That kind of encouraged me to be aggressive and attack the hitters,” Yamamoto said through interpreter Yoshihiro Sonoda.
The pitching has managed to hold their end of the bargain against Cincinnati this week, and Blake Snell looks to keep that trajectory in motion. On the offensive side of the ball, Teoscar Hernández has fortified the offense at Great American Ball Park, as the right-hander has crushed a pair of two-run home runs that put both games out of reach.
Hernández has once again found his stride that fans saw during spring training this year, and the Dodger outfielder’s recent success is the brainchild of hitting coach Aaron Bates, allowing Hernández to have a “twister tap” in his stride to the ball, per Maddie Lee of the Los Angeles Times.
“It was a great meeting we had,” Bates said. “We all talked about it, and then he felt comfortable enough to do it, and then the rest is to his credit. He’s just been who he is.”
“When Teo’s hips are loose that way, and his front leg looks like an Elvis knee, it’s a good sign for us,” Bates said. “Because that means that he can open and close it without his upper body going with it.”
Update on Shohei Ohtani
It’s an unusual feeling watching the Dodgers without Shohei Ohtani in the everyday lineup. So far, rookie Josue De Paula has filled in at DH to a small degree of success in limited time (.143/.368/.429, 19 PA) while the reigning two-time NL MVP recovers from multiple nagging issues.
Jack Harris of the California Post notes that Ohtani was able to take batting practice on Monday, and the team is optimistic that he can potentially return from the injured list before the end of the regular season.
“Today was positive,” Roberts said, “and hopefully we can just keep building towards that.”

item.title: [spectrumnews1.com] Dodgers beat Reds 4-0
item.dc:creator: Associated Press
item.description: CINCINNATI — Yoshinobu Yamamoto allowed one hit through seven innings as the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the Cincinnati Reds 4-0 on Tuesday night to edge closer to an NL West division title. The Dodgers reduced the magic number to clinch their 13th division title in the past 14 seasons to two. Los Angeles wrapped up a playoff spot on Monday and still is vying for the top seed in the NL. Cincinnati is assured of a non-winning season after its 81st loss. Yamamoto (14-8) made his team-high 27th start
item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI — Yoshinobu Yamamoto allowed one hit through seven innings as the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the Cincinnati Reds 4-0 on Tuesday night to edge closer to an NL West division title.
The Dodgers reduced the magic number to clinch their 13th division title in the past 14 seasons to two. Los Angeles wrapped up a playoff spot on Monday and still is vying for the top seed in the NL.
Cincinnati is assured of a non-winning season after its 81st loss.
Yamamoto (14-8) made his team-high 27th start and allowed only a third-inning double to Elly De La Cruz, after which he retired 10 straight. He walked two and struck out seven. It was the second straight game a Dodgers starter went seven scoreless after Tarik Skubal on Monday.
Dodgers pitching recorded its 12th shutout of the season. The Reds were blanked for the 17th time.
Freddie Freeman returned to the Dodgers lineup after missing three of the past five games with right knee soreness and had three singles in five at-bats. Freeman was 3 for 30 coming into Tuesday.
Josue De Paula batted leadoff for the first time in just his fifth career game for the Dodgers and went 0 for 5 with a strikeout. He's 2 for 14 since his callup.
Teoscar Hernandez's 15th homer of the season off right-hander Rhett Lowder followed a walk to Kyle Tucker and made the score 3-0 in the third. Lowder (6-11) allowed three earned runs on five hits in five innings.
Alex Freeland made the score 4-0 in the seventh with a solo homer off Pierce Johnson.
De La Cruz extended his on-base streak to 22 games dating to Aug. 22, going 2 for 3 with a double, walk, and stolen base.
Cincinnati had runners on first and third in the ninth against Tanner Scott who struck out the next three batters to seal the Dodgers' ninth straight win over the Reds.
Dodgers LHP Blake Snell (4-1, 1.91) will oppose Reds LHP Andrew Abbott (6-11, 4.84) on Wednesday.

Preguntas y respuestas
CINCINNATI.- Yoshinobu Yamamoto permitió un hit en siete entradas y los Dodgers de Los Ángeles vencieron el martes 4-0 a los Rojos de Cincinnati para acercarse al título de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional.
Los Dodgers redujeron a dos el número mágico para asegurar su 13er título divisional en las últimas 14 temporadas. Los Ángeles aseguró un puesto en los playoffs el lunes y todavía compite por el primer puesto de preclasificación en la Liga Nacional.
Cincinnati, por su parte, tiene garantizada una temporada sin récord ganador tras su 81ra derrota.
Yamamoto (14-8) realizó la 27ma apertura de su equipo, la mayor cantidad, y permitió únicamente un doble en la tercera entrada al dominicano Elly De La Cruz, tras lo cual retiró a 10 bateadores consecutivos. Dio dos bases por bolas y ponchó a siete. Fue el segundo juego seguido en el que un abridor de los Dodgers lanzó siete entradas sin permitir carreras, después de Tarik Skubal el lunes.

Freddie Freeman regresó a la alineación de los Dodgers después de perderse tres de los últimos cinco juegos por molestias en la rodilla derecha y conectó tres sencillos en cinco turnos. Freeman llegaba al martes con 3 hits en 30 turnos.

How Teoscar Hernández fixed his swing to help power Dodgers over the Reds
- Click here to listen to this article
-
CINCINNATI — A simple change opened a dramatic offensive turnaround for Dodgers left fielder Teoscar Hernández.
Hernández’s two-run homer Tuesday, in the Dodgers’ 4-0 win against the Reds, was his second home run in as many nights, as the team trimmed its magic number to clinch the division to one behind Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s seven innings of one-hit ball. And, significantly, this one was against a right-handed pitcher.
“It’s been very helpful,” manager Dave Roberts said after the game. “As certain guys are not seeing the ball as well, it’s nice to kind of backfill with guys like Teo swinging the bat. And when you can slug like he can, you can win baseball games, and he can carry us for a while. And the last 10 days, something like that, it’s been really good from him.”
Through the end of August, Hernández had just a .668 OPS against right-handed pitchers this season. So, when Roberts was asked in Detroit whether the Dodgers would consider setting up a left-field platoon with the team’s September call-ups, he said yes.
Hernández homered off Tigers left-hander Framber Valdez on the last day of the series. And before the Dodgers opened a three-game set against the Cardinals at Dodger Stadium, Hernández met with the hitting coaches.
Against Valdez, Hernández was in a closed stance, to delay his front hip from opening, according to Dodgers hitting coach Aaron Bates. But the team’s hitting group thought a return to a familiar setup could be a long-term solution.
“It was a great meeting we had,” Bates said. “We all talked about it, and then he felt comfortable enough to do it, and then the rest is to his credit. He’s just been who he is.”
Edwin Díaz struggled in his rehab start Sunday, and Dave Roberts is making it clear the Dodgers “got to see something” before putting him on the playoff roster.
In the past, Hernández had used a “twister tap” as his stride. He started in a more open stance, tapped his toe in line with the pitcher, and then set his foot down. But lower-body injuries the last couple of years — a left groin strain last season and a left hamstring strain earlier this season — forced him away from it.
His improved health and hip flexibility opened the avenue for him to return to that timing mechanism.
“When Teo’s hips are loose that way, and his front leg looks like an Elvis knee, it’s a good sign for us,” Bates said. “Because that means that he can open and close it without his upper body going with it.”
The advantage of the twister tap, as Hernández explained it, is how repeatable it is. A more traditional stride can be sped up or slowed down.
“Just being able to control my body and being in a good position,” Hernández said earlier this month. “I can see the pitch a little sooner and identify what kind of pitch it is and if it’s going to be a strike or a ball.”
With that change, he’s rewarded the Dodgers for deciding against platooning left field. Hernández entered Tuesday with a .777 OPS against right-handed pitchers — a sample size of just 28 plate appearances but still a significant jump.
“The biggest thing is his plate coverage away,” Bates said. “Because now he can spoil pitches, and he’s staying in at-bats longer.”
Hernández’s dramatic offensive turnaround, along with fellow corner outfielder Kyle Tucker’s improvement, have helped steady a Dodgers offense that’s missing Shohei Ohtani (on the IL with right biceps and left knee injuries) and includes a hobbled Freddie Freeman (right knee soreness).
Rookie Josue De Paula, mostly filling in for Ohtani at designated hitter, has already shown he can take mature at-bats and provide some pop. But he’s still finding his footing in a new league.
It lengthens the Dodgers lineup for Hernández, after a slow start to his year, to return to being a veteran power threat — just in time to, ideally, carry the momentum into the postseason.
On Monday, he launched his two-run shot off left-hander Nick Lodolo. On Tuesday, he replicated the feat off right-hander Rhett Lowder.
On the second pitch of the at-bat, Hernández recognized a hung slider, and he roped it over the left-field fence at 109.3 mph, according to Statcast. The blast put the Dodgers up 3-0 in the third inning, with Dodgers starter Yamamoto settling into a groove on the other side.
Yamamoto had walked the first two batters he faced, but he reined in his control to pitch seven scoreless innings and allow just one more baserunner — a double by Reds star shortstop Elly De La Cruz.
The Dodgers also scored on Hunter Feduccia’s second-inning single and Alex Freeland’s seventh-inning homer. And the Dodgers bullpen completed the shutout.
Freeman staying in the lineup
Freeman was all smiles after his three-hit game Tuesday — after going hitless for his last four games.
“I was supposed to be off tomorrow, but I played myself in there,” he said. “So I’m very excited.”
Roberts explained: “He was joking, saying, ‘If I get three hits, then can I be in there tomorrow?’”
Sure enough, the mechanical adjustments he made in the batting cage — focusing on getting his foot down early and making contact out in front — got him there.
“I’m just trying to find something that gives me results,” Freeman said. “We’re at the time where we’re just trying to get hot for five weeks here. So kind of like I did in the World Series a couple years ago, I did the step-out move. That’s not sustainable over six months. I’m not trying to find something that’s sustainable.”
Though Roberts has been trying to find opportunities to rest Freeman, he saw promising signs Tuesday beyond the results.
“Just my eyes, just watching him move, I feel good about him going tomorrow,” Roberts said.
De Paula, Freeland and third baseman Max Muncy will be out of the lineup Wednesday, Roberts said.

item.content:encoded:
How did Josue De Paula do for Dodgers vs. Reds on Sept. 15?
Josue De Paula made his first start as the Los Angeles Dodgers' leadoff hitter on Tuesday, Sept. 15.
He went 0-for-5 at the plate in the Dodgers' 4-0 win over the Cincinnati Reds.
The 21-year-old designated hitter jumped up into the leadoff spot in place of Tommy Edman, who was originally in the role after Shohei Ohtani's injury woes.
De Paula added to the Dodgers' offense in a game against the Miami Marlins, hitting a three-run home run for his first career homer on Sept. 13.
The 21-year-old De Paula made his major-league debut for the team at LoanDepot Park on Friday, Sept. 11, becoming the youngest Dodgers player since Alex Verdugo on Sept. 2, 2017.
De Paula has been viewed as the organization's top prospect and recently became the first Dodgers position player called up from AA, while skipping AAA, since Steve Sax in 1981.

item.title: [New York Post] Yoshinobu Yamamoto rounds into playoff form as Dodgers move to cusp of NL West title
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris

item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI –– There’s not much the Dodgers can do, manager Dave Roberts said Tuesday afternoon, to get their all-important rotation ready for the added workload that will come in the postseason.
Over the final couple weeks of the regular season, they have to just keep running their starters out there, and counting on them to round into elevated October form.
That’s what appeared to happen with Yoshinobu Yamamoto on Tuesday night at Great American Ball Park, in what was the right-hander’s most dominant performance of at least the last couple months.
In the Dodgers’ 4-0 win over the Cincinnati Reds, Yamamoto threw a one-hit masterpiece over seven scoreless innings, flashing the kind of ruthless efficiency that defined his heroics during last year’s playoffs.
After walking his first two batters in the first inning, he retired 21 of the 22 after with seven strikeouts and virtually no stress.
“After the first two hitters, it was vintage Yama,” Roberts said. “Just attacking, not trying to be too fine.”
The reigning World Series MVP hadn’t exactly been struggling lately, of course. Just last week, he held the Reds to one run over seven innings with 10 strikeouts back in Los Angeles.
But what Yamamoto did on Tuesday was different, keyed by quick and easy outs on soft and harmless contact.
It’s what he did as the ace of last year’s postseason staff, and what he will need to do again as the Dodgers go for a World Series three-peat this fall.
“I’d like to carry this,” Yamamoto said through an interpreter of his renewed stuff, “into October.”
The Dodgers are hoping they won’t have to ask as much out of Yamamoto this time around; that they need him to pitch back-to-back complete games (like he did in Game 2 of the NLCS and Game 2 of the World Series) or provide back-to-back nights of season-saving heroics (following up a victorious Game 6 start in the Fall Classic with a winning three-inning appearance out of the bullpen in Game 7).
But in a postseason environment, it’s impossible to know what exactly will be required.
“You can’t just try to create that during the regular season because you want these guys as strong and healthy for the October run [as possible],” Roberts said pregame. “But it’s one of those things that, once we get to the postseason, all bets are off and everyone is going to do what they can to contribute.”
It would help, of course, if the Dodgers’ currently Shohei Ohtani-less offense can keep turning a corner, with Tuesday bringing more positive –– albeit subtle –– signs.
The biggest development: Freddie Freeman returned to the lineup amid his ongoing right knee injury, and finally snapped out of a 3-for-30 slump by collecting three singles in the first, fifth and seventh innings.
“Feels better today than he did yesterday,” Roberts said, after Freeman missed his third game in the last week on Monday, “which is a good thing.”
The Dodgers’ scoring, meanwhile, came from elsewhere.

Hunter Feduccia laced an RBI single in the second off Reds starter Rhett Lowder, maintaining his unexpected status as the Dodgers’ best hitter against right-handed pitching since being re-acquired at the trade deadline (with a team-leading .292 average in such splits since the start of August).
Teoscar Hernández continued his late-season surge with a two-run homer in the third, giving him four home runs, eight extra-base hits, 18 RBIs and a .417 average over his last 14 games.
Even Alex Freeland chipped in with a solo blast in the seventh and a double in the ninth, helping him outshine fellow rookie Josue De Paula (who went 0-for-5 with his first two strikeouts of the season after getting bumped up to the leadoff spot).
That was all enough to help the team lower its magic number to clinch the National League West to one.
Still, when it comes to October, no position group will be more important than the Dodgers’ rotation.
That’s why, right now, outings like the one Yamamoto made on Tuesday, or Tarik Skubal spun the night before (also seven scoreless innings) are the most promising ways the Dodgers can ramp up toward the playoffs.
Once they get there, they’ll need their starters to be on.

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers news: Shohei Ohtani, Andy Pages get big injury updates before playoffs appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
With a spot in the MLB playoff locked up, the Los Angeles Dodgers have one major goal for the rest of September: get healthy.
Sure, there are sub-storylines to follow, from Josue De Paula filling in at DH, which bullpen arms are getting hot at the right time, and Kyle Tucker figuring it out down the stretch, but for the most part, the Dodgers simply want to take the field in October with their best guys all available for Dave Roberts to call upon.
Fortunately, on Tuesday, Roberts provided fans with some positive updates on that very front, noting that Shohei Ohtani and Andy Pages are trending in the right direction, as reported by The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
"Some more from Dave Roberts: Shohei Ohtani hit in the cage today. Hope is still for him to return before the end of the regular season," Ardaya wrote. "Andy Pages hit off the machine today. Plan is for him to do Trajekt next. Bullpen game on Thursday."
After breaking his hand in mid-August in a game against the Pittsburgh Pirates, Pages has missed almost a month as he works back from surgery. And as for Ohtani? Well, after missing four games earlier in the month, he returned for one but didn't ultimately look right, landing on the IL to allow him to recover from a series of injuries that have hampered his production down the stretch.
Without Pages and Ohtani, the Dodgers still found a way to manufacture offense, ripping off their longest win streak of the season, but folding that duo back into the fray, especially with De Paula proving he deserves a spot on the bench as a power-hitting pinch hitter, makes LA all the more dangerous down the stretch.
Related: Bobby Miller gets brutally honest on returning to Dodgers
Related: Why Dodgers' Dave Roberts is leading off Josue De Paula vs. Reds
