item.content:encoded:
Dodgers news: Roki Sasaki plan ahead of postseason remains uncertain appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Los Angeles Dodgers are preparing for the MLB postseason. Roki Sasaki has been recovering from a blister on his right middle finger. While he has been trending in the right direction, will Sasaki be ready for the postseason? Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic provided the latest update on Sasaki.
"Roki Sasaki will throw a simulated game tomorrow and will not start this week, Dave Roberts said. The Dodgers are still figuring out if he will start a game before the end of the regular season or if he will come back as a reliever," Ardaya reported.
It previously seemed as if Sasaki was close to returning. In all reality, Sasaki may still return fairly soon — it just won't be this week.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Dodgers fans will remember that Sasaki spent last postseason in the bullpen. While his first two regular seasons in MLB as a starter have been underwhelming, the right-handed pitcher performed well out of the bullpen last October. He recorded a stellar 0.84 ERA across nine outings to go along with three saves.
The Dodgers certainly wouldn't mind a similar postseason performance from Sasaki in 2026. One has to imagine that having him work out of the bullpen in the playoffs makes the most sense for LA, but it seems as if the ball club is still at least open to the idea of him starting again this year.
Updates on Roki Sasaki will continue to be monitored and provided as they are made available. Meanwhile, the Dodgers will play the Reds in Cincinnati on Tuesday night at 6:40 PM ET.
Related: Bobby Miller gets brutally honest on returning to Dodgers
Related: Why Dodgers' Dave Roberts is leading off Josue De Paula vs. Reds

item.content:encoded:
Elly De La Cruz is truly ascending into Tungsten Arm O'Doyle territory of late.
Monday night saw him completely destroy a baseball, one that was conservatively estimated at 457 feet as it buzzed past the power stacks in left-center field in Great American Ball Park en route to exiting the stadium altogether. It was reminiscent of the superblast he hit from the other side of the plate off Los Angeles Dodgers ace Tarik Skubal just a week ago, feats of strength irreplicable by just about any other sole on the planet.
The Cincinnati Reds lost last night, though. Elly's homer was their lone run in a 4-1 loss to those very same Dodgers, a loss that officially eliminated the Reds from any miracle chance at a spot in the postseason. It also sunk them to 10 full games under .500 at 70-80, and this season is rapidly deteriorating into yet another one to forget and chuck onto the scrap-heap of memories of this once proud franchise.
I digress.
Rhett Lowder has a lot to improve upon as he heads into a vital offseason for his overall development. Anything short of a rapid change of form means the Reds need to build in even more redundancy in their starting depth plans for 2027, and there's been precious little in the way of advancement from their former 1st round pick so far in his own disappointing 2026. He'll get the start tonight, while the Dodgers will counter with Yoshinobu Yamamoto.

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers rookie Josue De Paula may be known for his big bat, but it's the times he doesn't swing that are drawing comparisons to a future Hall of Famer.
De Paula has only two hits in his young MLB career — granted, one of them was a huge home run — but he's walked five times, recording at least one in each of his four games, without even a single strikeout.
That kind of plate discipline — and De Paula's funny reaction to pitches outside of the strike zone — have an unexpected superstar showing love to the young Dodger.
Rival player supports Josue De Paula
New York Met Juan Soto, who's battled the Dodgers as a member of the San Diego Padres and New York Yankees, took to Instagram to shout out his fellow Dominican slugger.
Sharing MLB's video of De Paula shaking his head at a pitch below his knees in a moment reminiscent of the "Soto shuffle," Soto gassed up the young slugger.
In Spanish, Soto praised De Paula, whom he called "my crazy friend," for "staying locked in at the plate."
As Dodgers Nation's Noel Sanchez pointed out, the two truly are friends, and their shared history goes beyond just the ability to take a walk or hit a home run.
"These two both attended El Niche Baseball Academy early in their respective careers and they've trained together in the past," Sanchez said. "In a sports world where comparison can be the thief of joy, it's so nice to see Soto co-signing De Paula after his early success."
Of course, Dodgers faithful probably aren't huge fans of Soto.
He and the Padres knocked the Dodgers out of the playoffs in 2022, and he spurned the Boys in Blue to sign with the Mets on a contract even bigger than that of superstar Shohei Ohtani.
That said, Soto's ability to recognize the talents of a younger player — even on another NL team — is worth celebrating, Sanchez said.
"A lot of Dodger fans don't show him love but like I said, everyone should respect this," he said.
What do you think of Juan Soto showing love to Josue De Paula?

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers' Dave Roberts Sent Kyle Tucker Clear Message in One-on-One Meeting
item.dc:creator: J P Hoornstra; Unknown
item.description: Kyle Tucker's home run Monday in Cincinnati was his third in his last five games. In that span he's raised his slugging percentage from a season-low .350 on Sept. 8 to .376 entering Tuesday's rematch against the Reds. September is halfway through, and it's shaping into Tucker's best month of the season. If it seems like he's stopped pressing at the plate, perhaps Tucker let up on himself after getting some needed reassurance in a one-on-one meeting with Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts.
item.content:encoded:
Kyle Tucker's home run Monday in Cincinnati was his third in his last five games. In that span he's raised his slugging percentage from a season-low .350 on Sept. 8 to .376 entering Tuesday's rematch against the Reds.
September is halfway through, and it's shaping into Tucker's best month of the season. If it seems like he's stopped pressing at the plate, perhaps Tucker let up on himself after getting some needed reassurance in a one-on-one meeting with Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts.
“I told him, I’m gonna ride or die with him,” Roberts said (via Jack Harris of the California Post). “That was my young term phrase.”
It's been a rough ride for Tucker in his first season in Los Angeles. The Dodgers signed the four-time All-Star to a four-year, $240 million contract over the winter. Despite being baseball's highest-paid player this season, Tucker hit only one home run in his first 17 games of the season.
Things didn't get much better from there. Among 138 qualified hitters through the end of August, Tucker's .683 OPS ranked 116th.
"I was prepared, the organization was prepared, to give him as much leash as we possibly could to work through some things, and I do think that now we’re starting to see the fruits,” Roberts said. “So I see no other reason why we would pivot from running him out there every day.”
Fans might beg to differ.
At Triple-A Oklahoma City, outfielder James Tibbs III has 29 home runs and 101 RBIs to go with a .417 on-base percentage. Prospect Josue De Paula, who's played right field in the minors, was promoted to take Shohei Ohtani's place on the active roster.
Since his debut, the 21-year-old has reached base in half of his first 14 plate appearances. Sunday, he hit his first career home run. Perhaps Roberts needed to reassure Tucker that De Paula wasn't coming for his job to unlock his production, a curious case of reverse psychology.
It will be hard for the Dodgers to take De Paula out of the lineup if he maintains his current level of production. Roberts said prior to Ohtani's IL stint that the team wasn't considering using him in the outfield.
Tucker, for his part, can reduce the Dodgers' temptation to use Ohtani or De Paula in right field if he continues to hit like a $60 million All-Star.
Sign up for our free newsletter and follow us on X/Twitter and Facebook for the latest news.
J.P. Hoornstra is an On SI Contributor. A veteran of 20 years of sports coverage for daily newspapers in California, J.P. covered MLB, the Los Angeles Dodgers, and the Los Angeles Angels (occasionally of Anaheim) from 2012-23 for the Southern California News Group. His first book, The 50 Greatest Dodgers Games of All-Time, published in 2015. In 2016, he won an Associated Press Sports Editors award for breaking news coverage. He once recorded a keyboard solo on the same album as two of the original Doors.

And yet, that wasn’t the biggest surprise in the team’s new-look batting order. Instead, rookie designated hitter Josue De Paula got an auspicious bump up for the club, getting the chance to serve as leadoff hitter for Tuesday’s matchup against Reds right-hander Rhett Lowder. item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI –– Despite Freddie Freeman’s ongoing right knee injury, the veteran first baseman was back in the Dodgers’ lineup on Tuesday.
And yet, that wasn’t the biggest surprise in the team’s new-look batting order.
Instead, rookie designated hitter Josue De Paula got an auspicious bump up for the club, getting the chance to serve as leadoff hitter for Tuesday’s matchup against Reds right-hander Rhett Lowder.
Tuesday only marked De Paula’s fifth game in the majors, following his call-up directly from double-A Tulsa last week.
He is still serving as DH on only a temporary basis, with Shohei Ohtani on the injured list nursing left knee and right arm injuries.
However, the 21-year-old top prospect has already made a positive impression, drawing five walks in his first 14 plate appearances while collecting his first two MLB hits on Sunday in Miami with a home run and a double. He is suddenly vying for a potential role in the postseason plans, as well.
Thus, the Dodgers are giving the promising left-handed hitter another new opportunity now, seeing how he looks as the leadoff man in their batting order –– one that was also vacated once Ohtani went on the IL.
“I like the at-bats. I like the at-bat quality,” manager Dave Roberts said. “I understand it’s a small sample, but that’s kind of who he is as a hitter. For me, it’ll be a good opportunity for him to get five at-bats tonight.”
For Freeman, meanwhile, Tuesday marks an important opportunity in its own right, as he tries to show progress with his right knee injury.
Freeman has been out for three of the Dodgers’ last five games because of the ailment, and only DH’d in the game before that.
Since the start of September, he has gone only 3-for-30 at the plate.
Roberts continues to insist an injured list stint won’t be needed for the newly-turned 37-year-old. Both he and Freeman voiced hopes of the injury being resolved (or, at least, not as much of an impediment) by the time the playoffs begin.
“I don’t see him getting to his front side as much as he normally does, which causes him to get a little bit underneath,” Roberts said. “So I know that the hitting guys are on it. He’s working through it, so we’ll see how he comes in today.”
Until he starts to hit again, however, concerns over his health will linger.
On Tuesday, he is batting directly after De Paula in the No. 2 hole.

item.title: [MLB.com] Dodgers' top prospect has his own version of the Soto shuffle
item.dc:creator: Max Ralph
item.description: Josue De Paula earned comparisons throughout his Minor League career to some of MLB’s best players, whether for his overall offensive profile to Yordan Alvarez or his plate approach to Juan Soto. That’s why he’s been ranked as one of the sport’s best hitting prospects, making his big league debut last week as MLB Pipeline’s No. 6 prospect overall. During Monday’s 4-1 Dodgers win over the Reds, De Paula put that Soto-like plate approach on full display. He drew a fifth-inning walk against Cincinn
item.content:encoded:
Josue De Paula earned comparisons throughout his Minor League career to some of MLB’s best players, whether for his overall offensive profile to Yordan Alvarez or his plate approach to Juan Soto. That’s why he’s been ranked as one of the sport’s best hitting prospects, making his big league debut last week as MLB Pipeline’s No. 6 prospect overall.
During Monday’s 4-1 Dodgers win over the Reds, De Paula put that Soto-like plate approach on full display. He drew a fifth-inning walk against Cincinnati starter Nick Lodolo after battling back from a 1-2 count.
The fifth pitch of the plate appearance fell just below the zone for ball three, prompting a challenge from Reds catcher Tyler Stephenson, who has been a top-10 challenging catcher this season based on Statcast’s Overturns vs. Expected metric. But Stephenson was wrong this time. Lodolo’s offering missed by 0.9 inches, according to the ABS Challenge System powered by T-Mobile.
De Paula seemed to know all along.
The 21-year-old rookie squatted in his stance, shaking his head in a display of confidence that was reminiscent of the famous “Soto Shuffle.” De Paula then watched a sinker finish well outside to earn the walk -- already his fifth in just four Major League games.
Even if you have to squint a bit to see the Soto Shuffle in De Paula’s reaction Monday night, it doesn’t take much effort to see why there are such widespread comparisons between De Paula and the Mets superstar.
Soto remains one of MLB’s best eyes at the plate at age 27, with a 98th-percentile walk rate (16.5%) and a 95th-percentile chase rate (20.7%) this season. As a 19-year-old rookie in 2018, Soto posted similarly elite numbers in walk rate (16%) and chase rate (18.4%).
De Paula, in his extremely limited Major League sample, has walked 35.7% of the time and chased just 13.5% of the time. Those numbers will balance out over time, but it’s still quite a start for the youngster.
De Paula’s connection with Soto goes back even further. A native of Brooklyn before he moved to the Dominican Republic in high school, De Paula trained at El Niche Baseball Academy, the same facility that worked with the likes of Soto, Elly De La Cruz and Otto Lopez. De Paula has also trained alongside Soto in the past.
In a playful moment between mentor and mentee, Soto shared De Paula’s charismatic take from Monday on his Instagram story, referring to De Paula as "el loco mio" ("my crazy guy" in Spanish).

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers Manager Has Concerning Admission About Freddie Freeman's Injury
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Sandoval; Unknown

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers star first baseman Freddie Freeman does not look like himself right now.
Freeman, who is hitting .293 this season with 16 home runs and an OPS of .818, is dealing with right knee tendinitis.
Since the start of August, the 10-time All-Star is hitting .252 with just one home run and an OPS of .651
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts touched on the injury this past weekend and said that while Freeman is feeling fine enough to play, he's far from the player the team is accustomed to seeing.
“Just talking to him today, he said he felt good,” Roberts said on Sunday, before adding: “Obviously, the swings don’t indicate that, don’t kind of validate that … The last week, it’s pretty obvious that he’s not himself in the box.”
Freeman's knee issue compromises his front side during swings, which has caused extra swing-and-miss at the plate and limited his mobility on defense.
On Monday for the team's series opener against the Cincinnati Reds, Freeman was out of the lineup for the fourth time in the last week.
Roberts said Freeman's injury is one they'll have to manage for the rest of the season.
“I think it’s one of those things where we’ve got to manage it … just pick spots to give him an off day here or there,” Roberts said. “Again, we’ve just got to make sure he’s at optimal health when we finish the season. So I think that he might not love it, but giving him a day off here or there might be beneficial.”
Freeman is expected to avoid an IL stint and remains day-to-day. It remains to be seen if he's back on Tuesday.
"I just think right now, with where we’re at in the season, an IL is not an option in the sense of — I personally don’t think we have a better option," Roberts said. "I don’t think it needs to be 10 days. But could it be more than one? That’s a fair question."
Shohei Ohtani Working His Way Back From Injury
Freeman's injury is just another in a long list of injuries that the Dodgers are dealing with as the regular season winds down.
Freeman is not the only All-SAtar missing time, as Shohei Ohtani is far from healthy as the season winds down.
Ohtani is currently on the 15-day IL with knee, biceps and neck injuries. Roberts said that Ohtani will hit off a tee on Tuesday as he begins his ramp-up.
The 32-year-old is looking to quickly get back as he is eligible to return to the lineup on Sept. 23, just five days before the end of the regular season.
In the meantime, the Dodgers' top prospect, Josue De Paula, has replaced Ohtani as the everyday designated hitter.
If the Dodgers want any chance of completing the three-peat, though, Freeman and Ohtani will need to be healthy and producing at their usual levels.
Thus, the Dodgers will look to get them as close to 100% as possible over the next two weeks.

Ricardo Sandoval is a freelance writer with On SI. He is a graduate of California State University, Northridge, and specializes in sports writing, particularly in MLB, NBA and NFL. He previously served as an Associate Editor for Dodgers Nation and has worked with Newsweek and The Sporting News.

item.title: [Diario AS] ¿Cuáles son las lesiones de Shohei Ohtani?
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Serrano
item.description: Shohei Ohtani se ha perdido seis de los últimos siete partidos de Los Angeles Dodgers debido a las lesiones que ha venido arrastrando esta temporada. item.content:encoded:
Shohei Ohtani se ha perdido seis de los últimos siete partidos de Los Angeles Dodgers debido a las lesiones que ha venido arrastrando esta temporada. La primera fue en la rodilla, una molestia que lo alejó del montículo desde principios de julio y que, con poco tiempo para recuperarse antes de los playoffs, hace casi un hecho que no vuelva a lanzar en 2026. Una baja sensible para los Dodgers en el tramo más importante de la campaña, en el que buscan conquistar su tercera Serie Mundial consecutiva.
Shohei Ohtani to be placed on the injured list (left knee, right biceps), Dodgers manager Dave Roberts announces. pic.twitter.com/AG3VlX3TVe
— MLB (@MLB) September 10, 2026
La segunda lesión que sufrió esta temporada fue en el bíceps, una molestia que ha ido empeorando con el paso de las semanas. Ohtani comenzó a sufrir molestias en el cuello como consecuencia de este problema, lo que obligó a los Dodgers a colocarlo en la lista de lesionados y provocó que se perdiera los últimos encuentros. La buena noticia es que el japonés ha estado trabajando para regresar en este cierre de temporada regular y volver a ocupar su puesto como bateador designado de cara a los playoffs de la MLB.
Ohtani será fundamental en las aspiraciones de los Dodgers
Previo al inicio de la serie ante los Reds en Cincinnati, el mánager de los Dodgers, Dave Roberts, confirmó que Ohtani tiene programado realizar swings desde un tee antes del partido del martes. La actividad representa un paso adelante en su recuperación y mantiene abierta la posibilidad de que pueda regresar a tiempo para ayudar a Los Angeles en los playoffs.
"I think it's important that he does pitch because he has the ability to do it. He's elite."@spillygoat19 shares his thoughts on whether or not he would discourage Shohei Ohtani from pitching in the future.
MLB Network + @NewBalance pic.twitter.com/KqBg6i0pMd
Por fortuna, los Dodgers se prepararon durante la temporada ante una eventual ausencia prolongada de su superestrella. Por esa razón, adquirieron al pitcher Tarik Skubal antes de la fecha límite de intercambios para fortalecer una rotación de lanzadores que buscará llegar en las mejores condiciones a la postemporada.
Shohei Ohtani could resume swinging Monday or Tuesday as he continues recovering from lingering right biceps and left knee issues.
Ohtani is eligible to return from the IL on September 23, giving him a short window to prepare for the postseason.#Dodgers #BlueDynasty pic.twitter.com/l2vdNja7kE
Además, los Dodgers llamó a uno de los mejores prospectos de las Grandes Ligas, Josue De Paula, para aportar a la ofensiva mientras Ohtani se recupera. El pelotero impresionó en sus primeros partidos ante los Marlins, una actuación que le permite a los Dodgers darle mayor tiempo de recuperación a Ohtani con la esperanza de que esté listo para disputar el Clásico de Otoño.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are one win away from clinching a National League playoff berth.
Monday, September 14, the Dodgers begin a three-game series against the Cincinnati Reds for the second time seven games.
Ahead of tonight’s game, the Dodgers make a couple changes in their lineup, one of them involving utility player Tommy Edman.
Tommy Edman is Back in the Lineup vs. the Reds After a Rest Day on Sunday
Per Los Angeles Dodgers reporter David Vassegh, the team announced their starting lineup against the Cincinnati Reds on Monday.
#Dodgers Lineup vs #Reds LHP, Nick Lodolo: Edman CF, Betts SS, Smith C, Tucker RF, T. Hernandez LF, Rojas 2B, Muncy 3B, E. Hernandez 1B, JDP DH, Tarik Skubal SP,” Vassegh wrote on X.
Edman sat out in Sunday’s loss against the Miami Marlins because Dodgers manager Dave Roberts, did not want him playing all three games on a turf field.
“#Dodgers Dave Roberts originally said Josue De Paula would DH all 3 games in Miami,” Dodgers insider Bill Plunket wrote on X ahead of Sunday’s game. “Thought it thru and decided he didn’t want Teoscar Hernandez or Tommy Edman to play all 3 games on turf here. So De Paula gets the start in LF.”
Edman and the Dodgers have been carefully monitoring the center fielder’s ankle, after spending nearly half the season on the injured list. The 31-year-old underwent an offseason ankle surgery and did not return to the Dodgers lineup until June 17.
While the Dodgers primary center fielder Andy Pages, remains on the injured list, Edman has spent most of starts in center.
Despite slashing .257/.339/.390 in 72 games, Edman’s seven game stretch shows signs of a quite the slump.
He’s batting .091 with five strikeouts, two hits, and two RBIs in his last 22 at-bats. Both of hits coming against the Washington Nationals on September 6.
Hopefully yesterday’s much needed rest day gets Edman back where he needs to be.
Los Angeles Dodgers Magic Number to Win NL West is Four
There only 15 days until the first MLB postseason game, and 13 games left in the season for the Dodgers. They can clinch a postseason berth tonight with a win against the Reds.
“LAD can clinch a postseason berth today with a win at Cincinnati *or* losses by both the Padres (@ COL) AND the Diamondbacks (v. MIA),” Dodgers beat writer Katie Woo wrote on X.
For the National League West, the Dodgers’ magic number is four.
After their series concludes against the Reds, the Dodgers are strictly facing NL West opponents. Two series at-home against the San Francisco Giants and San Diego Padres, and rounding off the season on the road to face San Francisco for the final time in 2026.

item.content:encoded:
El jardinero de 21 años abandonó Nueva York durante la pandemia para intentar firmar como profesional en República Dominicana. Los Dodgers lo contrataron por US$397,500 y cuatro años después se saltó Triple-A para llegar a Grandes Ligas.
El primer hit de Josué De Paula en las Grandes Ligas no fue un sencillo para guardar discretamente en una vitrina. Fue un cuadrangular de tres carreras.
El domingo, en Miami, el joven jardinero de los Dodgers encontró una recta de Eury Pérez y la envió al segundo nivel del jardín derecho del loanDepot park. La pelota recorrió unos 416 pies y salió del bate a 108.2 millas por hora. Más tarde agregó un doble y terminó de 2-2 en la derrota 6-4 de Los Ángeles ante los Marlins.
Era apenas su tercer día como jugador de Grandes Ligas.
La imagen resume una historia que comenzó de manera poco convencional. De Paula nació el 24 de mayo de 2005 en Brooklyn, Nueva York. Creció en Estados Unidos, asistió a Benjamin N. Cardozo High School, en Queens, y pertenece a una familia con antecedentes deportivos: es primo segundo de los exjugadores de la NBA Stephon Marbury y Sebastian Telfair.
Pero su camino hacia el béisbol profesional no pasó inicialmente por el sistema estadounidense de escuelas secundarias, universidades y draft.
Pasó por República Dominicana.
La pandemia cambió el camino
De Paula apenas había disputado su primer partido de béisbol con Cardozo cuando la pandemia de COVID-19 paralizó el deporte escolar en 2020.
Durante ese período, según relató posteriormente el propio jugador, su padre le planteó una alternativa: trasladarse a República Dominicana y tratar de abrirse paso por la ruta que cada año siguen cientos de prospectos latinoamericanos que entrenan para conseguir contratos con organizaciones de Grandes Ligas.
La familia se trasladó al país en 2021. De Paula tenía 15 años.
En Santo Domingo entrenó en El Niche Baseball Academy. El cambio era considerable: había nacido y crecido en Nueva York, pero entraba ahora al competitivo sistema dominicano de desarrollo de prospectos internacionales.
La apuesta tardó apenas unos meses en producir resultados.
US$397,500 y una firma que terminó pareciendo barata
El 15 de enero de 2022, cuando tenía 16 años, De Paula firmó con los Dodgers como agente libre internacional por un bono de US$397,500. Aunque nació en Estados Unidos, fue captado y firmado desde República Dominicana.
No era el nombre principal de aquella clase internacional de Los Ángeles. Los Dodgers anunciaron alrededor de 30 firmas y la atención se concentraba entonces sobre todo en otros prospectos de mayor cotización.
Con el tiempo, esos US$397,500 comenzaron a parecer una inversión muy favorable para la organización.
Su primera prueba profesional ocurrió precisamente en el país donde había buscado la firma.
En 2022 jugó para DSL Dodgers Bautista en la Dominican Summer League. Bateó .349, tuvo porcentaje de embazarse de .448 y slugging de .522 en 53 partidos, con cinco jonrones, 30 carreras impulsadas, 42 anotadas y 16 bases robadas. Fue seleccionado al equipo Todos Estrellas de postemporada de la liga.
El experimento dominicano había funcionado.
El difícil salto a Estados Unidos
En 2023 comenzó el recorrido por el sistema de ligas menores de Estados Unidos con Rancho Cucamonga, sucursal Clase A de los Dodgers.
Allí apareció una de las características que después llamaría la atención de la organización: su capacidad de controlar la zona de strike. En 74 partidos bateó .284, llegó a base a ritmo de .396 y produjo 40 carreras. El poder, sin embargo, todavía no había llegado: solo conectó dos cuadrangulares.
El crecimiento se hizo más evidente en 2024.
Entre Rancho Cucamonga y Great Lakes jugó 107 encuentros y terminó con promedio de .268, OBP de .404, 10 jonrones, 62 remolcadas y 27 bases robadas. Además negoció 84 transferencias, una cifra que reflejaba su disciplina en el plato a una edad en la que muchos prospectos todavía dependen casi exclusivamente de sus condiciones físicas.
Durante una de esas temporadas muertas entrenó en Miami junto a Juan Soto y Elly De La Cruz. La atención comenzó a trasladarse hacia el desarrollo de poder en un cuerpo de 6 pies y 3 pulgadas.
Los Dodgers empezaron a hablar de él en términos poco habituales. Dentro de la organización llegó a ser considerado uno de los bateadores jóvenes más avanzados desarrollados por el club en años recientes.
El jonrón que lo puso delante de todos
La explosión mediática llegó en julio.
De Paula fue seleccionado para el Juego de Futuras Estrellas y encontró a dos corredores en circulación frente al zurdo Noah Schultz, otro de los principales prospectos de MLB.
Conectó un slider y mandó la pelota 416 pies por el jardín derecho-central. El batazo salió a 108.5 millas por hora, dio ventaja 3-2 a la Liga Nacional y terminó convirtiéndolo en el Jugador Más Valioso del partido.
Era el primer prospecto de los Dodgers que recibía ese reconocimiento desde Chin-Lung Hu en 2007. Entre los dominicanos que lo habían ganado anteriormente estaban Alfonso Soriano y José Reyes.
Su temporada terminó con 12 cuadrangulares y 32 robos. Tras 98 encuentros con Great Lakes recibió finalmente el ascenso a Doble-A Tulsa, pero allí tuvo un aterrizaje abrupto: se fue sin hits en 18 turnos durante cuatro partidos.
Fue una pausa, no un techo.
¿Jugó con el Escogido?
De Paula pertenece a los Leones del Escogido.
El equipo lo seleccionó en la tercera ronda del Sorteo de Novatos de Lidom de 2023, cuando todavía era un jugador de Clase A de los Dodgers.
Sin embargo, en las fuentes oficiales y registros revisados no aparece evidencia de que haya disputado hasta ahora un partido oficial de temporada regular con los Leones. Es decir, sus derechos en el béisbol otoño-invernal dominicano pertenecen al Escogido, pero su desarrollo competitivo se ha mantenido dentro del sistema de los Dodgers.
El año que abrió la puerta
En 2026 regresó a Tulsa y convirtió Doble-A en su plataforma de lanzamiento.
En 124 partidos bateó .303, con .401 de porcentaje de embasarse y .547 de slugging. Disparó 27 jonrones, produjo 104 carreras y robó 31 bases. En toda su trayectoria de ligas menores acumuló 460 partidos con línea ofensiva de .286/.404/.453, 56 cuadrangulares y 280 impulsadas.
Ascenso a Grandes Ligas
También mejoró una variable que suele determinar si un bateador joven puede trasladar su producción a las Mayores: redujo su porcentaje de ponches mientras aumentaba considerablemente el poder.
En los entrenamientos de primavera ya había dado señales. Bateó .375 en 14 encuentros y volvió a participar en el Juego de Futuras Estrellas durante el verano.
Todavía faltaba un escalón: Triple-A.
Los Dodgers decidieron saltárselo.
De Doble-A directamente a sustituir a Ohtani
La oportunidad apareció cuando Los Ángeles colocó a Shohei Ohtani en la lista de lesionados.
El 11 de septiembre, los Dodgers seleccionaron el contrato de De Paula desde Tulsa. Para incorporarlo al roster de 40 jugadores trasladaron al lanzador Eric Lauer a la lista de lesionados de 60 días.
El movimiento resultó especialmente significativo: De Paula se convirtió en el primer jugador de posición de los Dodgers en saltar directamente de Doble-A a Grandes Ligas en más de una década.
Ni siquiera él esperaba que ocurriera de esa manera.
Cuando el dirigente de Tulsa, Eric Wedge, lo llamó a su oficina y le informó que tomaría un avión para reunirse con "los muchachos grandes", De Paula contó que inicialmente no entendió hacia dónde lo estaban enviando. Pensaba que Triple-A era el paso siguiente.
El viernes 11 de septiembre apareció como bateador designado y séptimo en la alineación contra Miami. Tenía 21 años y 110 días, convirtiéndose en uno de los Dodgers más jóvenes en debutar durante los últimos años. No consiguió hit en tres turnos, pero recibió una transferencia.
Dos días después ocupó por primera vez los jardines.
Y entonces llegó Eury Pérez.
De Paula conectó su primer hit de Grandes Ligas, un jonrón de tres carreras, y luego agregó un doble. Cuatro años y ocho meses después de firmar por US$397,500 en República Dominicana, el muchacho que salió de Brooklyn durante una pandemia y volvió al Caribe buscando una oportunidad ya estaba produciendo carreras para los Dodgers en septiembre.
La lesión de Ohtani abrió la puerta. Sus cuatro años atravesando la Dominican Summer League, Clase A, Clase A Avanzada y Doble-A explican por qué los Dodgers decidieron que no necesitaba tocar ninguna otra antes de entrar.

item.content:encoded:
MIAMI –– The Dodgers’ bullpen melted down once again on Sunday in Miami.
Only this time, they got an unhelpful hand from some shaky late-game defense.
In a 6-4 loss to the Miami Marlins, the Dodgers allowed all of the scoring in the final two innings of what became a walk-off defeat; watching three high-leverage relievers –– Edgardo Henriquez, Tanner Scott and Brock Stewart –– falter after their infield gave away extra outs behind them.
In Henriquez’s two-run eighth inning, one would-be groundout instead snuck between shortstop Mookie Betts and second baseman Miguel Rojas, leaving Rojas injured after he made a late sliding attempt. Another got stuck in Betts’ hand while he tried to make a charging throw on the run, gifting the Marlins a free scoring opportunity that would lead to a two-run single from Otto Lopez.
The four-run ninth inning, which was capped off by Agustín Ramírez’s walk-off homer against Stewart, was just as frustrating, as Scott’s bid for a four-out save imploded after a pair of infield singles; one on a bunt, and another on a bad underhand flipped from a hobbled Freddie Freeman at first base.
“When you give a team extra outs,” manager Dave Roberts said, “that’s what happens.”
Initially, it appeared as though the Dodgers might still escape.
After Lopez’s single in the eighth, Scott replaced Henriquez to face Griffin Conine and struck him out on three pitches to end the inning and keep a 3-2 lead intact.
In the top of the ninth, the Dodgers added to the advantage on Betts’ RBI double, giving them “enough to win” offensively, as Roberts put it, even though they left the bases loaded later in the frame.
Alas, the bottom of the ninth immediately went sideways on an Xavier Edwards ground ball to lead off the inning.
Freeman, who has been playing through a knee injury and is mired in a 1-for-26 slump, fielded the ball but made a bad underhand flip back to first. Scott had to adjust to it as he went to cover the base, and was too late to recover as Edwards beat the play out.
Jakob Marsee came up next and executed a perfect bunt inside the third-base line.
Then, Javier Sanoja got jammed by a slider but still muscled a two-run double into the left-field corner.
Just like that, the Dodgers’ lead was gone. It was only Scott’s fourth blown save in 26 opportunities this season, but also the sixth time in his last 11 outings he has given up a run.
“Actually, I think the last week has been really good as far as the stuff,” Roberts said when asked of that trend, which has pushed Scott’s ERA to 2.91. “Today I think was just an odd day.”
Four pitches later, the game was over. Stewart came in to face the pinch-hitting Ramírez, but grooved him a fastball that was launched to left for the walk-off blast.
“It was supposed to be up above the zone. That’s where my fastball plays best,” Stewart said. “Just missed my spot, threw it right down the middle.”
Thus, the Dodgers suffered a loss that wasted big days from Emmet Sheehan (who threw six scoreless innings in his start) and Josue De Paula (who mashed a monstrous three-run home run in the fourth inning for his first career hit), while also delaying any possibility of clinching a playoff spot for a second-straight day.
“It’s baseball,” Roberts said. “It sucks. It feels bad. But that’s part of the thing.”
With a sigh, he later added: “But yeah, today was a crappy one.”
